Drafted by Codex (read-only consult), posted at owner request. Follow-up to the 2026-11-04 live Calm Down run.

## Goal

Supplement academic abstracts with recent non-academic primary evidence through the existing allowlisted HTTPS fetch path.

Start with public BLS Employment Situation releases relevant to labor-market fears. Make these sources available to both application-controlled Claude retrieval and the tool-calling agent. Use free public pages only, with zero incremental cost and no paid API, new provider, or dependency.

## Allowed Files

- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down.py`
- `docs/experiments/calm-down.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a small, application-owned catalog of BLS Employment Situation release/index URLs on the already allowlisted BLS host.
   - Discover release links only from this bounded catalog.
   - Limit discovery to one index fetch and at most two release fetches per run; no recursive crawling, general web search, arbitrary model URLs, or paid services.
   - Validate every discovered link through the existing HTTPS safety path before fetching it.
   - Fetch releases newest first using explicit publisher dates; unknown dates must not be represented as recent.

2. Integrate the source channel into both research paths.
   - Claude planning remains query-only; the application selects catalog entries and executes retrieval.
   - Apply a deterministic, documented relevance rule for labor-market queries. Skip unrelated fears rather than forcing BLS citations.
   - Give both model paths instructions distinguishing measured aggregate employment outcomes from evidence about AI causation, occupational displacement, forecasts, and exposure.
   - Preserve balanced academic research; a government release must not automatically satisfy both sides of a fear.

3. Share existing budgets and deadlines.
   - Reserve at most two of Claude’s existing twelve planned read slots for primary releases, reducing academic reads accordingly; keep two reads per academic query as an upper bound.
   - All fetch attempts, including failures and discovery, consume the existing session read/fetch allowance before network activity. No separate unlimited allowance.
   - Preserve the fourteen-read session cap, 60,000-character Claude evidence cap, two-launch limit, one usage budget, model-request pacing, full `Retry-After` handling, and no retry/fallback after tool execution.
   - Record executed fetches in tool-call accounting. Do not launch synthesis after a terminal retrieval failure or deadline expiry.

4. Route discovery and release retrieval through `safe_get` and the existing text extraction machinery.
   - Retain HTTPS-only access, allowlist and public-address checks, validation on every redirect, redirect/byte/time limits, and unsupported-content refusal.
   - Do not widen the host allowlist or forward the OpenAlex key, cookies, private configuration, or private input to BLS.
   - Treat fetched text, page metadata, and discovered links as untrusted. Embedded instructions cannot select tools, alter policy, or cause further fetching.

5. Preserve auditable evidence.
   - Register releases as `backend="fetch"` with stable source IDs, final URL, publisher, verified publication year when available, retrieval time, exact bounded text, and its SHA-256 digest.
   - Distinguish publication date, statistical reference period, and retrieval time in source text or metadata supplied to synthesis.
   - Preserve bundle reload, digest validation, citation verification, and offline finalize compatibility without changing dossier schemas.
   - Do not infer publication date from retrieval time or treat an index page as a substantive statistical release.
   - If no relevant recent release exists, disclose that limitation without inventing data. Transport or safety failures follow the existing terminal failure policy.

6. Name and document the Tools trust boundary: application-owned discovery seeds → untrusted remote links/content → existing URL validation and bounded fetch → recorded source snapshots → synthesis and mechanical verification. This issue authorizes implementation only; it does not authorize live calls, sending, schedules, or deployment.

7. Add offline tests covering:
   - Relevant and irrelevant queries, newest-first selection, deduplication, unknown/stale dates, and publication dates differing from reference periods.
   - Successful release snapshots reaching Claude synthesis and the tool-agent path with valid provenance and digests.
   - HTTP downgrade, credentials, unusual ports, deceptive hostnames, off-allowlist redirects, private-address resolution, and redirect loops.
   - HTTP 429/503, DNS/transport failures, oversized or trickling responses, malformed discovery HTML, unsupported content, and empty extracted text.
   - Malicious embedded instructions and links causing no additional fetch or policy change; OpenAlex credentials never reaching BLS.
   - Discovery/release caps, failed-attempt accounting, exhausted read/evidence budgets, deadline expiry, and no retry, repair, fallback, or third Claude launch.
   - Bundle round-trip and offline finalize with fetched sources; fixture mode performs no network activity.

## Verification

Offline only. Use inline synthetic BLS HTML, mocked HTTP/DNS/time, mock providers, and the existing fake Claude executable. Do not fetch real releases or consume model quota.

Run:

```bash
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py tests/test_runtime.py tests/test_tools.py tests/test_claude_cli.py
bash scripts/check-scope.sh --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py --allowed tests/test_calm_down.py --allowed docs/experiments/calm-down.md
```

Report exactly which checks ran. Synthetic fixtures validate integration and failure handling; they do not establish live BLS markup compatibility or substantive support for a claim.

## Risks/Open Questions

- BLS aggregate statistics cannot establish that AI caused observed employment changes.
- Release revisions and differing reference periods can make apparently conflicting figures valid; synthesis must preserve their context.
- HTML layout changes and text truncation may omit relevant tables or caveats.
- Reserving primary-source reads reduces academic breadth within the same budget.
- Start with BLS only. Additional agencies, professional sources, or news require a separately approved scope.

## Goal
The runtime guarantee says every run, including crashes, is recorded with `error_class`, `git_sha` and `config_hash` (README, "Failure handling"). Experiment 2 (#4, PR #5) showed one case where that fails. When a Job hits `activeDeadlineSeconds`, Kubernetes sends SIGTERM and then deletes the pod. The agent prints no RunRecord, nothing is appended to `runs.jsonl`, and the pod log is gone, so n8n reports `log unavailable`. Evidence: Job `agent-lab-n8n-js455`, `DeadlineExceeded`, `agent: null`.

Two layers to fix:
1. **Ordering:** the agent's own `AGENT_LAB_DEADLINE_SECONDS` should fire before the Job deadline and record `error_class=limit`. Today the defaults allow the reverse: the n8n Job uses 120 s for both, and `k8s/cronjob.yaml` uses 300 s against a 120 s agent default.
2. **Termination:** on SIGTERM, the runtime should finish the in-flight RunRecord as failed (`error_class=limit`, or a new class if the contract owner prefers), write it to the run log and stdout, and exit within `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.

This changes a runtime guarantee, so it is substantive and needs failure-path tests.

## Allowed Files
- `src/agent_lab/runtime.py`, `src/agent_lab/cli.py` (signal handling, record on termination)
- `tests/test_runtime.py` (or a new `tests/test_termination.py`)
- `n8n/agent-lab-run-k8s-job.json` (set `AGENT_LAB_DEADLINE_SECONDS` below the Job deadline)
- `k8s/cronjob.yaml` (deadline ordering, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` if needed)
- `README.md`, `docs/learning/n8n-kubernetes.md` (statements this makes untrue)
- `src/agent_lab/contracts/` and `contracts/` only if a new `error_class` value is chosen (owner decision first)

## Acceptance Criteria
- SIGTERM during a run yields exactly one failed RunRecord with `error_class`, `git_sha`, `config_hash` and the attempts so far, both on stdout and in `runs.jsonl`, and a non-zero exit.
- No retry or fallback starts after SIGTERM, and a tool that already executed is not re-run (existing guarantees hold).
- Every shipped manifest and workflow has `AGENT_LAB_DEADLINE_SECONDS` < `activeDeadlineSeconds`.
- On k3d, a Job killed by its deadline leaves a RunRecord on the PVC, and n8n reports it where the pod log survives long enough.

## Verification
- `pytest tests/test_runtime.py` (or the new test file) covering SIGTERM before, during and after a tool call, offline with the mock provider.
- If contracts change: `python scripts/export_contract_schemas.py && git diff --exit-code contracts/`.
- Local k3d run of the timeout scenario showing the record on the PVC.
- `check-scope.sh` with the Allowed Files above. CI `ci.yml` and `k3d-smoke.yml` on the PR head.

## Goal
Add recent BLS Employment Situation releases as a bounded primary-source channel for labor-market fears, on both research paths, using the existing allowlisted `safe_get` fetch path.

## Allowed Files
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py`

## Acceptance Criteria
- `retrieval.py`: `BLS_CATALOG` holds one application-owned index URL. Release links must match the publisher's dated archive pattern `empsit_MMDDYYYY.htm`. Undated, invalid, future, stale and duplicate links are dropped, and the rest are sorted newest first. Each run makes at most one index fetch and two release fetches. Every attempt is counted against the 14-read session cap before any request. Redirects are pinned to `www.bls.gov` through a new `pin_host` option on `safe_get`. Each release is recorded as a `backend="fetch"` source with optional `published` and `reference_period` fields. Its snapshot header lists publication date, reference period and retrieval time separately. When no recent release exists, that is recorded as a disclosed limitation. Adds the `bls_employment_releases` tool for the tool-calling agent.
- `pipeline.py`: a deterministic relevance rule (`labor_market_query`) is applied to the fear and the planned queries. For relevant fears, academic reads are reduced to 10 of the 12 planned reads, and characters are reserved for two releases. BLS is read only after both sides have academic coverage and never counts toward either side. Each BLS step is recorded as a tool call. Any failure or deadline expiry ends the run before synthesis.
- `__init__.py`: rule 8 tells both model paths that releases measure aggregate outcomes, not AI causation, displacement, forecasts or exposure. The planning step stays query-only.
- Bundle and dossier schemas are unchanged; old bundles still load because the new fields default to `None`.

- Not run: any live BLS fetch or model call. Ruff is not installed locally.
- A slow, trickling stream is covered only as an `httpx.ReadTimeout`, plus the existing shared-deadline thread test. There is no new real slow-stream test.

Drafted by Codex (read-only consult), posted at owner request. Follow-up to #36 / PR #39.


## Goal

Move Claude subprocess lifecycle protection into `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py`, replacing the runner-specific workaround introduced by #36 / PR #39 where equivalent guarantees can be demonstrated.

Currently, the delivery runner passes its `run.lock` descriptor to the research CLI, but `ClaudeCliContext._launch()` starts Claude in a separate session without forwarding that descriptor. If both the runner and research CLI are externally SIGKILLed, Claude can survive while the lock becomes available.

Ensure that surviving research cannot run outside serialization. Catchable-interrupt cleanup alone cannot address SIGKILL; use explicit lock-descriptor inheritance or another demonstrably equivalent mechanism.

## Allowed Files

- `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py`
- `scripts/calm-down-delivery.py`
- `tests/test_claude_cli.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down_email.py`

Limit documentation changes to relevant docstrings and comments in these files. Additional paths require owner approval before implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Establish an explicit lifecycle contract between the runner, research CLI, and Claude subprocess:
  - While Claude research remains alive, a competing runner cannot acquire `run.lock` or reserve another attempt.
  - This holds when the runner dies, the research CLI dies, or both are externally SIGKILLed after Claude launches.
  - Once all lock holders exit, a subsequent runner can acquire the lock normally.
- If forwarding the lock descriptor:
  - Preserve the same locked open file description through each subprocess boundary.
  - Forward only the designated descriptor; keep unrelated descriptors closed.
  - Validate any descriptor handoff and fail closed on invalid configuration.
  - Preserve direct Claude CLI use when no delivery-runner lock is supplied.
  - Keep the descriptor out of prompts, model arguments, persisted records, and unrelated subprocesses.
- Preserve bounded process-group cleanup for normal completion, deadline expiry, output overflow, and catchable interruptions. Cover exceptions after spawning and before communication setup completes.
- Do not silently report successful cleanup when termination cannot be confirmed. Define bounded, fixed diagnostic failures and retain serialization while surviving research holds the lock.
- Remove the runner’s `ctypes`/`prctl` subreaper setup, `/proc` descendant scan, descendant kill/reap loop, and associated constants and diagnostics **only if** the replacement preserves their relevant guarantees. Replace implementation-specific tests with behavioral regression tests. If equivalent protection requires retaining any part, explain the remaining dependency.
- Add offline failure-path tests using local fake executables and real subprocesses where kernel behavior matters:
  - Normal success, nonzero exit, and spawn failure.
  - Deadline expiry and stdout/stderr overflow.
  - `KeyboardInterrupt` and termination during active research.
  - Independent and combined external SIGKILL of runner and research CLI.
  - Claude descendants holding pipes open or surviving their immediate parent, including a separate-session descendant.
  - Cleanup failure, invalid descriptor handoff, unrelated descriptor isolation, and eventual lock release.
  - A competing runner is refused before reservation while research survives; interrupted or abandoned reserved attempts remain counted.
- Preserve existing runtime guarantees: shared request/usage accounting and monotonic deadline; no retry, fallback, repair, or automatic login; byte caps; temporary-directory cleanup where execution can unwind; launch gates and environment filtering; fixed secret-free diagnostics; and run records with `error_class`, `git_sha`, and `config_hash` for recordable failures.
- Preserve durable attempt accounting and delivery state transitions. Do not claim that SIGKILL permits a final `RunRecord` or synchronous cleanup.
- No new dependency, provider, quota source, schedule, delivery behavior, or live model call.

## Verification

Offline only, with fake Claude executables, temporary state directories, and no credentials or network retrieval.

Run:

```bash
pytest tests/test_claude_cli.py tests/test_calm_down_email.py
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py
bash scripts/check-scope.sh \
  --allowed src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py \
  --allowed scripts/calm-down-delivery.py \
  --allowed tests/test_claude_cli.py \
  --allowed tests/test_calm_down_email.py
```

Use explicit synchronization and bounded waits for process tests. Test teardown must terminate fake survivors even after assertion failures. Report platform skips and exactly which checks ran; mocked subprocess tests alone do not prove lock inheritance or SIGKILL behavior.

These are proposed implementation checks; they were not run while drafting this issue.

## Risks / Open Questions

- `_communicate()` already kills Claude’s process group on failure and completion. The missing guarantee crosses process boundaries; adding another interrupt handler alone does not fix it.
- How should the designated descriptor reach `ClaudeCliContext` without broadening the environment allowlist or leaking it into unrelated children?
- Lock inheritance prevents overlapping runs but does not terminate an orphan. A hung holder can block future runs indefinitely; define the supported recovery procedure without automatically breaking the lock.
- A descendant can change sessions or close inherited descriptors. Define the supported process-tree boundary and demonstrate that removing the subreaper does not reopen the separate-session escape covered by PR #39.
- Process-group signaling does not reap arbitrary grandchildren. Distinguish confirmed termination, direct-child reaping, and lock retention in implementation claims.
- SIGTERM handling differs from `KeyboardInterrupt`; verify actual signal behavior rather than assuming both reach Python cleanup.
- The current group-kill helper suppresses signaling errors and wait timeouts. Decide how cleanup uncertainty becomes a safe diagnostic without masking the original failure.
- Define the supported OS/filesystem boundary for inherited advisory `flock`; Linux verification must not imply portability.

## Goal
Add explicit mechanically checked, human-unreviewed Calm Down rendering and an inactive, manually triggered local n8n workflow that can deliver one edition to the owner under #34's activated allowance.

## Dependencies and boundaries
Depends on merged #34 and #35; standing permission must be explicitly activated before live use. Requires its own owner START. This contract covers repository implementation and offline validation only: importing/configuring n8n, host access, credentials, real research and Gmail sends are separate owner-controlled actions. No existing workflow or infrastructure is changed.

## Allowed Files
- `src/agent_lab/cli.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/verify.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/render.py`
- `scripts/calm-down-delivery.py` — new bounded host runner and persistent delivery/attempt state
- `n8n/agent-lab-calm-down-email.json` — new inactive workflow
- `tests/test_calm_down.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down_email.py` — new offline host/workflow tests
- `docs/experiments/calm-down.md`
- `README.md` — workflow/rendering behavior statements only

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Add an explicit opt-in CLI rendering mode that skips only human support approval after research. Default research/finalize behavior and review hashes remain unchanged. All mechanical citation, evidence, balance, schema, bundle-integrity and output-safety checks still apply; no synthetic human approvals or reviewer identity. Report human review as absent rather than describing the edition as human-approved.
2. Render a prominent **“Unreviewed, AI-generated”** banner in HTML and text for this mode; retain fixture labeling. Mechanical acceptance does not establish factual support. Automated delivery refuses fixture editions, pending/insufficient reports and failed runs.
3. Define the actual host execution transport before coding: use an owner-configured local n8n instance that can invoke the fixed host runner directly; if n8n is containerized/remote without that capability, stop for a separately scoped host bridge. Do not assume an Execute Command node escapes a container. No new network listener, Kubernetes bypass, infrastructure edits or credentials in the export.
4. The manual workflow passes bounded fear text as data, never interpolated shell code. The host runner launches the CLI with an argument array and `shell=False`, fixed executable/subcommand and application-generated output paths; leading hyphens and shell payloads remain literal input. Model output cannot choose commands, paths or recipient.
5. Before any research, atomically reserve a daily attempt in durable private local state using #34's New York day boundary and shared manual/n8n accounting. Refuse a fourth attempt, concurrent over-allocation, corrupt/unavailable state, or revoked allowance; crash consumes the reservation. Document that direct manual CLI runs must follow the same ledger procedure. Preserve at most two Claude launches and disable workflow-level retries of research.
6. Use a fresh, exclusively created execution directory under a private configured root. Bind ready artifacts to execution/run ID, successful research, mechanical report, live retrieval, unreviewed mode and HTML/text digests. Missing/stale/changed artifacts, path traversal, symlink escape, absent banner or failed checks prevent sending. Gmail receives validated `email.html` as HTML, with a fixed subject policy and private recipient configuration.
7. Persist an atomic delivery claim before Gmail is invoked, with states distinguishing ready, send-attempted, sent and unknown. Concurrent workers/re-executions cannot claim the same edition twice; a crash, timeout, ambiguous Gmail failure or lost acknowledgement after the claim prevents automatic resend, including after restart. Disable node/workflow send retries. Do not claim exactly-once delivery: at-most-once attempts can lose an email. No automatic recovery sends.
8. Gmail credentials, recipient, host paths and state stay private; export placeholders only. Export is inactive with a manual trigger only; no schedule/webhook or automatic activation. Validate required local configuration before research. No actual Gmail connection or email is part of implementation verification.

## Verification
- Run `pytest tests/test_calm_down.py tests/test_calm_down_email.py` with fake CLI/retrieval, temporary state and a Gmail stub, offline without credentials.
- Test default human gate, explicit bypass with no fabricated approvals, retained mechanical failures, banner/escaping, fixture-send refusal, hostile/leading-hyphen input, stale/missing/changed artifacts and path/symlink escapes.
- Test fourth daily attempt, shared/concurrent reservations, New York midnight/DST, crash/corrupt state, duplicate claims, restart after send claim, ambiguous Gmail outcome and disabled retries. Assert rejected cases invoke no send; preflight/attempt rejection invokes no research.
- Parse and validate workflow nodes/connections and exercise its data/state transitions with a stub; do not equate JSON parsing with native n8n compatibility. Run scope checker at committed head.
- Report native host/n8n/Gmail compatibility and live evidence as unverified unless separately authorized and actually exercised.

## Goal

Address the owner-reported 2026-11-04 run: only 8 of 29 sources read were published in 2026; the remainder dated from 2002–2025.

For each live search, combine the existing relevance search with a publication-date-filtered search. Make recent evidence available within existing result and reading budgets, and instruct both model paths to acknowledge older evidence without discarding useful foundational research.

This issue covers academic retrieval and instructions. Non-academic sources belong to the companion issue.

- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down.py`
- `docs/experiments/calm-down.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each valid live `search_sources` call performs two sequential OpenAlex searches when the deadline permits:
   - The existing relevance search with `has_abstract:true`.
   - The same query and abstract requirement plus `from_publication_date`, calculated from a configurable recent window.
   - Default the window to 730 days. Validate it as a positive, bounded integer before network activity; document its supported range and configuration mechanism.
   - Resolve the effective window and UTC reference date once per research session. Pass configuration explicitly through the research pipeline and include the effective retrieval policy in the Claude `config_hash`.

2. Merge results deterministically, deduplicating by OpenAlex work ID across passes and searches. Preserve previously read source records and digests. Return at most the existing `MAX_RESULTS_PER_SEARCH = 5`.
   - Alternate recent and relevance candidates, starting with recent, skipping duplicates and filling unused positions from the other list.
   - With distinct results from both passes, the first two candidates include one from each pass, so Claude’s two-read limit does not hide the recent pass.
   - An empty recent result set may use relevance results; it must not imply recent evidence was found.

3. Preserve existing bounds: eight logical searches, fourteen reads, tool-call and token limits, Claude’s six planned queries, two reads per query, 60,000 evidence characters, two launches, and the shared deadline.
   - Reserve the logical search before either request.
   - Explicitly bound added transport work to two initial OpenAlex requests per logical search: at most sixteen per session, excluding only already-bounded redirect hops.
   - No pagination, additional model calls, automatic reruns, or expanded result/read allowances.

4. Update tool-agent, planning, and synthesis instructions to prefer relevant recent evidence for current developments, retain older foundational evidence when appropriate, and disclose when evidence is older or recent evidence is unavailable.
   - Do not equate newer publication with stronger evidence or impose a citation-year quota.
   - Respect existing numeric-writing rules: age disclosures must not introduce unsupported years into claims or caveats.

5. Name the trust boundary: public query text goes to OpenAlex through `safe_get`; returned metadata and abstracts remain untrusted data. Preserve HTTPS checks, credential isolation, keyed redirect restrictions, redaction, source snapshots, and quote verification.

6. Preserve one usage budget per run, model-request pacing, full `Retry-After` handling, and no retry or fallback after tool execution. A failed pass ends the search through the existing error path; it must not silently become an empty result, trigger an anonymous retry, or restart research. The second pass is planned retrieval, never recovery from failure.

7. Add offline failure-path tests covering:
   - Exact filter construction, frozen-date boundaries, invalid window configuration, and both keyed and anonymous requests.
   - Stable merging, duplicate-only results, empty passes, and recent candidates surviving five-result truncation and Claude’s two-read selection.
   - First-pass and second-pass HTTP errors, malformed responses, timeouts, and deadline expiry between passes; no subsequent request or synthesis after terminal failure.
   - Exhausted search/read budgets, preserved read records, key redaction, and keyed redirect refusal.
   - Shared usage accounting, request pacing, `Retry-After`, and no retry/fallback after tool execution using mocked providers and clocks.

Offline only, with mocked HTTP, DNS, clocks, and providers; use the existing fake Claude executable. No credentials or live research.

```bash
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py tests/test_runtime.py tests/test_tools.py tests/test_claude_cli.py
bash scripts/check-scope.sh --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py --allowed tests/test_calm_down.py --allowed docs/experiments/calm-down.md
```

Report exactly which checks ran. Offline tests establish request construction and bounded behavior, not live OpenAlex coverage or citation freshness.

- Two searches increase transport work and deadline pressure while leaving model and reading budgets unchanged.

## Goal

Correct Claude CLI usage accounting observed after #21, run `8f157545`. Its RunRecord reports two requests, `input_tokens=4`, and `output_tokens=3013`.

`ClaudeCliContext._account()` currently reads only top-level `usage.input_tokens` and `usage.output_tokens`. It ignores `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens`; `modelUsage` supplies only the served-model name. Consequently, `usage_complete` can be true despite omitted cache usage.

Include reported cache input tokens in the existing input total, with explicit handling of incomplete usage. Preserve the RunRecord schema.

**Uncertainty:** The supplied dossier, limitation, bundle, and RunRecord do not contain the raw CLI envelopes. Cache omission is confirmed in code, but the historical cache counts and corrected total cannot be recovered from these artifacts. Four may accurately represent the reported uncached component.

- `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py`
- `tests/test_claude_cli.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down.py` — usage-envelope fixtures and accounting assertions only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Define Claude CLI `input_tokens` as the sum of reported uncached input, cache-creation input, and cache-read input. Count each component once per launched call.
2. Use top-level `usage` as the accounting source. Do not additionally sum overlapping `modelUsage` counters or nested cache-creation breakdowns.
3. Validate each component as a nonnegative integer, excluding booleans. Explicit zero is available usage; missing, null, negative, string, boolean, or otherwise malformed values are unavailable.
4. Preserve known components as lower-bound totals when any required component is unavailable. Mark affected calls and the run using the existing `usage_unavailable` and `usage_unavailable_for_some_calls` conventions. Do not infer zero cache usage from absent fields.
5. Accumulate usage across both calls, including parseable error envelopes and responses whose generated JSON or schema validation fails. Preserve unavailable markers when no usable envelope exists.
6. Preserve RunRecord fields and types, output-token enforcement, request counting, shared deadlines, launch gates, and the prohibition on retry or fallback.

- Explicit cache zeros remain complete.
- Missing or malformed components retain known totals and mark usage unavailable.
- When all input components are unavailable but valid output usage is reported, the run retains zero input tokens as a lower bound, preserves output usage, and marks both the affected call and run as usage unavailable.
- Nominal Calm Down fake CLI envelopes explicitly report zero cache components so they continue to represent complete usage; deliberately incomplete envelopes retain unavailable markers.
- Overlapping `modelUsage` and nested cache breakdowns are not double-counted.
- Error envelopes, malformed generated JSON, and schema failures retain reported consumption without retry.
- Missing envelopes retain unavailable markers.

## Goal

Fix the confirmed guarantee-check false positive in run `8f157545`:

> Nobody can promise any profession is safe forever, so stay curious, keep verifying the robot’s homework, and keep learning.

`_check_text()` applies `_GUARANTEE.search()` without checking assertion scope. The regex matches both `is safe` and `safe forever` inside this explicit denial of a promise.

Introduce a narrow exception for an explicitly denied guarantee proposition. Preserve rejection of actual guarantees and all other verification gates.

**Risk:** An overly broad negation exception could admit unsupported reassurance, especially when an unrelated disclaimer precedes a real guarantee. Regex-based scope handling cannot establish arbitrary natural-language meaning; ambiguous constructions should retain existing rejection behavior.

## Allowed Files

Verified existing paths:

- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/verify.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The exact saved verdict no longer receives a guarantee/proof problem solely for its explicit “Nobody can promise … is safe forever” disclaimer.
2. Limit suppression to guarantee matches within a narrowly recognized denied proposition. Do not exempt an entire field, sentence, or paragraph merely because it contains a negation word.
3. Handle overlapping matches within that proposition: suppressing `is safe` alone must not leave `safe forever` incorrectly flagged.
4. Continue rejecting affirmative guarantees, including “This profession is safe forever,” “Lawyers will never be replaced,” and existing guarantee/proof patterns.
5. Continue rejecting mixed statements such as “Nobody can promise any profession is safe forever, but accountants are safe forever,” including sentence-separated variants and unrelated negation such as “Do not worry; this profession is safe forever.”
6. The minimum supported disclaimer form is the exact phrase “Nobody can promise any profession is safe forever” with case-insensitive matching and whitespace variation between words. Recognize only that denied proposition; the trailing advice in the saved verdict remains outside it. Broader disclaimer grammar is not required. Document the deliberately limited recognized grammar; ambiguous constructions retain existing rejection behavior, and do not claim general semantic verification.
7. Preserve claim/quote negation checks, number and URL checks, citation checks, section integrity, source diversity, approval hashes, and human review. Clearing this false positive must not make the original dossier complete: its caveat-number and F8 failures remain.

## Verification

Run offline with fixtures and no credentials:

```bash
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py
```

Required tests:

- Exact saved verdict and supported disclaimer variants avoid the guarantee problem.
- Affirmative, mixed-clause, separate-sentence, unrelated-negation, and overlapping-match cases behave as specified.
- Reject an affirmative guarantee after a semicolon: “Nobody can promise any profession is safe forever; accountants are safe forever.”
- Reject an affirmative guarantee after a conjunction: “Nobody can promise any profession is safe forever and accountants are safe forever.” The supported disclaimer must not suppress the later assertion.
- Exercise the shared editorial checker through verdict, caveat, uncertainty, and limitation fields.
- Removing the false positive alone leaves a representative dossier insufficient when F5/F6-style unsupported years and an F8-style negation mismatch remain.
- A mechanically valid changed verdict still requires fresh human editorial approval.
- Existing guarantee, proof, URL, number, citation, and finalization failure tests remain valid.

Before handoff, check the committed head:

```bash
bash scripts/check-scope.sh --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/verify.py tests/test_calm_down.py
```

Require independent review of the exact implementation head, focusing on false-negative risks and scope boundaries. Report checks actually executed and skipped. No tests were executed while drafting. Any live validation requires a separate, complete **OWNER AUTHORIZATION RECORD**.

## Out Of Scope

Deleting guarantee patterns, blanket negation exemptions, changing claim/quote negation rules, model-based verification, prompt changes, automatic human approval, saved-bundle edits, live runs, and adjacent refactors.

## Goal
Each live `search_sources` call now runs the existing OpenAlex relevance search and then a second search limited to recently published work. - Two sequential requests per search: `has_abstract:true`, then the same query plus `from_publication_date`. The window comes from `AGENT_LAB_CALM_DOWN_RECENT_DAYS`: default 730, an integer from 1 to 3650, validated before any output or network activity. The window and UTC reference date are fixed once per `ResearchSession`, passed explicitly from `run_calm_down`, and included in the Claude `config_hash` through `session.retrieval_policy()`.
- `merge_candidates`: results from the two searches alternate, recent first. Duplicates are dropped by OpenAlex id, the other list fills empty slots, and the total is capped at 5. Records already in the session (read flag, digest) are reused.
- Bounds are unchanged. The logical search is reserved before either request. The new `MAX_OPENALEX_REQUESTS` caps sessions at 16 initial requests (redirect hops are excluded and bounded by `MAX_REDIRECTS`). If the Claude deadline passes after the first request, the second is not sent (`session.expired`).
- Either request failing (HTTP error, timeout, malformed JSON or shape, refused keyed redirect) ends the search through the existing `ModelRetry`/`retrieval_failed` path. There is no retry, no anonymous fallback and no partial result.
- New instruction rule 7 (tool agent + synthesis) and a plan note: prefer relevant recent evidence, keep foundational work, newer is not stronger, no year quota, and disclose evidence age in words without years.

Drafted by Codex (read-only consult), posted at owner request. Follow-up to the 2026-11-04 live Calm Down run.

## Goal

Supplement academic abstracts with recent non-academic primary evidence through the existing allowlisted HTTPS fetch path.

Start with public BLS Employment Situation releases relevant to labor-market fears. Make these sources available to both application-controlled Claude retrieval and the tool-calling agent. Use free public pages only, with zero incremental cost and no paid API, new provider, or dependency.

## Allowed Files

- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down.py`
- `docs/experiments/calm-down.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a small, application-owned catalog of BLS Employment Situation release/index URLs on the already allowlisted BLS host.
   - Discover release links only from this bounded catalog.
   - Limit discovery to one index fetch and at most two release fetches per run; no recursive crawling, general web search, arbitrary model URLs, or paid services.
   - Validate every discovered link through the existing HTTPS safety path before fetching it.
   - Fetch releases newest first using explicit publisher dates; unknown dates must not be represented as recent.

2. Integrate the source channel into both research paths.
   - Claude planning remains query-only; the application selects catalog entries and executes retrieval.
   - Apply a deterministic, documented relevance rule for labor-market queries. Skip unrelated fears rather than forcing BLS citations.
   - Give both model paths instructions distinguishing measured aggregate employment outcomes from evidence about AI causation, occupational displacement, forecasts, and exposure.
   - Preserve balanced academic research; a government release must not automatically satisfy both sides of a fear.

3. Share existing budgets and deadlines.
   - Reserve at most two of Claude’s existing twelve planned read slots for primary releases, reducing academic reads accordingly; keep two reads per academic query as an upper bound.
   - All fetch attempts, including failures and discovery, consume the existing session read/fetch allowance before network activity. No separate unlimited allowance.
   - Preserve the fourteen-read session cap, 60,000-character Claude evidence cap, two-launch limit, one usage budget, model-request pacing, full `Retry-After` handling, and no retry/fallback after tool execution.
   - Record executed fetches in tool-call accounting. Do not launch synthesis after a terminal retrieval failure or deadline expiry.

4. Route discovery and release retrieval through `safe_get` and the existing text extraction machinery.
   - Retain HTTPS-only access, allowlist and public-address checks, validation on every redirect, redirect/byte/time limits, and unsupported-content refusal.
   - Do not widen the host allowlist or forward the OpenAlex key, cookies, private configuration, or private input to BLS.
   - Treat fetched text, page metadata, and discovered links as untrusted. Embedded instructions cannot select tools, alter policy, or cause further fetching.

5. Preserve auditable evidence.
   - Register releases as `backend="fetch"` with stable source IDs, final URL, publisher, verified publication year when available, retrieval time, exact bounded text, and its SHA-256 digest.
   - Distinguish publication date, statistical reference period, and retrieval time in source text or metadata supplied to synthesis.
   - Preserve bundle reload, digest validation, citation verification, and offline finalize compatibility without changing dossier schemas.
   - Do not infer publication date from retrieval time or treat an index page as a substantive statistical release.
   - If no relevant recent release exists, disclose that limitation without inventing data. Transport or safety failures follow the existing terminal failure policy.

6. Name and document the Tools trust boundary: application-owned discovery seeds → untrusted remote links/content → existing URL validation and bounded fetch → recorded source snapshots → synthesis and mechanical verification. This issue authorizes implementation only; it does not authorize live calls, sending, schedules, or deployment.

7. Add offline tests covering:
   - Relevant and irrelevant queries, newest-first selection, deduplication, unknown/stale dates, and publication dates differing from reference periods.
   - Successful release snapshots reaching Claude synthesis and the tool-agent path with valid provenance and digests.
   - HTTP downgrade, credentials, unusual ports, deceptive hostnames, off-allowlist redirects, private-address resolution, and redirect loops.
   - HTTP 429/503, DNS/transport failures, oversized or trickling responses, malformed discovery HTML, unsupported content, and empty extracted text.
   - Malicious embedded instructions and links causing no additional fetch or policy change; OpenAlex credentials never reaching BLS.
   - Discovery/release caps, failed-attempt accounting, exhausted read/evidence budgets, deadline expiry, and no retry, repair, fallback, or third Claude launch.
   - Bundle round-trip and offline finalize with fetched sources; fixture mode performs no network activity.

## Verification

Offline only. Use inline synthetic BLS HTML, mocked HTTP/DNS/time, mock providers, and the existing fake Claude executable. Do not fetch real releases or consume model quota.

Run:

```bash
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py tests/test_runtime.py tests/test_tools.py tests/test_claude_cli.py
bash scripts/check-scope.sh --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py --allowed tests/test_calm_down.py --allowed docs/experiments/calm-down.md
```

Report exactly which checks ran. Synthetic fixtures validate integration and failure handling; they do not establish live BLS markup compatibility or substantive support for a claim.

## Risks/Open Questions

- BLS aggregate statistics cannot establish that AI caused observed employment changes.
- Release revisions and differing reference periods can make apparently conflicting figures valid; synthesis must preserve their context.
- HTML layout changes and text truncation may omit relevant tables or caveats.
- Reserving primary-source reads reduces academic breadth within the same budget.
- Start with BLS only. Additional agencies, professional sources, or news require a separately approved scope.

Drafted by Codex (read-only consult), posted at owner request. Follow-up to #36 / PR #39.


## Goal

Move Claude subprocess lifecycle protection into `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py`, replacing the runner-specific workaround introduced by #36 / PR #39 where equivalent guarantees can be demonstrated.

Currently, the delivery runner passes its `run.lock` descriptor to the research CLI, but `ClaudeCliContext._launch()` starts Claude in a separate session without forwarding that descriptor. If both the runner and research CLI are externally SIGKILLed, Claude can survive while the lock becomes available.

Ensure that surviving research cannot run outside serialization. Catchable-interrupt cleanup alone cannot address SIGKILL; use explicit lock-descriptor inheritance or another demonstrably equivalent mechanism.

## Allowed Files

- `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py`
- `scripts/calm-down-delivery.py`
- `tests/test_claude_cli.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down_email.py`

Limit documentation changes to relevant docstrings and comments in these files. Additional paths require owner approval before implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Establish an explicit lifecycle contract between the runner, research CLI, and Claude subprocess:
  - While Claude research remains alive, a competing runner cannot acquire `run.lock` or reserve another attempt.
  - This holds when the runner dies, the research CLI dies, or both are externally SIGKILLed after Claude launches.
  - Once all lock holders exit, a subsequent runner can acquire the lock normally.
- If forwarding the lock descriptor:
  - Preserve the same locked open file description through each subprocess boundary.
  - Forward only the designated descriptor; keep unrelated descriptors closed.
  - Validate any descriptor handoff and fail closed on invalid configuration.
  - Preserve direct Claude CLI use when no delivery-runner lock is supplied.
  - Keep the descriptor out of prompts, model arguments, persisted records, and unrelated subprocesses.
- Preserve bounded process-group cleanup for normal completion, deadline expiry, output overflow, and catchable interruptions. Cover exceptions after spawning and before communication setup completes.
- Do not silently report successful cleanup when termination cannot be confirmed. Define bounded, fixed diagnostic failures and retain serialization while surviving research holds the lock.
- Remove the runner’s `ctypes`/`prctl` subreaper setup, `/proc` descendant scan, descendant kill/reap loop, and associated constants and diagnostics **only if** the replacement preserves their relevant guarantees. Replace implementation-specific tests with behavioral regression tests. If equivalent protection requires retaining any part, explain the remaining dependency.
- Add offline failure-path tests using local fake executables and real subprocesses where kernel behavior matters:
  - Normal success, nonzero exit, and spawn failure.
  - Deadline expiry and stdout/stderr overflow.
  - `KeyboardInterrupt` and termination during active research.
  - Independent and combined external SIGKILL of runner and research CLI.
  - Claude descendants holding pipes open or surviving their immediate parent, including a separate-session descendant.
  - Cleanup failure, invalid descriptor handoff, unrelated descriptor isolation, and eventual lock release.
  - A competing runner is refused before reservation while research survives; interrupted or abandoned reserved attempts remain counted.
- Preserve existing runtime guarantees: shared request/usage accounting and monotonic deadline; no retry, fallback, repair, or automatic login; byte caps; temporary-directory cleanup where execution can unwind; launch gates and environment filtering; fixed secret-free diagnostics; and run records with `error_class`, `git_sha`, and `config_hash` for recordable failures.
- Preserve durable attempt accounting and delivery state transitions. Do not claim that SIGKILL permits a final `RunRecord` or synchronous cleanup.
- No new dependency, provider, quota source, schedule, delivery behavior, or live model call.

## Verification

Offline only, with fake Claude executables, temporary state directories, and no credentials or network retrieval.

Run:

```bash
pytest tests/test_claude_cli.py tests/test_calm_down_email.py
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py
bash scripts/check-scope.sh \
  --allowed src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py \
  --allowed scripts/calm-down-delivery.py \
  --allowed tests/test_claude_cli.py \
  --allowed tests/test_calm_down_email.py
```

Use explicit synchronization and bounded waits for process tests. Test teardown must terminate fake survivors even after assertion failures. Report platform skips and exactly which checks ran; mocked subprocess tests alone do not prove lock inheritance or SIGKILL behavior.

These are proposed implementation checks; they were not run while drafting this issue.

## Risks / Open Questions

- `_communicate()` already kills Claude’s process group on failure and completion. The missing guarantee crosses process boundaries; adding another interrupt handler alone does not fix it.
- How should the designated descriptor reach `ClaudeCliContext` without broadening the environment allowlist or leaking it into unrelated children?
- Lock inheritance prevents overlapping runs but does not terminate an orphan. A hung holder can block future runs indefinitely; define the supported recovery procedure without automatically breaking the lock.
- A descendant can change sessions or close inherited descriptors. Define the supported process-tree boundary and demonstrate that removing the subreaper does not reopen the separate-session escape covered by PR #39.
- Process-group signaling does not reap arbitrary grandchildren. Distinguish confirmed termination, direct-child reaping, and lock retention in implementation claims.
- SIGTERM handling differs from `KeyboardInterrupt`; verify actual signal behavior rather than assuming both reach Python cleanup.
- The current group-kill helper suppresses signaling errors and wait timeouts. Decide how cleanup uncertainty becomes a safe diagnostic without masking the original failure.
- Define the supported OS/filesystem boundary for inherited advisory `flock`; Linux verification must not imply portability.

## Goal

Build an **internal, offline-tested Claude CLI execution core** for later Calm Down integration. This issue does not enable `AGENT_LAB_PROVIDER=claude-cli`.

Use only the owner’s **existing Claude subscription**, with no new paid service, API billing, overage purchase, or automatic paid fallback. The intended acceptable live use is **one manually authorized research run producing approximately 5,000 output tokens total**. This is a usage expectation, not a proven hard service-side cap.

## Start Gate

**Start gate: do not begin until the owner comments START on this issue.**

`START` authorizes implementation only. It does not authorize a live Claude call, live retrieval, deployment, or subscription changes.

### Authorization record

Before **each live Claude subprocess invocation**, the owner must post an issue comment recording:

```text
AUTHORIZE_LIVE_CLAUDE

Purpose/input: <public research topic or bounded diagnostic>

```

Failures consume authorization once launched. Record the resulting run ID, outcome, and known usage in a follow-up comment without secrets. Further calls require new authorization.

This phase-specific record supplements, and does not replace, the complete OWNER AUTHORIZATION RECORD required by CONTRIBUTING.md, including numeric caps, quota/spend limits, expiry, and stop conditions. No live invocation is authorized by this issue or by START.

## Allowed Files

**A only:**

- `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py` — new internal module.

1. **No production entry point.** A remains internal and unselected by configuration. Mock remains default; Gemini behavior is unchanged.

2. **Concrete launch gate.** Before every launch, require `AGENT_LAB_ALLOW_CLAUDE_CLI=1`; refuse if either `CI` or `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` is present, even empty. Rejection launches nothing and returns a `config` failure. This prevents accidental use in marked environments; it cannot detect cron, prove human presence, verify GitHub comments, or resist someone controlling the environment. Scheduled/unattended use remains prohibited by policy.

3. **Subprocess boundary.** Use an argument array, no shell, stdin prompt, a fresh empty temporary cwd, and:
   ```text
   claude -p --output-format json --tools "" --no-session-persistence --disable-slash-commands --setting-sources ""
   ```
   Explicitly select the approved model. Unsupported flags fail closed. Use a documented environment allowlist for execution and existing-login discovery; exclude Gemini/API-key overrides and unrelated secrets. Never copy or modify credentials. Treat prompts and all subprocess output as untrusted. These controls are not an OS sandbox.

4. **Runtime guarantees, implemented in one reusable execution context:**

   | Guarantee | Required behavior and assertion |
   | --- | --- |
   | Shared accounting | Check request allowance before launch; increment once after successful spawn, including failed calls. Preserve known input/output usage and served model across calls. Represent unavailable usage explicitly in the core result; never imply zero consumption. |
   | No repeated work | No retry, fallback, repair, or automatic login calls, regardless of tool execution or service errors. Rate/reset guidance never triggers another launch or an early retry. |

   | Output limits | Bound captured bytes and validate reported output tokens against the configured per-response allowance. Document that post-response checking cannot impose a hard service-side token cap; do not claim otherwise. |
   | Failure records | Provide a wrapper producing the existing `RunRecord` on success and caught execution failures, including unexpected exceptions, with `git_sha`, secret-free `config_hash`, attempts and partial accounting. Hash model, bounds, launch policy and supplied instructions. Host termination and storage failure cannot guarantee persistence. |
   | Classification | Missing binary/login, unsupported flags and gate/config errors → `config`; explicit service/rate failures → `transient`; deadline/output/accounting exhaustion → `limit`; malformed envelope/generated JSON/schema → `validation`; unexpected exceptions or unrecognized nonzero exits → `internal`. Parse zero-exit error envelopes as failures. |

5. Parse the CLI envelope separately from generated JSON; validate generated output against a caller-supplied schema. Persist only fixed/sanitized diagnostics. Do not place raw prompts, stdout, stderr, credentials, or arbitrary exception text in records or console output; use a safe `RunRecord.prompt` descriptor.

Assert no retry or fallback.

Provider activation, two-phase research, retrieval changes, prompt changes, dependencies, workflows, images, Kubernetes, schedules, credentials, and live calls without individual authorization.

The dependent integration contract is #21. Do not implement it in this issue.

## Goal

Address the owner-reported 2026-11-04 run: only 8 of 29 sources read were published in 2026; the remainder dated from 2002–2025.

For each live search, combine the existing relevance search with a publication-date-filtered search. Make recent evidence available within existing result and reading budgets, and instruct both model paths to acknowledge older evidence without discarding useful foundational research.

This issue covers academic retrieval and instructions. Non-academic sources belong to the companion issue.

## Allowed Files

- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py`
- `src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down.py`
- `docs/experiments/calm-down.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each valid live `search_sources` call performs two sequential OpenAlex searches when the deadline permits:
   - The existing relevance search with `has_abstract:true`.
   - The same query and abstract requirement plus `from_publication_date`, calculated from a configurable recent window.
   - Default the window to 730 days. Validate it as a positive, bounded integer before network activity; document its supported range and configuration mechanism.
   - Resolve the effective window and UTC reference date once per research session. Pass configuration explicitly through the research pipeline and include the effective retrieval policy in the Claude `config_hash`.

2. Merge results deterministically, deduplicating by OpenAlex work ID across passes and searches. Preserve previously read source records and digests. Return at most the existing `MAX_RESULTS_PER_SEARCH = 5`.
   - Alternate recent and relevance candidates, starting with recent, skipping duplicates and filling unused positions from the other list.
   - With distinct results from both passes, the first two candidates include one from each pass, so Claude’s two-read limit does not hide the recent pass.
   - An empty recent result set may use relevance results; it must not imply recent evidence was found.

3. Preserve existing bounds: eight logical searches, fourteen reads, tool-call and token limits, Claude’s six planned queries, two reads per query, 60,000 evidence characters, two launches, and the shared deadline.
   - Reserve the logical search before either request.
   - Explicitly bound added transport work to two initial OpenAlex requests per logical search: at most sixteen per session, excluding only already-bounded redirect hops.
   - No pagination, additional model calls, automatic reruns, or expanded result/read allowances.

4. Update tool-agent, planning, and synthesis instructions to prefer relevant recent evidence for current developments, retain older foundational evidence when appropriate, and disclose when evidence is older or recent evidence is unavailable.
   - Do not equate newer publication with stronger evidence or impose a citation-year quota.
   - Respect existing numeric-writing rules: age disclosures must not introduce unsupported years into claims or caveats.

5. Name the trust boundary: public query text goes to OpenAlex through `safe_get`; returned metadata and abstracts remain untrusted data. Preserve HTTPS checks, credential isolation, keyed redirect restrictions, redaction, source snapshots, and quote verification.

6. Preserve one usage budget per run, model-request pacing, full `Retry-After` handling, and no retry or fallback after tool execution. A failed pass ends the search through the existing error path; it must not silently become an empty result, trigger an anonymous retry, or restart research. The second pass is planned retrieval, never recovery from failure.

7. Add offline failure-path tests covering:
   - Exact filter construction, frozen-date boundaries, invalid window configuration, and both keyed and anonymous requests.
   - Stable merging, duplicate-only results, empty passes, and recent candidates surviving five-result truncation and Claude’s two-read selection.
   - First-pass and second-pass HTTP errors, malformed responses, timeouts, and deadline expiry between passes; no subsequent request or synthesis after terminal failure.
   - Exhausted search/read budgets, preserved read records, key redaction, and keyed redirect refusal.
   - Shared usage accounting, request pacing, `Retry-After`, and no retry/fallback after tool execution using mocked providers and clocks.

## Verification

Offline only, with mocked HTTP, DNS, clocks, and providers; use the existing fake Claude executable. No credentials or live research.

Run:

```bash
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py tests/test_runtime.py tests/test_tools.py tests/test_claude_cli.py
bash scripts/check-scope.sh --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/retrieval.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/__init__.py --allowed src/agent_lab/agents/calm_down/pipeline.py --allowed tests/test_calm_down.py --allowed docs/experiments/calm-down.md
```

Report exactly which checks ran. Offline tests establish request construction and bounded behavior, not live OpenAlex coverage or citation freshness.

## Risks/Open Questions

- Two searches increase transport work and deadline pressure while leaving model and reading budgets unchanged.
- A 730-day window is a starting policy, not evidence that the selected literature covers the latest developments.
- OpenAlex indexing delays and missing abstracts limit recent coverage.
- The reported 29-source count exceeds this checkout’s fourteen-read session cap; reconcile the run artifact and revision before treating that count as a reproducible baseline.

## Goal
Add a reusable `calm_down` research agent on the existing runtime. It investigates a fear about AI on both sides, verifies its citations against retrieved text, and renders a one-off playful email, a plain-text version, and a research dossier. Nothing is sent.

## Allowed Files
Matches #9, which was amended to add `tests/test_runtime.py` (its registry assertion became untrue). `check-scope.sh --base origin/main` passes at head `5a64c7f`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Runtime reuse.** Registered in `REGISTRY` and run through the unchanged `runtime.run_agent`, so the same bounds, retries, error classes, and `RunRecord` apply.
- **Retrieval.** Offline fixtures by default. Opt-in live mode (`AGENT_LAB_CALM_DOWN_RETRIEVAL=live`) uses OpenAlex plus allowlisted HTTPS fetches: every redirect hop is re-checked, non-public IPs are refused, and count, size and time are capped. Live retrieval with the mock provider is refused.
- **Mechanical verification** (fails closed with `insufficient`, exit 4):
  - Every cited source must have been read and must contain the verbatim quote.
  - A claim may not add numbers beyond its quote, and its negation must match the quote's.
  - Every rendered model-written field is checked: no URLs, guarantees, or unsupported numbers.
  - Sections hold the stance they present, with no overlap. Diversity counts distinct works by URL.
- **Two separate actions:**
  - `agent-lab calm-down "<fear>" --out DIR` does **research only**. It writes an immutable `bundle.json` (dossier plus source-text snapshot) and a human-readable `review-request.json`, then exits 5. It never renders an email.
  - `agent-lab calm-down-finalize DIR --review review.json` is **offline**. It loads that exact bundle, checks the source digests, applies the approvals, and renders. It never calls a model or the network.
- **What an approval binds.** Each finding's hash covers the claim, quote, stance, kind, confidence, caveat, analogy, surprising flag, and each source's URL and recomputed text digest. The editorial hash covers the copy, the doom score, the section selections, and the advice mapping. Any change invalidates the approval.
- **Fixture approval.** `--review fixture` is the authoring agent's own non-independent self-review of the offline preview. It is refused for live bundles.
- **Stale outputs.** Research clears every generated file first. Finalize clears `email.*` and `LIMITATION.md` **before** anything can fail. Any refused finalize writes `LIMITATION.md` and keeps the bundle and review request for a retry.
- **Fixture preview** is in `examples/calm-down/`, labelled FIXTURE PREVIEW throughout.

- `git diff --check`: clean.

**Not run / not proven:**

## Goal
Each live `search_sources` call now runs the existing OpenAlex relevance search and then a second search limited to recently published work. - Two sequential requests per search: `has_abstract:true`, then the same query plus `from_publication_date`. The window comes from `AGENT_LAB_CALM_DOWN_RECENT_DAYS`: default 730, an integer from 1 to 3650, validated before any output or network activity. Drafted by Codex (read-only consult), posted at owner request. Follow-up to #36 / PR #39.


## Goal

Move Claude subprocess lifecycle protection into `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py`, replacing the runner-specific workaround introduced by #36 / PR #39 where equivalent guarantees can be demonstrated.

Currently, the delivery runner passes its `run.lock` descriptor to the research CLI, but `ClaudeCliContext._launch()` starts Claude in a separate session without forwarding that descriptor. If both the runner and research CLI are externally SIGKILLed, Claude can survive while the lock becomes available.

Ensure that surviving research cannot run outside serialization. Catchable-interrupt cleanup alone cannot address SIGKILL; use explicit lock-descriptor inheritance or another demonstrably equivalent mechanism.

## Allowed Files

- `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py`
- `scripts/calm-down-delivery.py`
- `tests/test_claude_cli.py`
- `tests/test_calm_down_email.py`

Limit documentation changes to relevant docstrings and comments in these files. Additional paths require owner approval before implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Establish an explicit lifecycle contract between the runner, research CLI, and Claude subprocess:
  - While Claude research remains alive, a competing runner cannot acquire `run.lock` or reserve another attempt.
  - This holds when the runner dies, the research CLI dies, or both are externally SIGKILLed after Claude launches.
  - Once all lock holders exit, a subsequent runner can acquire the lock normally.
- If forwarding the lock descriptor:
  - Preserve the same locked open file description through each subprocess boundary.
  - Forward only the designated descriptor; keep unrelated descriptors closed.
  - Validate any descriptor handoff and fail closed on invalid configuration.
  - Preserve direct Claude CLI use when no delivery-runner lock is supplied.
  - Keep the descriptor out of prompts, model arguments, persisted records, and unrelated subprocesses.
- Preserve bounded process-group cleanup for normal completion, deadline expiry, output overflow, and catchable interruptions. Cover exceptions after spawning and before communication setup completes.
- Do not silently report successful cleanup when termination cannot be confirmed. Define bounded, fixed diagnostic failures and retain serialization while surviving research holds the lock.
- Remove the runner’s `ctypes`/`prctl` subreaper setup, `/proc` descendant scan, descendant kill/reap loop, and associated constants and diagnostics **only if** the replacement preserves their relevant guarantees. Replace implementation-specific tests with behavioral regression tests. If equivalent protection requires retaining any part, explain the remaining dependency.
- Add offline failure-path tests using local fake executables and real subprocesses where kernel behavior matters:
  - Normal success, nonzero exit, and spawn failure.
  - Deadline expiry and stdout/stderr overflow.
  - `KeyboardInterrupt` and termination during active research.
  - Independent and combined external SIGKILL of runner and research CLI.
  - Claude descendants holding pipes open or surviving their immediate parent, including a separate-session descendant.
  - Cleanup failure, invalid descriptor handoff, unrelated descriptor isolation, and eventual lock release.
  - A competing runner is refused before reservation while research survives; interrupted or abandoned reserved attempts remain counted.
- Preserve existing runtime guarantees: shared request/usage accounting and monotonic deadline; no retry, fallback, repair, or automatic login; byte caps; temporary-directory cleanup where execution can unwind; launch gates and environment filtering; fixed secret-free diagnostics; and run records with `error_class`, `git_sha`, and `config_hash` for recordable failures.
- Preserve durable attempt accounting and delivery state transitions. Do not claim that SIGKILL permits a final `RunRecord` or synchronous cleanup.
- No new dependency, provider, quota source, schedule, delivery behavior, or live model call.

## Verification

Offline only, with fake Claude executables, temporary state directories, and no credentials or network retrieval.

Run:

```bash
pytest tests/test_claude_cli.py tests/test_calm_down_email.py
pytest tests/test_calm_down.py
bash scripts/check-scope.sh \
  --allowed src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py \
  --allowed scripts/calm-down-delivery.py \
  --allowed tests/test_claude_cli.py \
  --allowed tests/test_calm_down_email.py
```

Use explicit synchronization and bounded waits for process tests. Test teardown must terminate fake survivors even after assertion failures. Report platform skips and exactly which checks ran; mocked subprocess tests alone do not prove lock inheritance or SIGKILL behavior.

These are proposed implementation checks; they were not run while drafting this issue.

## Risks / Open Questions

- `_communicate()` already kills Claude’s process group on failure and completion. The missing guarantee crosses process boundaries; adding another interrupt handler alone does not fix it.
- How should the designated descriptor reach `ClaudeCliContext` without broadening the environment allowlist or leaking it into unrelated children?
- Lock inheritance prevents overlapping runs but does not terminate an orphan. A hung holder can block future runs indefinitely; define the supported recovery procedure without automatically breaking the lock.
- A descendant can change sessions or close inherited descriptors. Define the supported process-tree boundary and demonstrate that removing the subreaper does not reopen the separate-session escape covered by PR #39.
- Process-group signaling does not reap arbitrary grandchildren. Distinguish confirmed termination, direct-child reaping, and lock retention in implementation claims.
- SIGTERM handling differs from `KeyboardInterrupt`; verify actual signal behavior rather than assuming both reach Python cleanup.
- The current group-kill helper suppresses signaling errors and wait timeouts. Decide how cleanup uncertainty becomes a safe diagnostic without masking the original failure.
- Define the supported OS/filesystem boundary for inherited advisory `flock`; Linux verification must not imply portability.

Build an **internal, offline-tested Claude CLI execution core** for later Calm Down integration. This issue does not enable `AGENT_LAB_PROVIDER=claude-cli`.

This is the execution-core issue only. Calm Down provider selection, two-phase research, prompts and bundle integration are tracked separately in #21, which depends on this issue merging. One issue, one PR. Claude implements; Codex independently reviews the exact final head.

Use only the owner’s **existing Claude subscription**, with no new paid service, API billing, overage purchase, or automatic paid fallback. The intended acceptable live use is **one manually authorized research run producing approximately 5,000 output tokens total**. This is a usage expectation, not a proven hard service-side cap.

## Start Gate

**Start gate: do not begin until the owner comments START on this issue.**

`START` authorizes implementation only. It does not authorize a live Claude call, live retrieval, deployment, or subscription changes.

### Authorization record

Before **each live Claude subprocess invocation**, the owner must post an issue comment recording:

```text
AUTHORIZE_LIVE_CLAUDE
Issue: #17
Commit: <full SHA>
Purpose/input: <public research topic or bounded diagnostic>
Model: <explicit model>
Call: <one named phase; exactly one invocation>
Usage: <output allocation within the approximately 5k-token research-run expectation>
Billing: existing subscription only; no API billing or paid overage
Expiry: <one-use authorization and expiration>
```

Failures consume authorization once launched. Record the resulting run ID, outcome, and known usage in a follow-up comment without secrets. Further calls require new authorization.

This phase-specific record supplements, and does not replace, the complete OWNER AUTHORIZATION RECORD required by CONTRIBUTING.md, including numeric caps, quota/spend limits, expiry, and stop conditions. No live invocation is authorized by this issue or by START.

## Allowed Files

**A only:**

- `src/agent_lab/claude_cli.py` — new internal module.
- `tests/test_claude_cli.py` — new offline tests.
- `docs/experiments/calm-down.md` — existing; document the disabled core, gates, usage policy, and limits.

No other existing source files need modification for A.

Integration scope and acceptance criteria are in #21; they are not authorized changes under this issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No production entry point.** A remains internal and unselected by configuration. Mock remains default; Gemini behavior is unchanged.

2. **Concrete launch gate.** Before every launch, require `AGENT_LAB_ALLOW_CLAUDE_CLI=1`; refuse if either `CI` or `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` is present, even empty. Rejection launches nothing and returns a `config` failure. This prevents accidental use in marked environments; it cannot detect cron, prove human presence, verify GitHub comments, or resist someone controlling the environment. Scheduled/unattended use remains prohibited by policy.

3. **Subprocess boundary.** Use an argument array, no shell, stdin prompt, a fresh empty temporary cwd, and:
   ```text
   claude -p --output-format json --tools "" --no-session-persistence --disable-slash-commands --setting-sources ""
   ```
   Explicitly select the approved model. Unsupported flags fail closed. Use a documented environment allowlist for execution and existing-login discovery; exclude Gemini/API-key overrides and unrelated secrets. Never copy or modify credentials. Treat prompts and all subprocess output as untrusted. These controls are not an OS sandbox.

4. **Runtime guarantees, implemented in one reusable execution context:**

   | Guarantee | Required behavior and assertion |
   | --- | --- |
   | Shared accounting | Check request allowance before launch; increment once after successful spawn, including failed calls. Preserve known input/output usage and served model across calls. Represent unavailable usage explicitly in the core result; never imply zero consumption. |
   | No repeated work | No retry, fallback, repair, or automatic login calls, regardless of tool execution or service errors. Rate/reset guidance never triggers another launch or an early retry. |
   | Bounded deadline | One monotonic deadline supplied to the context; every call uses remaining time. Refuse expired calls. Concurrently drain stdout/stderr with explicit byte caps; timeout/overflow terminates and reaps the process group with bounded cleanup and removes temporary files. |
   | Output limits | Bound captured bytes and validate reported output tokens against the configured per-response allowance. Document that post-response checking cannot impose a hard service-side token cap; do not claim otherwise. |
   | Failure records | Provide a wrapper producing the existing `RunRecord` on success and caught execution failures, including unexpected exceptions, with `git_sha`, secret-free `config_hash`, attempts and partial accounting. Hash model, bounds, launch policy and supplied instructions. Host termination and storage failure cannot guarantee persistence. |
   | Classification | Missing binary/login, unsupported flags and gate/config errors → `config`; explicit service/rate failures → `transient`; deadline/output/accounting exhaustion → `limit`; malformed envelope/generated JSON/schema → `validation`; unexpected exceptions or unrecognized nonzero exits → `internal`. Parse zero-exit error envelopes as failures. |

5. Parse the CLI envelope separately from generated JSON; validate generated output against a caller-supplied schema. Persist only fixed/sanitized diagnostics. Do not place raw prompts, stdout, stderr, credentials, or arbitrary exception text in records or console output; use a safe `RunRecord.prompt` descriptor.

## Verification

Run offline:

```sh
pytest tests/test_claude_cli.py
```

Mock process creation and service output. Test exact arguments, stdin, environment/cwd, every gate combination, shared accounting/deadline across two synthetic calls, malformed and zero-exit error envelopes, missing login/binary, unsupported flags, unknown exits, partial usage, timeout/overflow, cleanup, and secret canaries. Assert no retry or fallback.

Before push, run `scripts/check-scope.sh` against committed HEAD with the three allowed paths. Require applicable CI and independent review at the exact head.

**Contract checks:** the split was published at the owner's request on 2026-11-04 after reading the current issue and repository guidance. No source files changed. **Not checked:** tests executed, CI, installed Claude version/flags, native login, subscription billing behavior, live research, or the reported trial.

## Out Of Scope

Provider activation, two-phase research, retrieval changes, prompt changes, dependencies, workflows, images, Kubernetes, schedules, credentials, and live calls without individual authorization.

The dependent integration contract is #21. Do not implement it in this issue.

## Owner Decisions Needed

- Comment START naming this execution-core task when ready. The owner requested publication of the split; that request does not start implementation.

hits.body:
## Goal
Experiment 2: let the local n8n instance submit, monitor, and collect results from the demo agent running as a Kubernetes Job on a throwaway local k3d cluster, using narrowly scoped RBAC. Demonstrate success, deterministic limit failure, and deadline timeout. Learning experiment only: no schedule, no persistent infrastructure, no runtime changes.

Trust boundary: n8n (Docker) -> Kubernetes API over the private k3d Docker network, authenticated by a short-lived ServiceAccount token. The ServiceAccount may only create/get/delete Jobs and read pods/logs in `agent-lab`. A ValidatingAdmissionPolicy pins what those Jobs may contain (image, args shape, no command/lifecycle hooks/probes, env allowlist, no secrets, no SA token, bounded deadline, single pod, capped resource limits), and the namespace enforces Pod Security `restricted`. Prompts are untrusted: they are passed as one argv element after `--`, never through a shell.

## Allowed Files
- `k8s/n8n/` (new: namespace PSA labels, RBAC, admission policy)
- `n8n/` (new: exported workflow JSON, no credentials)
- `docs/learning/n8n-kubernetes.md` (new)
- `README.md` (link only)

## Acceptance Criteria
- `kubectl apply -k k8s/ && kubectl apply -f k8s/n8n/` on a fresh k3d cluster creates the base resources plus SA/Role/RoleBinding and admission policy; no ClusterRole bindings, no cluster-admin.
- The SA cannot read secrets, cannot create Jobs that violate the policy (wrong image, extra env, secretRef, missing `--`), and cannot act outside `agent-lab` (verified with `kubectl auth can-i` and rejected creates).
- Importable n8n workflow(s) contain no tokens or certificates.
- Evidence of three real executions: success, `error_class=limit` failure, and `DeadlineExceeded` timeout.
- Doc gives exact reproduce + cleanup steps and explains triggers, external Job control, RBAC, polling vs events, error propagation, and cloud changes.
- Existing `k8s/` base, runtime, and Fantasy GM workflows unchanged.

## Verification
- Manual local run of all three scenarios through n8n (`n8n execute`), with n8n output, `kubectl` and pod logs recorded in the PR.
- RBAC/policy negative checks via `kubectl auth can-i --as` and rejected Job creates.
- `bash scripts/check-scope.sh --allowed k8s/n8n/ --allowed n8n/ --allowed docs/learning/n8n-kubernetes.md --allowed README.md`.
- CI (`ci.yml`) on the PR head. k3d-smoke does not exercise `k8s/n8n/`.



## Amendment (owner-approved, after Codex review of ed7daeb)
- Entry point changed from `kubectl apply -k k8s/n8n/` to `kubectl apply -k k8s/ && kubectl apply -f k8s/n8n/`: kustomize rejects an overlay nested inside its own base (`cycle detected`).
- Admission policy must also reject lifecycle hooks/probes, `parallelism`/`completions` other than 1, and missing or excessive resource limits.
