## Problem

- A flaky story fails the visual review gate of a merge queue run and kicks every PR in the batch, until a person quarantines it.

## Changes

A run that closes a flake proof now quarantines the story and passes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    A[Run finishes diffing]:::phYellow --> B[Stamp quarantines and count]:::phBlue --> C[Gate]:::phYellow
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    A[Run finishes diffing]:::phYellow --> P[A story failed: look for a flake proof]:::phBlue
    P --> G[Commit ancestry from GitHub]:::phRed
    P --> Q[Quarantine proven flakes]:::phBlue --> B[Stamp quarantines and count]:::phBlue --> C[Gate]:::phYellow
```

- A proof: the story failed, rendered clean on a commit that contains that failure, then failed again on a commit that contains the clean one. Two pictures on one commit also count.
- One failure and one clean run prove nothing, because a break and a fix look the same.
- Only full master and merge queue runs count, only against the default branch's baseline, and their commits are verified on GitHub.
- `auto_quarantine_mode` on the repo: `off` (default), `preview` (log only), `on` (14 days, owner notice).
- Past 10 automatic quarantines in 24 hours, proofs are not applied and the visual review owners get one Slack notice.

hits.body:
**Context**

Devex runs week to week without a great way to tell if the loop is actually getting faster. "CI feels slow" and "the stack is heavy" are vibes, not numbers. Without measurement we can not prioritise well, prove impact, or tell product teams where they are the bottleneck.

**Goal**

Give every loop (local dev, CI, review/merge) a metric, surfaced in one place. Make wins visible and regressions catchable, and give leadership a clear number for what % of engineering spend goes to devex.

**Scope / ideas**

- Open-PR-to-merge time (overall and per team)
- Flakiness: how often a job runs more than once per PR, and which jobs
- CI run times and cost, attributed per product so teams own their own footprint
- Stack startup time and RAM usage tracked over time
- A single dashboard product/eng leadership can read without us in the room

**Current state**

In flight via the engineering_analytics work (cost/friction lens, GitHub source selector, warehouse-shape fixes). This epic is about turning that into a durable, trusted measurement layer.

**How it fits**

Measurement, not reduction — CI costs (Q) and fast CI (C) are the work of cutting the numbers this surfaces. Code ownership (NN) is what makes the per-team slices land on someone.

**Open questions**

- Can this replace Mendral?
- Can we extend it to other repos beyond the monorepo?

## Problem

The web, mobile and desktop apps and the agent each bundle a copy of the task model catalog. A new model version needs that copy regenerated, and a desktop release, before a picker can show it. The backend no longer reads the catalog, so the copies can also disagree with it.

## Changes

- The catalog's model rows, price tables and effort tables are deleted. The generator now emits only choices: adapters, effort tiers, default models, slider rungs and the families a picker offers.
- Web and mobile read `GET /tasks/models/`. It now also returns each model's cost summary, whether pickers offer it and the cost baseline's name.
- Desktop and the agent read a model's adapter, name, efforts, context window and price from the gateway listing they already fetch. They offer the two newest versions of each allowed family, the rule the backend uses.
- The hand-kept fallbacks are deleted: the web and mobile effort fallback, mobile's retired-model list and the desktop loop picker's offline model list.

Visible:

- Desktop's default Codex model moves from GPT-6 Sol to GPT-6.2 Sol.
- A model the gateway doesn't describe has no effort picker. Today that is GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 Flash, Kimi and any ChatGPT-plan variant the gateway doesn't list.
- Efforts and prices follow the gateway where the catalog differed. Claude Sonnet 4.6 gains Max, for example.
- DeepSeek rows have no gateway name, so they read "Deepseek V4 Flash 0731".
- Pickers are empty until the listing loads. The web retries a failed load three times.
- The long-context price tier that GPT Sol models showed is gone, because the gateway lists base rates only.
- On the legacy gateway fallback, desktop offers every model that gateway lists and shows no effort picker, because its listing has no families or efforts.

Trade-off: desktop reads the allowed families from its bundle, so a new family still needs a desktop release. A new version of a family doesn't.

## How did you test this code?

The backend, web, mobile, desktop, agent, agent-contracts and harness suites pass locally, and the desktop workspace type-checks. One test checks the agent's offered list against the backend's for the same saved production listing. Not run locally: the desktop SQLite tests, which need a native build this machine lacks. No picker was rendered in a browser or in the desktop app.

CI report: the complexity warnings name functions this PR edits but doesn't restructure. The two call assertions it counts read the request a run sends and the config a session starts with. Its duplicates are two generated OAuth scope files this PR doesn't touch and the report model resolver, which the desktop and web hosts already bound the same way and which gains one line in each here. Its coverage section predates the last pushes. A local run covers every changed line in the three backend modules it lists. The three lines in a test file are a TypedDict's field annotations. The MCP snapshot gains the models tool's `include_unoffered` parameter. The two eager graph roots over budget show the same delta on #139329, which changes eight bytes of web code. The two flaky Playwright tests cover person properties and trace screenshots.

## Problem

Notebook authors need an obvious way to turn their own cells into an app. An author reviewing a rollout also needs to bring together a feature flag, an adoption funnel, and the recordings behind a drop-off.

## Changes

**Create app** opens a blank builder. Authors can add notebook cells, text, and inputs as usual. **Start from a template** offers an optional **Feature launch review**. In a populated app, **More app actions → Add from template…** adds the review on a new tab.

## Problem

- Coding agents can approve, tolerate and finalize visual review snapshots over MCP, but they cannot quarantine one.
- A flaky story that blocks a PR therefore pushes an agent toward a toleration. A toleration accepts one exact hash forever, cannot be undone through the API, and helps no other PR.
- A quarantine covers every PR and expires, so it is the right tool for a story that flakes on master.
- The triage skill also contradicted itself: approve and tolerate were "reversible, no gate needed" in one section and "never without user confirmation" in another, and quarantine was "via the UI".

## Changes

- **Agents can quarantine, lift and recompute.** Three existing endpoints get MCP tools: `quarantine-create`, `quarantine-expire-create` and `recompute-create`. Recompute is what turns the required check green after a quarantine or toleration.
- **An agent quarantine always expires within 30 days.** Through MCP, an omitted or later `expires_at` becomes 30 days out, because no agent comes back to lift it. The UI keeps any expiry, including none.
- **Agents notify the owning team.** The skill tells them to pass `notify_owners: true` (added in #109094), so the people who must fix the story hear about the quarantine.
- **The skill now opens with a decision table**, taken from a replay of recent PR runs against the flakiness overview:

| Evidence | Agent action | Human yes |
|---|---|---|
| Own change, intended | approve, then ask for finalize | yes, per run |
| Story outside the change, `unstable`, `hard_count` ≥ 5, flaked in the last 7 days | quarantine, then recompute | no |
| `broken` (a stale baseline) | report, recommend re-baseline | yes |
| Same size, `change_kind: pixel`, named noise | tolerate, then recompute | no |
| Anything else | report and stop | yes |

- **The thresholds come from data, not from the state alone.**
  - One master failure is enough for `unstable`. In the replay, those single failures looked like real changes that a quarantine would hide.
  - `window_runs` is the repo's run count, the same for every entry, so it cannot gate anything.
  - Diff percentage does not separate noise from a real change: most same-size diffs under 1% were `structural` and approved as real.
- **Tolerate is now described as render noise only**, never a way past the gate.
- Mechanical: every VR tool description condensed (about 9.5k to 6.3k characters across more tools), regenerated MCP and frontend types, one README line.

> [!NOTE]
> Independent of #109785, which makes recompute re-run only the completing CI job and closes a gate bypass. Without it, recompute still works, but it captures every snapshot again. #109779 touches the same tools.yaml entry for run snapshots, and whichever lands second regenerates.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran the visual review backend tests, the MCP instructions unit test, `hogli lint:skills` and `pnpm --filter=@posthog/mcp lint-tool-names` locally.
- Not run: the new tools against a live MCP session. The endpoints already serve the UI.

**Test rationale:** `test_an_agent_quarantine_always_expires_within_the_cap` (parameterized over actor and requested expiry) catches an agent quarantine that never expires or outlives the cap, and a cap that leaks into human quarantines. No existing test covered the `source` of a quarantine.

- [ ] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [x] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

The new tools carry the existing `visual-review` MCP feature flag, like every VR tool.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

The triage skill and the visual review README are updated in this PR.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

## Problem

- Teams that run a data governance process cannot see a definition's description, owner, verified, or hidden fields in SQL, so they cannot alert on definitions that miss metadata. #124827 left these fields out of `system.event_definitions` and `system.property_definitions`.
- Stacked on #128730, which adds the team-scoped metadata tables that this PR reads.

## Changes

- `system.event_definitions` and `system.property_definitions` get `description`, `verified`, `verified_at`, `verified_by_id`, `hidden`, `updated_at`, and `updated_by_id`. Events also get `owner_id`.
- A definition that nobody opened or edited reads NULL for the text and time columns, and 0 for `verified` and `hidden`.
- The columns come from a lazy join to the metadata tables. Only a query that selects them reads those tables, and the team guard reaches the Postgres read. The definition tables are read as before.
- The `hogql-definition-metadata` flag gates the join. It is evaluated only for a query that selects these columns. When it is off, that query fails with a clear error.
- Object-level access control on a definition also hides its metadata. Property-level restrictions apply to a direct read of the hidden metadata table.
- Mechanical: the schema snapshot, the resolver manifest, and isolation-test exclusions for the two hidden tables.

> [!NOTE]
> Turn on the flag after the backfill from #128730 is complete and a rerun changes about 0 rows. To measure the new read volume, filter ClickHouse `query_log` for the `__metadata` join alias, or check `pg_stat_statements` on the HogQL read endpoint. HogQL has no per-table metric.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the cases extend `TestSystemDefinitionTables` in `test_system_tables.py`, next to the existing definition table tests.

- Column mapping for both tables, including 0 for a definition without metadata. HogQL prints `toInt` as `accurateCastOrNull`, which an earlier version got wrong.
- The metadata of another team stays out of the join and out of a direct read of the hidden table.
- The flag off fails the query with the error.
- The metadata of a restricted property stays out of a direct read.

The printed ClickHouse SQL shows `WHERE team_id = <id>` inside the Postgres read of both metadata tables. A ClickHouse trace log was not captured. Not checked locally: repo-wide mypy and semgrep. CI runs both.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- When the flag is on for everyone, the "System tables" section of the posthog.com docs (`contents/docs/data-pipelines/sources/posthog.mdx`) needs the new columns. That is a separate PR in the posthog.com repo.

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions` (read from `.agents/skills`).

- **Decisions:** the flag is checked in the join resolver, not with `_cached_team_flag` when the database is built, so queries that do not read these columns pay nothing.

## Problem

- Stripe webhook deliveries fail with 400 "Bad signature" when the `Stripe-Signature` header carries more than `t` and one `v1`. Both the Stripe webhook source and the Stripe warehouse source reject them.
- [Stripe's docs](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks?verify=verify-manually#verify-signature) describe the header below. A verifier must accept unknown entries, must not depend on their count or order, and must accept a delivery when any `v1` is valid.
- Stripe sends one `v1` per active signing secret, for example while a secret is rolled.

```text
t=1798765432,
v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd,
v1=38c9f77a6fdb86d7f67e427e6076f1e38e244eb8ddc7a90f7f9dd4478d5bb2c2,
v0=6ffbb59b2300aae63f272406069a9788598b792a944a07aba816edb039989a39,
secret=whsec_****************************PzVt,
destination=we_1TN7mG6oEAX7HoXLZoZugElv,
payload=a25aefc6
```

The example comes from Stripe's docs. The real header is one line.

The parser came in with #36316, and #48106 copied it into the warehouse source.

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!CAUTION]
> 🔴 **Merge risk: high** · one-way door (merge-risk rubric)
> - Running the new command rewrites the stored code and bytecode of live Stripe webhook sources. A parser bug would then drop their deliveries without an error anyone sees. Few teams use these sources.
> - The merge alone is two-way: it changes only templates, and nothing rewrites stored code until someone runs the command. The command test, a live run, and a production check of every stored function limit the risk.
> - **Revert:** `git revert` the merge commit. After the command has run, also run the six replacements in reverse on the functions it updated. Nothing keeps a copy of the old code.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

Each entry of the header, before and after:

| Entry | Old parser | New parser |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret=whsec_…` | `like 't=%'` matches anywhere, so it replaced the timestamp | Ignored. Keys match with `startsWith` |
| Two `v1` | Kept the last. Failed when the first one matched | Accepts a match on any `v1` |
| `v0`, `destination`, `payload` | Ignored | Ignored |

- Warehouse sources run the template's bytecode, so they get the fix on deploy.
- Webhook sources keep a copy of the template code. A new `update_hog_function_code` option rewrites six lines in them. It skips a function when any of the six is missing or another read of the old variable is left, and lists that function for a manual update.
- Mechanical: the consumer test's parser copy, a bytecode fixture, and two misdirected `compile_hog` patches in the command tests.
- The PR mixes the Node and Python lanes on purpose, with the `cross-lane-change` label: the same bug lives in one template of each.

> [!NOTE]
> After deploy, run this in each region, `--dry-run` first:
> `python manage.py update_hog_function_code --replace-key stripe-signature-header-parsing`

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Stripe's header shape fails on the old parser and passes on the new one, in both template tests. The command test runs migrated bytecode on that header and on a forged one, and checks that two hand-edited functions are skipped and listed.

- Live run: a local CDP API returned 400 for that header, then 200 after the command. A forged delivery still got 400. A hand-edited function was listed and kept working as before.
- Shadow diff: old and new parsers over 18 headers. Nothing unsigned is newly accepted.
- Production check: every stored webhook source with the old parser matches all six lines.
- Not run: a live warehouse delivery. Its template and consumer tests cover it.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

| Question | Answer | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Which Stripe header format do we support? | The full documented format. Replaced a fix for unknown fields only | 👤 Human | [comment](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/135555#issuecomment-6946074271) |
| Accept the review gap from the GPT sandbox outage? | Yes. A full-diff GPT-6.1-sol review stands in for the cross-family panel | 👤 Human | [comment](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/135555#issuecomment-6946074271) |
| Split the PR or label it for mixing lanes? | One PR with `cross-lane-change`. Replaced the recommended split | 👤 Human | [comment](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/135555#issuecomment-6946074271) |
| Which stored functions does the migration rewrite? | Webhook sources only. Warehouse sources use template bytecode | 🤖 Agent | [comment](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/135555#issuecomment-6946074271) |
| How does the migration rewrite stored code? | Six line replacements with an all-or-nothing guard | 🤖 Agent | [comment](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/135555#issuecomment-6946074271) |
| Guard against other reads of the old variable? | Yes. Skip and list the function. Replaced "no", after the proof judge noted a function can change before the command runs | 🤖 Agent | [comment](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/135555#issuecomment-6946074271) |

**Agent:** Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/merge-risk`, `/qa-swarm`

## Problem

We currently have a [workflow](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/workflows/01a17cbf-4136-0000-b328-91ffb1cef416/workflow) that uses `user account deleted` to opt the user's email out of marketing after a one-hour wait.

I think the email should stay on the opt-out list after account deletion, just in case a background job or late event arrives after that (e.g. , someone could open an email sent before they deleted their account and we capture event). 

After #137035, account deletion immediately requests person profiles, events, recordings deletion. Profile deletion can run in the request or a queued worker. Event deletion runs separately, on a weekly schedule by default. It only covers events with `_timestamp` at or before the deletion request time. Recordings are deleted through a separate Temporal workflow. 

**The `user account deleted` event can itself arrive after that cutoff and survive deletion**, potentially recreating the profile with the same Distinct ID. I'd remove the event and record the opt-out directly. This also avoids relying on the workflow finding an email on an already-deleted profile.

## Changes

- Record an email-based marketing opt-out after commit, before deleting person profile (only in cloud deployments). 
- Remove `user account deleted` and its reporting helper.
- If opt-out fails, log the error and continue with analytics deletion. No automatic retry yet. 

> Requires `messaging_preference:write` on `POSTHOG_USER_DELETION_API_KEY` and `workflows-transactional-email-api` enabled for the target project.  

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Extend existing deletion tests to cover request ordering, opt-out failure, both regions, missing distinct IDs, and removal of the event.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- No existing document covers this internal integration; setup requirements are above.

## 🤖 Agent context

Other late-arriving events remain a separate concern.

## Problem

The flakiness overview reports about 2,400 storybook snapshots as "noisy", so the repo looks far flakier than it is, and people chase stories that never block anyone.

- `noisy` meant: rendered a picture other than the baseline, absorbed below the diff thresholds with room to spare.
- A sample of 8 master runs shows ~1,720 of those render one stable picture that differs slightly from the baseline, matched by an auto-minted tolerated hash. Only ~400 vary between runs.
- Every auto variant is diffed against the baseline itself, so the 2.5% pixel / 1% SSIM thresholds bound the total drift. Past that, the run reports `changed` and someone approves a new baseline. Drift below the line is internal bookkeeping, not instability.

## Changes

- The `noisy` state is gone. A snapshot that only absorbed diffs with room to spare is `clean`.

hits.body:
A query that reads a group property now loads only the groups of the events it matches. Two common query shapes used to load every group of that type instead.

## Problem

Reading a group property joins the groups table. Unbounded, that join loads every group of that type in the project, properties included, however few events the query matches ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0BNGDM28RX/p1794507361864589)). HogQL bounds the join for simple queries with a key filter built from the query's WHERE. It gave up in two cases.

The first is a table alias. Funnels, paths, experiments and the session recording list all read `FROM events AS e`. The second is a WHERE that filters on a group or person property, which is what a group property filter on any insight produces.

On PostHog's own project, this query differs with and without the alias only in the key filter:

```sql
SELECT group_0.properties.name AS org, count() AS c
FROM events AS e
WHERE e.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND e.event = '$pageview'
GROUP BY org ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 5
```

| | ClickHouse time | Memory per shard | Received from the groups table |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| With the alias, no key filter | 2.4 s | 431 MB | 444 MB |
| Without the alias, key filter | 1.2 s | 160 MB | 50 MB |

## Changes

Results do not change. The groups read of an affected query gains the key filter. This is an experiment with a group property filter, from the test snapshots:

```sql
-- before
FROM groups
WHERE and(equals(groups.team_id, 99999), equals(index, 0))

-- after
FROM groups
WHERE and(equals(groups.team_id, 99999), equals(index, 0),
          globalIn(key, (SELECT DISTINCT events.`$group_0` AS `$group_0`
                         FROM events
                         WHERE and(equals(events.team_id, 99999),
                                   greaterOrEquals(toTimeZone(events.timestamp, 'UTC'), ...),
                                   lessOrEquals(toTimeZone(events.timestamp, 'UTC'), ...),
                                   in(events.event, ['$feature_flag_called', '$experiment_exposure']),
                                   ...))))
```

The outer WHERE also holds `equals(events__group_0.properties___name, 'Test Group')`, the term the key subquery leaves out.

The pushdown, `_outer_prefilter`, now accepts any alias and repeats it in the key subquery. It used to skip a WHERE that names a group or a person. It now splits the WHERE into top-level AND terms and keeps the ones that do not, because a copied group term would resolve the same join again and recurse. Fewer terms only widen the key set, so no needed group is lost. A term under an OR is never split. A term that calls `rand()` is left out too: the key subquery reads events separately and would sample other rows. A term that holds a subquery is left out as well, because its copy does not resolve again.

The WHERE must still hold a timestamp term. Each affected query scans its matched events once more for the keys, as unaliased queries already do. That loses when almost every group appears in the date range.

## How did you test this code?

CI runs the tests; nothing ran locally. The table is four runs through the production query API, where master already adds the key filter for the unaliased form.

**Test rationale:** `test_bounds_each_group_join_whose_key_subquery_can_reuse_the_where` catches a key subquery that keeps a group or person term or drops a term under an OR. `test_key_subquery_leaves_out_a_term_that_differs_on_each_read` catches a copied `rand()`.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2)

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code desktop, local. The work started from query logs of PostHog's own project. The test queries are invented, and no log data is in this PR.
- **Decisions:** A term under an OR stays in the key subquery, because dropping it would lose rows.
- **Decisions:** The same-table check runs on the kept terms only. A dropped term never reaches the key subquery.
- **Decisions:** `_PREFILTER_SOURCES` replaces the per-table alias list, because every alias is now accepted.
- **Decisions:** A term that calls a nondeterministic function is left out with `contains_nondeterministic_function`, the rule the persons join pushdown already applies. A term that holds a subquery is left out with `contains_subquery`; master copied it for an unaliased FROM, and the copy fails to resolve when the subquery has its own lazy join or reads a scalar WITH binding.
- **Decisions:** A leading name is peeled as a table qualifier only when the FROM puts it in scope: the alias when one is set, otherwise the table chain or its last part.
- **Decisions:** The new cases replace the two tests that asserted the old skip.
- **Decisions:** A search for an open PR with the same fix found nothing.
- **Read closely:** `_outer_prefilter` in `posthog/hogql/database/schema/groups.py`.

</details>

Recalculation keeps rerunning metrics that fail the same way every time, and nothing records which metric version failed. `metric_errors` entries do not store the calculation key, and a later run on the same window overwrites the result row that holds it.

This is PR 0 of a stack for a pre-run recalculation skip classifier. The classifier can only compare keys written after this PR deploys, so this change ships first and alone.

<!-- Does this fix an issue? Uncomment the line below with the issue ID to automatically close it when merged -->
<!-- Closes #ISSUE_ID -->

## Changes

<!-- For each change a person can notice, say what they will now see or do differently, not only the code path that does it. Mark the rest as mechanical so a reviewer knows nothing user-visible is hiding in it. -->

<!-- If there are frontend changes, please include screenshots. For a new interaction that one screenshot cannot show, a short GIF or animated WebP of the flow can replace the after screenshot. -->
<!-- PostHog employees: `hogli pr:upload-image <file>` uploads to the public PostHog/pr-assets repo and prints markdown to paste here. Never upload customer data, secrets, or internal info. -->

<!-- If a reference design was involved, include a link to the relevant Figma frame! -->

Every terminal failure entry in `ExperimentMetricsRecalculation.metric_errors` now stores the metric's `calculation_key`. Nothing user-visible changes, so there are no screenshots. Classification, retries and the UI behave as before.

### Store the key on each failure entry

`_record_failure` and `_fail` take a required keyword `calculation_key: str | None`, so a new caller must choose a real key or `None`. The calculation activity and the out-of-time recorder compute the key once, where `has_completed` already computes it. No failure path computes the key, so a key error cannot hide the original failure. Discovery failures (experiment gone, metric gone, no `start_date`) store `None`.

- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/recalculation_logic.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/test_recalculation_activities.py`

### Rejected recalculations keep no key

`_create_rejected_recalculation` writes `step: "request"` entries outside `_record_failure` and keeps no `calculation_key` on purpose. Those runs fail on experiment age, not on the metric, so the classifier ignores them.

### API docs

The `metric_errors` `help_text` lists the new field and says it can be null or absent.

- `products/experiments/backend/presentation/serializers.py`
- `products/experiments/frontend/generated/api.schemas.ts` (generated)
- `services/mcp/src/api/generated.ts` (generated)

## Bug description

When a user asks Max AI to edit values inside a Hog function's filter configuration, the agent occasionally edits the **field description / UI label** instead of the actual field value. The result is that the Hog function configuration UI gets visibly mutated (labels rewritten) rather than the underlying filter values being changed.

The issue is inconsistent — in the same trace, GPT-4.1 produced the bug while Sonnet 4.5 handled the same request correctly on a follow-up call.

The `create_hog_function_filters` tool is part of a legacy agent implementation that still runs on GPT-4.1, and the subagent response does not use structured output, so the model has room to write the value into the wrong field of the schema.

## How to reproduce

1. Open a Hog function (destination or source) configuration.
2. Ask Max AI to edit a filter value (e.g. "change the filter value for X to Y").
3. Observe that, intermittently, the field's label/description is rewritten instead of the value.

Note: not 100% reproducible — depends on which model the subagent ends up running and how it interprets the schema on a given call.

## Additional context

From: https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/47775 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/57261)

Proper fix is part of the broader migration of legacy agent tools to MCP tools with structured output enforced. Short-term mitigations worth considering if the migration takes a while: enforce structured output on the existing GPT-4.1 subagent call, or add input validation that rejects writes to label/description fields.

hits.body:
## Context

PR #59070 wires `@typescript/native-preview` (tsgo) as a shadow type-checker alongside `tsc`, with `typescript@6.0.3` retained via `pnpm.overrides` for every tool that consumes the programmatic Compiler API. The largest such consumer is **kea-typegen**, which generates the `*Type.ts` files we depend on for kea logic typing.

This issue tracks the upstream gaps that block migrating kea-typegen (and the rest of our programmatic-API consumers) off `typescript@6`.

## Why this is blocked today

`@typescript/native-preview` currently ships **zero JS-callable code** — `package.json` has no `main`/`types`, only a `bin` entry that subprocesses the native binary. The "Corsa" IPC API exists in [microsoft/typescript-go](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go) source (`_packages/native-preview/src/api/sync/api.ts`) but is not bundled to npm.

Even once Corsa ships, kea-typegen's hot path needs APIs that aren't designed yet:

- `ts.factory.*` — kea-typegen **constructs** `*Type.ts` AST nodes
- `ts.createPrinter` — serializes constructed nodes to text
- `checker.typeToTypeNode` — converts a resolved `Type` back into a printable `TypeNode`
- `checker.typeToString`, `checker.getExportsOfModule` — listed as gaps, no open PR

There is also an architectural mismatch: kea-typegen holds live `ts.Node` references across many checker calls and mutates the AST in-memory. Corsa is IPC: opaque handles, serialize/deserialize per call. No in-process AST graph.

## Upstream issues to watch

- microsoft/TypeScript#63771 — _Transformer Plugin or Compiler API_ (open, no timeline)
- microsoft/TypeScript#63800 — _API usage patterns for complex editor extensions_ (Corsa design)
- microsoft/typescript-go#3610 — _API: additional Checker methods for transpiler consumers_ (subset of methods landing incrementally; `typeToTypeNode` is a listed gap)
- microsoft/typescript-go#3616 — _API emit support_ (open PR, not merged)

## Definition of done

- [ ] `@typescript/native-preview` (or a Microsoft-blessed sibling package) ships a JS-importable module with: `ts.factory`, `ts.createPrinter`, `ts.createSourceFile`, `Program.getTypeChecker()`, `TypeChecker.typeToTypeNode`, `TypeChecker.typeToString`, `TypeChecker.getExportsOfModule`, and the ~40 `ts.is*` AST predicates kea-typegen relies on.
- [ ] kea-typegen's `peerDependencies.typescript` is bumped to support the 7.x line.
- [ ] We drop the `pnpm.overrides.typescript = "6.0.3"` pin and rely on the catalog entry only.
- [ ] Same applies to other API consumers we currently pin: `ts-jest`, `ts-node`, `ts-json-schema-generator`, `@parcel/packager-ts`, `@parcel/transformer-typescript-types`.

## Realistic timeline

TS 7.1 at the earliest, more likely 7.2+. Microsoft has not committed to a date. No engineering action is feasible until upstream lands the APIs above — this is a watch-list, not a backlog item.

## Related

- PR #59070 — adds the tsgo shadow CI step and the coexistence setup this issue depends on.

## Bug description

Native canvas replay inside a cross-origin iframe can disappear after a seek even though the recorded canvas frame decodes successfully. A separate sizing defect can apply an ancestor transform twice, shrinking the artwork. This affects the hosted CanvasReplayerPlugin path; the bundled rrweb replayer by itself did not reproduce the same behavior.

Environment: PostHog Cloud US; observed player build `13ff07ce8b6b64d23e21826c8fd2e4f569c28a98`; recording SDK `posthog-js 1.433.1`; Fabric `6.7.1`; Chromium. The problematic reuse and bounding-rectangle sizing are also present in current master at report time.

## Runnable synthetic reproducer and candidate patch

[Self-contained reproducer, original plugin, fixed candidate, patch and upstream license](https://gist.github.com/geoff-wp/a278b5618c5897def02b96c8f7c49105).

The fixture needs no private repository, credentials, real PostHog project, or customer recordings. It intercepts all browser network requests and records real Fabric canvas frames in a synthetic cross-origin child, forwarding them into the parent's session. It then plays those recorded events through the pinned hosted canvas plugin with `UNSAFE_replayCanvas: false` and `useVirtualDom: false`.

```sh
git clone https://gist.github.com/a278b5618c5897def02b96c8f7c49105.git canvas-replay-repro
cd canvas-replay-repro
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
cp canvas-plugin.original.ts canvas-plugin.ts
npm test
# Reproduced failure: native playback image absent after seeking.
cp canvas-plugin.fixed.ts canvas-plugin.ts
npm test
# Pass: genuine recorded artwork at its recorded size after forward/backward seeks.
```

Both modes were exercised before submission. A wider private synthetic fixture with the candidate passed eight checks including cross-origin native pixels, seeking, reload, large idle artwork, and deliberately removed frames remaining blank. The public fixture isolates the playback failure.

## Cause 1: cached element belongs to the old iframe document

[onBuild](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/13ff07ce8b6b64d23e21826c8fd2e4f569c28a98/common/replay-shared/src/canvas/canvas-plugin.ts#L398) reuses `containers.get(id)` when rrweb rebuilds a canvas with the same node ID. During an iframe seek, that cached image belongs to the discarded iframe document. The reconstructed canvas belongs to the new document. In the reproducer, canvas decoding and toBlob succeed, but loading the old-document image never completes and the new iframe retains an unrendered canvas.

The candidate only reuses the cached image when its `ownerDocument` matches `canvasElement.ownerDocument`; otherwise it creates a new image in the rebuilt document. This preserves the scriptless sandbox and the existing native-frame playback mechanism.

## Cause 2: transformed bounds become untransformed CSS dimensions

[Canvas dimension calculation](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/13ff07ce8b6b64d23e21826c8fd2e4f569c28a98/common/replay-shared/src/canvas/canvas-plugin.ts#L271) uses `getBoundingClientRect()` and assigns that size to the playback image, which remains inside the same transformed ancestor. A 220px canvas inside `transform: scale(0.49)` should display at 107.8px; we observed 52.82px. Once the original canvas is detached, fallback dimensions can differ again, making this intermittent.

The candidate uses recorded logical CSS dimensions and retains inline dimensions after detachment, instead of using transformed screen bounds.

## Patch and review limits

[Unified patch](https://gist.github.com/geoff-wp/a278b5618c5897def02b96c8f7c49105#file-native-canvas-player-patch) is a proposed upstream correction, not a hosted deployment. Please review broader responsive sizing, percentage/calc dimensions and overlapping-seek behavior and run the upstream suite. No substitute screenshots or artwork are introduced. Missing recorded frames must remain missing.

Private replay links and customer artwork are intentionally omitted from this public report. The fully synthetic reproducer demonstrates the defect without them.

## Problem

- The weekly deletes job can stall merges across the whole of `sharded_events_json` while it deletes.
- That table takes deletes as patch parts, in one `DELETE` whose `dictHas(...)` predicate cannot be pruned to a partition.
- ClickHouse then holds a block number open in every partition until the statement finishes, and merges cannot span it. #114370 fixed the same problem for the person_id squash.
- A team deletion is worse as patch parts: it stores one patch row for every row the team has, until merges or `APPLY PATCHES` fold them in.

## Changes

- Person, event and adhoc deletions on `sharded_events_json` run as one `DELETE ... IN PARTITION` per partition, on only the shards that hold it.
- Those statements also require `team_id` to be in the dictionaries' team sets, so the read skips teams with nothing to delete.
- Team deletions on `sharded_events_json` run as a classic mutation (`lightweight_delete_mode = 'alter_update'`). The op creates it only when a team deletion is pending.
- `sharded_events` and `flag_evaluations` keep one mutation each. Their predicate text is byte-for-byte unchanged, so mutation reuse and the post-sweep count still match.
- Mechanical: the partition lookup moves from `person_overrides.py` to `deletion_targets.shards_by_partition`, shared by the squash and the deletes.
- Not changed: `data_deletion_requests` and `cleanup_old_events_by_partition`.

> [!NOTE]
> The subqueries need `allow_nondeterministic_mutations = 1` on replicated tables. The `dagster` user already runs with that setting.

## How did you test this code?

- Not run locally: the ClickHouse-backed tests need the dev stack, which was not started. CI runs them.
- Not verified: that ClickHouse accepts `DELETE ... IN PARTITION` as a lightweight update. `lightweight_update_force` makes the statement fail rather than fall back to a mutation, so the new test would show it.

**Test rationale:** `test_events_json_deletes_reach_every_partition_for_person_and_team_deletions` puts a pending person deletion and a pending team deletion across two partitions of `sharded_events_json`. It asserts only the unrelated row survives. It fails if the loop misses a partition, or if the team arm is left out of both paths. The existing job tests only write to `sharded_events`, so none covered these paths with data.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)

## Bug Description

When a user asks PostHog AI a complex question with a large dashboard attached as context, the agent can fail silently with no response shown in the chat.

The Temporal activity that runs the chat agent has a 5 minute (300 s) heartbeat timeout, and heartbeats are only emitted when the LangGraph stream yields a chunk. If the root node runs for longer than 300 s without yielding anything, no heartbeat fires and Temporal cancels the activity with asyncio.CancelledError at ~300 s. No FailureMessage is yielded. The user sees no response and no error.

This is amplified by the activity's retry policy (maximum_attempts=3). Each retry replays from the checkpointer, so the input state grows on every attempt. In one observed trace the state grew from ~95 KB to ~285 KB across three retries, all of which were cancelled at exactly 309 s. In a separate trace from the same user the first attempt was cancelled the same way but a later retry succeeded, so the failure is intermittent. (links to traces in ticket below)

## How to reproduce

1. Open PostHog AI in a project that has at least one moderately large dashboard (around 20+ insights).
2. Attach the dashboard as context and send a multi-part analytical question (several distinct asks combined into one prompt) in the default product_analytics agent mode.
3. Wait. After about 5 minutes the agent will be silently cancelled, with no reply or error shown in the chat.

## Additional context

Raised in: https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/58027 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/59923)

I might raise a PR just to stop the silent failure as well, will attach here once it's done.

hits.body:
## Problem

A model is suspended after 5 materialization failures in a row. A ClickHouse node dropping its connection mid-query counts as one of those failures, even though the model's SQL did nothing wrong.

This error is `Code: 32 ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF … While executing Remote`. It shows up when a remote node restarts or loses its connection. It can outlast the activity's 3 retries (10s, then 20s backoff) and fail the job. If a node stays unhealthy across several scheduled runs, healthy models get suspended.

## Changes

- `Code: 32. ` is added to `EXTERNALLY_ABORTED_MARKERS`, so the failure counter treats this error like `Code: 202` (too many simultaneous queries): it ends the streak instead of adding to it.
- The trailing period keeps codes 320–329 out of the match.
- The job is still recorded as `Failed`, and the existing retries are unchanged. Only suspension counting is affected.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** adds the real error shape as a case to the parameterized `test_externally_aborted_failures_do_not_suspend`. Without the marker, that case would suspend the node after 5 failures. It is the existing test for this exact classification, so no new test is needed.

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both files. The pre-push preflight passed.
- The pytest suite was not run locally (the worktree venv had no dev dependencies). CI runs it.
- The matching was checked against a code 32 error, a code 321 error and a code 241 error: only code 32 is treated as external.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5

- Came from diagnosing an intermittent materialization failure. The run's logs showed all 3 activity retries used up while one ClickHouse node was unhealthy.
- No duplicate: an open-PR search for this error and for `EXTERNALLY_ABORTED_MARKERS` found only unrelated marker changes.
- Error strings in the test are invented (`example.com` host).

## Problem

- The workflow event matcher puts far more load on the job database than any other workflow service.
- Most lookups find a waiting run or goal, but the event matches neither, so nothing happens.

## Changes

- The matcher checks each event against its team's waits and goals in memory, and looks up only events that pass.
- It uses the same filter evaluation that decides a wake or conversion, so a skipped event could never have matched.
- `CDP_HOGFLOW_SUBSCRIPTION_MATCHER_FILTER_FIRST`: `off` (default), `shadow` (counts what `on` would skip), `on`.
- The check stops after 50 ms per batch and skips flows whose filters use randomness. Those events go to the normal lookup.
- `cdp_hogflow_matcher_filter_first_missed` must stay at zero in shadow before turning it on.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Event batch]:::y --> B[Look up waiting runs and goals]:::r --> C[Evaluate filters]:::b
  classDef y fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef r fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef b fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Event batch]:::y --> F[Evaluate filters in memory]:::b -->|passes| B[Look up waiting runs and goals]:::r --> C[Evaluate filters]:::b
  F -->|fails| X[Skip]:::g
  classDef y fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef r fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef b fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef g fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

## How did you test this code?

Real matcher, Kafka and Postgres. Four flows (filtered wait, named wait, property goal, event goal), 40 people, 2,000 non-matching events plus one match per flow:

| Mode | Batches | Run lookups | Goal lookups | Wakes / conversions | Missed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `off` | 101 | 101 | 101 | 2 / 2 | 0 |
| `shadow` | 102 | 102 | 102 | 2 / 2 | 0 |
| `on` | 101 | 1 | 1 | 2 / 2 | 0 |

- Same four people woken or converted in every mode.
- The goal check stays broad after a flow edit, through the existing pinned-goal safety.

**Test rationale:** The unit suite runs with the check `on`, so existing wake cases catch over-skipping (27 fail if it skips everything). Cases for plain filters, random filters and an over-budget check each fail when their guard is removed.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

- None.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/writing-plainly`

**Security review:** not needed

<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** Shadow by default so production shows the skip rate and a zero miss count before `on`.
- **Follow-ups:** Keep the distinct pinned goals in a small table written with each watcher, so the goal check stays exact after flow edits and the full-table refresh can go.
- **Read closely:** `checkFilters`, `couldMoveRun` and `couldConvert` in the matcher consumer.

## Problem

- Google Play Console users get only 180 days of vitals history on a first sync, so they cannot move their older crash and ANR data from another tool into PostHog.
- `METRIC_SET_HISTORY_DAYS = 180` fixes the first-sync start date for all 22 vitals rate tables and their breakdowns.
- Play does not document how far back vitals go. The code comments disagree ("roughly a year" in one place, "years" in another).

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0eb8a-f9be-73de-b5aa-e1b2c4f60f49 -->
## Origin

- Conversations: [ticket](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a0eb4e-c4de-0000-8e8c-b787d1f1ce44)
- First signal: 2026-09-29
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0eb8a-f9be-73de-b5aa-e1b2c4f60f49)
- Likely cause: [`a54d80ac`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/a54d80ac9d26d30c0ec295ae2c28d05b7a24cb6d)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P3 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0eb8a-f9be-73de-b5aa-e1b2c4f60f49 -->

## Changes

- New connections (and full resyncs) backfill vitals rate tables up to 730 days back:

```diff
-METRIC_SET_HISTORY_DAYS = 180
+METRIC_SET_HISTORY_DAYS = 730
+METRIC_SET_PROVEN_HISTORY_DAYS = 180
```

- A metric window that starts more than 180 days back and gets a `400` from Play is skipped. The sync continues with the next window.
  - Why: the source classifies a `400` as permanent. Without the guard, an unknown retention limit could fail every first sync.
  - A `400` for a window inside the old 180-day depth still fails the sync, same as before.
- `error_counts`, `error_reports` and `error_issues` keep the 30-day window. Play keeps only about 56 days of error data and rejects older starts.

> [!WARNING]
> - Existing schemas do not backfill on their own. The start date is the stored watermark, so they need a full resync to get the older data.
> - A first sync of the default tables now reads up to about 4x more days, so it takes longer and syncs more billed rows.
> - At the retention edge, a rejected 30-day window loses the oldest days Play still keeps inside that window.

Out of scope: Play bulk reports (installs, ratings, reviews) from the `pubsite_prod_*` GCS bucket. That is a separate schema family.

## How did you test this code?

- `hogli test products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/google_play_console/tests`: passes.
- New parameterized test `test_metric_set_skips_a_rejected_window_only_beyond_the_proven_history`:
  - Catches removal of the guard, which would let a deep rejected window fail the whole first sync.
  - Catches a guard that is too wide and hides real `400`s inside the proven depth.
- Updated the expected crash_rate first-sync start in `test_first_sync_history_window_depends_on_the_metric_set`.
- Not tested: a real query against the Play Developer Reporting API. The actual retained depth for vitals is unverified. The guard makes that safe, but the depth a user gets depends on Play.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None. No doc in this repo covers the history depth of this source.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop (Claude Code), claude-opus-5-5

- Started from an inbox report about a limited Google Play first-sync history.
- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.

- Public artifact: the diff and this description hold no customer material.

**Context:** spans from TanStack AI's `otelMiddleware` (`@tanstack/ai` 1.8.0), file read on `master` 2026-11-21.

`nodejs/src/ingestion/pipelines/ai/otel/attribute-mapping.ts` maps the `gen_ai.usage.*` token attributes, but it has no entry for `gen_ai.usage.cost`. ## Problem

- Trace judges on agent runs answer N/A because they never see the task prompt ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C087XQ7K9K7/p1795011878017719)).
- Each step resends the conversation, so the transcript overflows its 150,000-character budget.
- Every long message then keeps 1,000 characters, prompt included, with no sign on the result.

## Changes

- Judges see repeated messages once, as `[1-17] Same as messages 1-17 of the previous generation's input above`. Only equal messages collapse.
- The trace budget rises to 300,000 characters, falling back to 150,000 when the judge's context window rejects it.
- Results from a cut transcript set `$ai_evaluation_input_truncated: true`.
- Traces still over 150,000 characters after the collapse send up to twice the input tokens to the customer's judge key.

The judge call gains one fallback:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Render at 150k]:::phYellow --> B{{Judge}}:::phBlue --> C[Verdict or skip]:::phGray
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Render at 300k]:::phYellow --> B{{Judge}}:::phBlue
  B -->|context window exceeded| D[Render at 150k]:::phYellow --> E{{Judge}}:::phBlue --> C[Verdict or skip]:::phGray
  B --> C
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:**

- New tests fail if the collapse is off, a changed message collapses, or the context-window fallback retries wrongly.
- Not checked: a real judge on a real agent trace.

<details>

hits.body:
## Problem

`signals-scout-billing` (#137999) watches an organization's own PostHog bill. It finds a usage step or a spend ramp, prices it, and hands the root cause to another scout. It makes little use of the official skills that already cover the same ground.

- **It names one official skill.** `SKILL.md` ends with a pointer to `posthog:understanding-billing-usage`, to read "when a drilldown needs more than the routing table". Nothing else is named.
- **It does not know `posthog:managing-self-driving-spend`** (#124825). For Self-driving credits, the handoff table in `references/usage-types.md` says only "The Signals inbox — which includes this scout. Surface the loop once, plainly". Every other meter gets an owner and a drilldown. This one gets neither, so a report on Self-driving spend states the projection and stops. The spend skill already breaks that spend down by signal source, scout and day, and ranks the controls that lower it.
- **It reaches the AI cost skills only by accident.** `posthog:exploring-llm-costs` and `posthog:analyzing-expensive-users` are named in `understanding-billing-usage/references/usage-type-routing.md`, not in the scout. The scout's own row for PostHog AI credits says no sibling scout owns the meter and names no skill.
- **It carries a second copy of the usage type table.** `signals-scout-billing/references/usage-types.md` has a vocabulary table and a handoff table keyed by usage type. `understanding-billing-usage/references/usage-type-routing.md` has a routing table keyed by the same usage types, with the follow-up skill for each. A new meter must be added in both, and the two can drift.
- **It has no discovery step.** The skill does not tell the scout to look for a matching skill before it writes its own drilldown.

`signals-scout-ai-observability` already shows the pattern this scout lacks: a "Deep-dive skills (baked into the sandbox ...)" line and a lens table that names the skill to open for each lens.

## Goal

The billing scout owns only what is specific to a scheduled billing watcher. For everything else it reads the official skill and follows it. When an official skill already answers the question a finding raises, the scout acts as a thin wrapper: it supplies the trigger, the pricing and the report, and the skill supplies the investigation.

One fact lives in one place. A change to a usage type, a spend control or a cost query is made once.

## Proposal

### 1. Decide what the scout owns

Keep in the scout:

- Access gates and the no-access and volume-only modes.
- Cadence, cursor and scratchpad memory rules, including what must never be stored there.
- The two lanes: step detection and the trajectory read.
- The pricing mechanics: period boundaries, the difference-of-two-prices rule, which projection field to quote, and "may, not will" for limits.
- Report framing and dedupe.

Move out, or replace with a pointer:

- The usage type vocabulary and the per-meter follow-up, where `understanding-billing-usage` already has it.
- Any drilldown query an official skill already carries.

### 2. Add a skill map to the handoff table

Give each row in "Where each usage type hands off" a third column: the official skill to read when the scout needs more than the one-line hint. Start from the list in `usage-type-routing.md`. At least:

| Meter group | Skill to lean on |
| --- | --- |
| Self-driving credits | `posthog:managing-self-driving-spend` |
| PostHog AI credits, AI observability events | `posthog:exploring-llm-costs`, `posthog:analyzing-expensive-users` |
| Events, identified events | `posthog:investigate-metric`, `posthog:exploring-autocapture-events` |
| Warehouse synced rows | `posthog:auditing-warehouse-source-health`, `posthog:tuning-incremental-sync-config` |
| Logs and traces | `posthog:investigating-logs` |
| Replay Vision credits | `posthog:exploring-replay-vision-observations` |
| Anything else | `posthog:understanding-billing-usage` and its routing reference |

The scout still hands the root cause to the owning scout. The skill is for the cases where no scout owns the meter, or where a short read makes the report useful on its own.

### 3. Wrapper mode for meters with no owning scout

Self-driving credits and PostHog AI credits have no sibling scout. For these, the scout runs the read-only part of the matching skill and puts the result in the report:

- Self-driving credits: the breakdown by signal source, scout and day from `managing-self-driving-spend`, and its ranked list of controls as recommendations.
- PostHog AI credits: the breakdown from `exploring-llm-costs`.

The scout never applies a control. `managing-self-driving-spend` changes settings only after a person confirms each one, and a scheduled run has no person to ask. The report lists the recommended changes and names the skill, so the reader can run it and confirm.

### 4. Remove the duplicate table

Pick one source for the usage type list. Two options:

- **A.** `understanding-billing-usage/references/usage-type-routing.md` is the source. The scout's reference keeps only the billing-service field mechanics and a short table of scout handoffs, and tells the scout to read the routing reference for the rest.
- **B.** Keep both files, and add a test that fails when the set of usage types differs between them.

A is the better end state. B is a cheap guard if A needs a harness change first.

### 5. Add the reverse links

- `understanding-billing-usage/references/usage-type-routing.md` names `posthog:managing-self-driving-spend` for the Self-driving meters. Today it sends the reader to `posthog:inbox-exploration` only.
- `managing-self-driving-spend` says the billing scout can raise the spend finding that leads to it.

### 6. Add a discovery rule

One line in the scout's "Seams" section: before the scout writes a drilldown that is not in its own skill, it checks for an official skill that covers it and reads that skill.

## Open questions

- Which official skills are available inside a scout run today, and by what route (baked into the sandbox, or loaded through the MCP)? The scout's skill says `understanding-billing-usage` is baked in. This needs a check for the others before the map is written.
- Does a scout run have the scopes for `inbox-usage-get` and `billing-limits-get`, which `managing-self-driving-spend` starts from? If not, wrapper mode for Self-driving credits needs a grant first.
- `inbox-usage-get` reports recorded usage, which includes exempt work and is not an invoice. The report must not mix that number with the billed figure from the billing tools. Which one leads?
- Does every pointer need a fallback line for a team that has edited or removed its copy of the scout skill, or for a run where the skill is not available?
- Should the same audit run across the other canonical scouts? #103304 refreshed them against harness capabilities, not against the official skills.

## Acceptance

- The billing scout's skill names every official skill it depends on, per meter group.
- A finding on Self-driving credits produces a report with a breakdown by source and scout, and a list of recommended controls.
- The usage type list has one source, or a test that keeps two in step.
- No drilldown query in the scout repeats one in an official skill.

Related: #137999 (the scout), #124825 (the spend skill), #103304 (canonical scout refresh).

## Problem

After #141562 nothing calls `services/llm-gateway`, but the service, its CI and deploy workflows, its dev tooling and three migration skills are still in the repo and still cost CI time.

## Changes

Deletes the legacy Python gateway and its tooling, about 34k lines.

- Deletes `services/llm-gateway/`, its CI and CD workflows, `bin/start-llm-gateway`, the mprocs entry and `hogli start:llm:gateway`.
- **Dev intents:** `llm_gateway` leaves the five AI intents. Local runs that need inference opt in to the **`ai_gateway`** capability, which needs a sibling `ai-gateway` clone.
- Removes the legacy quota cache (`invalidate_llm_gateway_quota_cache`, `LLM_GATEWAY_REDIS_URL`) and the desktop test that compared chip prices with the deleted service's rate table.
- Replaces the three migration skills with a short `/calling-the-ai-gateway` skill.
- **Kept:** the `llm_gateway:read` scope and the team policy and quota projections, which Go reads, and `LLM_GATEWAY_URL` as a reserved sandbox key.

**Before merge:** an admin removes the required check "LLM Services Tests Pass" from the `master` ruleset (id 6958621).

**After deploy:**
- Remove the `llm-gateway` release, ingress and alerts from `PostHog/charts`.
- Delete the `llm-gateway` images in ECR, GHCR and DockerHub, and the `CLOUDFLARE_LLM_GATEWAY_TOKEN` repo secret.

## How did you test this code?

`hogli lint:workflows`, `hogli lint:skills`, `hogli build:projections --check`, the repo invariants, the CI script tests, the hogli devenv and test-runner tests, and the touched tasks, gateway client and organization tests pass.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

Internal docs and agent skills updated alongside the deletion.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5. Requires human review.

hits.body:
## Context

**Goal:** improve the default prompt, system prompt and detector behaviour that every user gets out of the box. These are changes to the defaults, not tuning for particular alerts.

The sampled alerts nearly all carry hand-written author instructions. Most users will not write any, so judge each change on alerts without instructions too.

We reviewed a week of AI detector checks on internal alerts before the wider rollout of `alerts-llm-detector`. Almost all checks are hourly, all of them run on one model, and none errored. Verdicts are mostly sensible. The items below are small, independent changes. Each one can ship as its own PR.

## 1. Write values as plain decimals

**Problem:** `prompt.py` formats values with `:g`. A count of 1,175,594 reaches the model as `1.17559e+06`, which drops the low digits and makes neighbouring values look identical.

**Change:** add a formatter that writes integers in full, rounds other values of 1 or more to two decimals, and writes small values positionally. Bump `PROMPT_REVISION`.

## 2. Bound the earlier-alerts block

**Problem:** the block lists one rationale for every flagged point in the window, so it grows with the fire rate. On the noisiest alerts it is about three quarters of the prompt. That raises cost, and a wall of earlier "anomaly" reasons pushes the model to flag again.

Two smaller defects in the same block:
- The 200-character cut lands mid-word ("so the elev").
- Old rationales quote values from the time of that check. Those values often no longer match the table, because buckets get revised.

**Change:**
- Keep the most recent N rationales (for example 5). Add a one-line summary such as "this alert flagged 42 of the 168 points in the window, most recently at <date>".
- Cut at a sentence or word boundary.
- Label the quoted numbers as the values at the time of that check.

## 3. Make sustained level shifts consistent

**Problem:** when a series moves to a new level and stays there for days, verdicts flip between `level_shift` and `none` from one hour to the next on the same state. One alert fired on most checks for days on a shift that started early in the window. A similar alert stopped firing on its shift after about a day.

The comparable-points line adds to this. With a 7-day hourly window, the "same weekday" value is the one point from before the shift, so it always reads as a 2-3x jump.

**Change:** decide what a check means during an ongoing shift, then say it in the prompt. Either it means "still anomalous", so it keeps firing and the alert state machine handles renotification, or it means "new or worsening", so it fires once and then only on a further move. Pass the alert's current firing streak as data. Add an eval case for a shift that holds for 1, 3 and 5 days.

## 4. Revisit the hourly lookback

**Problem:** `llm_detector_lookback("hour")` covers 7 days, so "same hour on the same weekday in earlier weeks" has at most one value. Weekly seasonality cannot be learned from that.

**Change:** try 14 days for hourly series. Item 2 frees enough tokens to pay for the extra rows. Compare verdicts on a labelled set before and after.

## 5. Skip re-checks of an unchanged point

**Problem:** about three quarters of hourly points are judged twice. The likely cause is a check cadence shorter than the bucket, but that is not confirmed. The second call sees the same series, give or take a few late events, and disagrees with the first call about 2% of the time. That costs twice as much and can flap.

**Change:** reuse the last verdict when the current point's date matches and the values in the window are within a small tolerance of the last check. The memo key covers `evaluation_id` today, so this needs a second, point-keyed lookup. Cost story: this removes roughly half of the model calls for hourly alerts.

## 6. Escape metadata without quote entities

**Problem:** `html.escape` runs with its default `quote=True`, so HogQL filters in the metric description reach the model as `"` and `'`.

**Change:** use `escape(..., quote=False)`. Only `<`, `>` and `&` matter for keeping data inside its tags. The existing tag-escape test still covers the injection case.

## Out of scope / later

- Measure whether the chart image changes verdicts. It is attached to every call. An ablation on a labelled set would tell us whether it pays for its tokens.

## Summary
`LLM Analytics` trace-level `totalCost` currently appears to exclude `$ai_total_cost_usd` from `$ai_span` events.

In our traces, custom operations (for example reranking) are captured as `$ai_span` with valid `$ai_total_cost_usd`. The span-level UI shows the cost, but the trace header/table `totalCost` does not include it.

## Expected behavior
Trace/session `totalCost` should include all AI event costs that belong to the trace, including `$ai_span` events with `$ai_total_cost_usd`.

## Actual behavior
Trace/session `totalCost` includes only `$ai_generation` and `$ai_embedding` costs.

## Evidence in code
Current trace queries sum cost only for `event IN ('$ai_generation', '$ai_embedding')`:

- `posthog/hogql_queries/ai/trace_query_runner.py`
- `posthog/hogql_queries/ai/traces_query_runner.py`

Both queries compute `total_cost` using:

```sql
sumIf(toFloat(properties.$ai_total_cost_usd), event IN ('$ai_generation', '$ai_embedding'))
```

## Repro
1. Send one `$ai_generation` event with `$ai_total_cost_usd = 0.058`
2. Send one `$ai_span` event in the same trace with `$ai_total_cost_usd = 0.004`
3. Open trace in LLM Analytics

Result:
- Span shows `0.004` correctly
- Trace `totalCost` shows `0.058` instead of `0.062`

## Notes
This makes trace/session totals under-report costs whenever teams put billable work on `$ai_span` (rerank/search/tool/API operations) instead of `$ai_generation`/`$ai_embedding`.

If this is intentional, could docs explicitly state that trace/session totals only aggregate generation/embedding events?

## Problem

- An organization with a managed warehouse has no place in PostHog to see usage and spend, find an expensive query, see what is stored, manage logins or get connection details.
- This is layer 4 of 5. It adds the pages on top of the API in the two layers below.

## Changes

With `managed-warehouse-console` on, the Warehouse menu gains a Manage group:

| Page | What a person can do |
| --- | --- |
| Usage | See compute scanned, storage and estimated spend for the month, split by source, login or project. Set a budget and a scan limit. |
| Queries | See running queries and cancel one. Search history by status, login and source. A Performance tab shows rate, errors, duration and load. |
| Storage | See each table's size, rows and files. A Data readiness tab shows event backfill and imported sources. |
| Access | Create, disable and delete project logins, and reset the root password. |
| Connect | Copy host, port, catalog and schema, plus snippets for common clients. |
| Settings | See warehouse status and provision, onboard or deprovision. |

- Data ops stops being a page while the flag is on. `/data-ops` redirects to the page that now holds each of its tabs.
- With the flag off, nothing changes, and Data ops works as before.
- The pages use quill and share one set of section, stat, meter, badge and table components.
### Screenshots

Local app, demo project, fake control plane. These are new pages, so there is no before. The captures come from the top of the stack: the sidebar on the left is added in #141427, and this layer shows the same pages under a dropdown menu.

> [!WARNING]
> The pages depend on control plane routes that are not deployed. With the flag on in production today they show an error state.

## How did you test this code?

- Frontend typecheck reports 0 errors. 123 Jest suites (1,805 tests) pass locally, including the new logic and format suites.
- Kea typegen, the products build and the app URL manifest show no diff.
- The pages were rendered in the local app against a fake control plane at several widths.
- Not checked: any page against real warehouse data, and the 403 state, which shows a generic error message.

**Test rationale:** The new cases pin number, byte and duration formatting, the mapping of raw logins to labels, paging in query history, and the `/data-ops` redirects for each flag state.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None. The console sits behind `managed-warehouse-console`, and no existing doc covers it.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, claude-fable-5-2 (review and orchestration) with Claude Sonnet 5.5 subagents (implementation)

**Skills:** `/writing-ui-components`, `/writing-kea-logics`, `/adopting-generated-api-types`, `/working-with-charts`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-tests`, `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** not needed. The pages only call the endpoints reviewed in the layers below.

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** The console was first pushed as one change inside #113361, then split into this stack so each layer is reviewable alone.
- **Decisions:** Prices are constants in the backend and every amount is labeled as an estimate, because billing does not read them yet.
- **Follow-ups:** Attach screenshots. Add a specific message for the 403 state. Decide if Usage should be named Spend.
- **Read closely:** `DataOpsEntryScene.tsx` for the redirects, and `todayWarehouseItems.ts` for the menu.
- CodeRabbit: the local review was skipped. The CLI was signed out and setup was declined, so the bot review on this PR is the first pass.

## Problem

- An agent that follows the `exploring-llm-costs` skill to its most expensive trace can hit a dead end ([inbox report](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/15db89eb-5388-4b86-ada6-269bc4d6efa8)).
- `query-llm-trace` timed out on a trace with over 100,000 generations, and the skill gave no other way to continue.
- On smaller traces the tool returns only the earliest events, so a cost sum from them is too low.

## Changes

- The "Cost by trace" recipe now breaks down the cost of any trace in SQL, and keeps `query-llm-trace` for reading specific calls.
- The single-trace workflow and step 5 of `analyzing-expensive-users` point to that SQL when the tool fails.

## How did you test this code?

- Both new queries completed during review on a trace with over 100,000 LLM calls.
- Not run locally: `hogli build:skills`. CI builds the skills.

**Test rationale:** Docs-only change to two skills.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, claude-fable-5-2

**Skills:** `/writing-skills`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code, with the PostHog MCP `execute-sql` tool for the query check.
- **Decisions:** The first version gated the tool on a 1,000-call cutoff. Review measured that the response holds about 40 events at any trace size, so the cutoff went and SQL became the default for cost.
- **Decisions:** The fallback queries read `events` with the same time filter as the query that found the trace, so their totals match the row that led to them.
- **Follow-ups:** Cap events or skip heavy columns on the server, so `query-llm-trace` does not fail on very large traces.
- **Read closely:** `references/breakdown-patterns.md`, section "Cost by trace".
- **Public artifact:** The diff carries no trace ID, cost, or other project data.

</details>

## Problem

Teams comparing offline experiments have to weigh several item-level pass rates themselves to decide which run performed better.

## Changes

- Define one experiment score from item scorer statistics. For example, weight accuracy at 60%, grounded answers at 25%, and resolved requests at 15%.
- Assign a formula to a suite in one environment. Each new run pins its scorer version, so later edits preserve historical results.
- Choose how each input handles scorer upgrades. By default, a run that mixes versions shows which input prevented scoring. Pooling uses individual scored items.
- Preview a formula on an existing run, then follow scores in experiment details, recent experiments, and scorer history.

<details>
<summary>Experiment score and recent runs</summary>

![Experiment score of 91.67 out of 100 above the item scores](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/e768c94f4ecd2cc8dca7ddb00a662acd13b1ed30/2026/11/8f6aa4c3-b106-4d85-8e54-0e7371f88640.png)

![Recent experiments with overall scores and a reason for an unscored run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/e768c94f4ecd2cc8dca7ddb00a662acd13b1ed30/2026/11/77c30093-c832-473d-bb09-9e828103d73c.png)

## How did you test this code?
