## Problem

Teams that run their tagging through Google Tag Manager have no way to bring that configuration into the PostHog data warehouse, so container and tag setup stays invisible to queries and monitoring. Requested by a customer as a P1.

Closes #79110

## Changes

- Adds a Google Tag Manager source syncing seven tables: accounts, containers, workspaces, tags, triggers, variables, and container versions (including archived versions).
- Auth is Google OAuth through a new `google-tag-manager` integration kind requesting the `tagmanager.readonly` scope. The kind fails closed with "Google Tag Manager app not configured" until the app credentials deploy, matching the other Google source kinds.
- Every table is full refresh: the GTM API has no modification-time filter, and the tables hold small configuration objects. The primary key is the resource `path`, the only identifier unique across parents (bare ids like `tagId` repeat per workspace).
- The GTM API allows 0.25 QPS and 10,000 requests per day, project-wide, shared by every connection through one OAuth app. The client spaces requests 4.5 s apart, honors `Retry-After`, and separates quota 403s (retried, then handed to Temporal as retryable) from permission 403s (fail the sync with a reconnect prompt).
- An optional account IDs field limits syncing to named GTM accounts; `validate_credentials` rejects IDs the connected user cannot access.
- Canonical table and column descriptions come from the GTM API reference, so semantic enrichment skips the LLM for this source.
- New Django migrations only re-list enum choices; both are SQL no-ops (verified with `sqlmigrate`).
- No screenshot: the new wizard tile and connect form render entirely from the registered source config and an icon already in the repo; no UI component changed.

> [!NOTE]
> Before OAuth connect works in production, ops needs to register the Google OAuth client (scope `tagmanager.readonly`, standard redirect URIs) and deploy `GOOGLE_TAG_MANAGER_APP_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_TAG_MANAGER_APP_CLIENT_SECRET` via charts to the web app and the data-warehouse Temporal worker, per the OAuth app deployment reference. Given the shared 0.25 QPS project quota, requesting a GTM API quota increase for that project is worth doing at the same time. A follow-up worth considering before GA: routing this source through `posthog/egress/` so concurrent syncs share one Redis-backed budget.

## How did you test this code?

- Transport tests: quota-vs-permission 403 routing (a permission 403 must never be retried; a quota 403 must never disable the source), page-token advance, three-level fan-out path construction, the account filter pruning the walk, and the `includeDeleted` param reaching version_headers.
- Source tests: OAuth error mapping to reconnect prompts (raw `RefreshError` reprs must not leak to users), full-refresh-only schema declarations, and account-filter validation including the paginated-probe case.
- Ran the registry-wide source guard suites and the OAuth integration model tests locally; repo-wide mypy is clean, and the frontend type check reports no new errors against the master baseline.
- Not run: a live sync against the real GTM API. The OAuth app is not registered yet, so the source ships as `ALPHA` with request/response shapes verified against the GTM API v2 reference instead.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

Companion posthog.com PR adds `/docs/cdp/sources/google-tag-manager` (linked in comments once open). `audit_source_docs` passes against that checkout.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

- Authored with Claude Code from issue #79110.
- Skills invoked: /implementing-warehouse-sources, /django-migrations, /writing-tests, /writing-user-facing-copy, /writing-code-comments, /documenting-warehouse-sources, /writing-pr-descriptions.
- Generated artifacts refreshed with `pnpm generate:source-configs`, `pnpm run schema:build`, `hogli build:openapi`, and targeted kea typegen for logic files embedding the IntegrationKind union.
- Considered a service-account key upload for auth; chose OAuth to match every sibling Google source kind and their fail-closed rollout path.
- All sample data in tests is invented; nothing from the session beyond the public issue is referenced.

---

## Problem

- A project that drops to the free plan keeps every alert running, past the free limit of 5 per project.
- The limit is checked only when an alert is created. Context: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C08ERRQT41E/p1795111863099579

## Changes

- Past the limit, the newest enabled alerts run. The rest are skipped, stay enabled, and resume after an upgrade.
- Only a numeric `limit` on the `alerts` feature caps them. A missing feature means no cap. Creates are unchanged.
- Alerts that can never run take no slot: a lost cadence, a deleted insight, a copy whose alert is gone, or disabled by their owning stack.
- An alert is skipped only if a second ranking agrees, because an ownership change between the two reads can drop it once.
- Both stacks share one ranking helper. Turning an alert on is refused when running alerts fill the limit.
- The skip advances `next_check_at` only if the schedule is unchanged. The weekend skip has the same race, left as is.
- The API exposes a read-only `over_plan_limit`.

## How did you test this code?

An agent wrote and ran the tests. Nothing was tested by hand.

- New tests failed before the fix, covering each rule above in both stacks, the API and the Max tool.
- Also ran the alerts and Temporal alert suites, mypy, and `spectacular --fail-on-warn`.
- `EXPLAIN` shows both ranking queries on per-team indexes, so no new index.

**Test rationale:** `test_alert_limit` and `test_skip_branches` cover only creates and other skip reasons.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/writing-dataclasses`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-pr-descriptions` (read from `.agents/skills`)

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver. The driver decided the policy: per project, newest N by `created_at`, skip instead of disable.

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code, local devbox with the dev stack in Docker.
- **Decisions:** take-ownership is refused over the limit because it shares `validate_alert_write` and `update_limit_error`; no extra code.
- **Decisions:** `update_limit_error` now returns `AlertLimitRefusal`, so the enable refusal reports on `enabled`, not `calculation_interval`.
- **Follow-ups:** a UI tag or banner for `over_plan_limit`; generated API types are left for the CI regen bot (no node toolchain locally).
- **Read closely:** `AlertConfiguration.alerts_kept_by_plan_limit`, which merges insight rows with platform-only alerts.
- **Read closely:** complexity of `prepare_alert` rises by one branch (preflight warn-only).

</details>

hits.body:
## Problem

- Support teammates get one Support AI run per ticket. The investigation goes stale when the customer adds detail before anyone replies.
- A teammate has no way to ask for a fresh run.

## Changes

- The AI triage panel has a "Run again" button. Its output is always a private note, also on channels set to auto-reply.
- A new setting under AI agent, "Run again when the customer adds a message", is off by default. When on, each new customer message starts a run until a teammate replies, up to 3 more runs per ticket.
- A second click with no new customer or teammate message is refused with a reason, so one ticket state costs one run.
- Run events carry `trigger`. Two new events record requested and refused manual runs.

One run per ticket becomes one run per trigger:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[First customer message] --> R{{Support AI run}}
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    class R phBlue;
    class A phYellow;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[First customer message] --> R{{Support AI run}}
    B[Later customer message, setting on, no teammate reply] --> R
    C[Run again button] --> R
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    class R phBlue;
    class A,B,C phYellow;
```

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** The run decision is a pure function with a case matrix, plus one scan test per setting value as the wiring guard. The endpoint tests cover the started run and each refusal. One workflow test checks the new child id.

- Not run: the UI. Storybook did not build locally, so there is no screenshot.
- Not regenerated: the desktop API client.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, claude-fable-5-2

**Skills:** `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/writing-ui-components`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/organizing-conversations-code`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code.
- **Decisions:** The driver chose the button and the "until a teammate replies" level. "Every customer reply" and interrupting a running workflow were left out.
- **Decisions:** The coordinator gates the new child id behind `workflow.patched`, placed before the data check, so older histories replay with the first-draft id.
- **Decisions:** Manual runs stay private through the context and persist activities, so the reply workflow emits the same commands.
- **Decisions:** The scan window grows from 5 to 10 minutes, so a message that arrives during a run is still in the scan when that run finishes.
- **Release status:** Support AI runs only for organizations on the allowlist flag. The new UI has no flag check of its own.
- **Duplicate search:** no open PR covers this.
- **Read closely:** `customer_reply_rerun_key` and the workflow loop in `products/conversations/backend/temporal/coordinator.py`, and `products/conversations/backend/ai/rerun.py`.
- **Review findings:** fixed, except the two below. Manual runs key on the latest customer or teammate message and claim the ticket before dispatch. Scouts cannot call the endpoint.
- **Review findings, follow-up mode:** a failed first run stays on the retry path, a safety block stops further runs, and clarification notes and follow-up ids are scoped to the asking run.
- **Not changed:** a private teammate note does not count as new input for a manual run, because the run context leaves private notes out.
- **Follow-ups:** a message that arrives during a run longer than the scan window does not start a run.

</details>

## Problem

- Stripe tables on webhook sync with no enabled webhook stopped updating after [#123644](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/123644). Each skipped run still shows "Completed".
- Users find out only when a downstream revenue report goes wrong. The only signals are a sync-log warning and a health check that sends no email by default.

Closes #127527

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a19d0c-c6b5-79fb-b825-29426e7e5f36 -->

## Changes

- The schemas table now shows a warning tag, **Completed, no webhook**, in place of "Completed". The tooltip says the table gets no webhook updates and tells the user to set up the webhook or change the sync method.
- A new read-only API field, `webhook_not_registered`, drives the tag. It uses the same rule as the `webhook_not_registered` health check. The serializer looks up each source once per response.
- The poll skip stays, so the cost saving from #123644 stays.
- New Prometheus counter `warehouse_stripe_webhook_unregistered_skips_total{endpoint}` counts each skipped run.
- Mechanical: regenerated OpenAPI types.

**Test rationale:** The parameterized API test fails if the field ignores a disabled webhook, a pending initial sync, or the sync type. A query-count test fails if the lookup runs once per schema and not once per source. No existing test covered this field.

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

> **Handover: do not merge or queue.** This is for AI observability review, with `merge: manual`. It reads the properties that https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/139307 records.

> **Scope:** results, failures, failure rate and unknown tools called. Latest intent and the `$ai_tool_intent` taxonomy/MCP allowlist entry were removed in `0184fc01`, along with Carlos's review fixes.

## Problem

The Tools tab counts tool calls but does not show which captured results failed or which calls named tools absent from the agent's definitions.

## Intended scope

The table adds four columns in one pass over generations:

- **Failure rate:** failures as a share of captured results, empty when no results were captured.
- **Failures** and **Results:** errors and total tool results sent back to the model.
- **Unknown tools called:** calls whose name is absent from the supplied tool definitions. This does not establish which capabilities the agent wanted.

Results arrive in the generation after the call. Explicit SDK error flags take precedence; without one, ingestion uses text starting with Error, Exception or Traceback. Failures which end a run before the next generation are not captured by this query.

Intent extraction was removed from the ingestion PR because derived text needs the same access restrictions as its source. Latest intent and its `$ai_tool_intent` taxonomy entry are removed here too, since every `$ai_` taxonomy entry lands on the MCP trace allowlist. The other five tool properties keep their entries: they hold only tool names and counts, derived from `$ai_tools` and `$ai_input`, which are already on the MCP trace allowlist, so MCP clients receive nothing they could not already read.

## Before / after evidence

Screenshots use invented data in a mocked Storybook scene. The after shot was captured at `346639fe`, with intent removed and the review fixes applied.

## Problem

- A hobby install on a small host runs short of memory, and its Temporal worker is the largest process.
- At start, that worker imports every data warehouse source and its vendor SDK. Most hobby installs have few sources or none.

## Changes

- On a hobby install, the worker imports only the source types that the install has a source for. Set `TEMPORAL_PRELOAD_ALL_DATA_IMPORT_SOURCES=true` in `.env` to restore the full preload.
- Cloud and dev keep the default, the full preload.
- `SourceRegistry.is_registered` now imports only the requested type, as `get_source` already did. Before, the first sync on a selective worker imported every source. This applies to every process that calls it.
- A worker that cannot read the sources at boot logs a warning and falls back to the full preload.
- A source type that gets its first source after the worker started is imported on its first sync, as the source registry already does for other processes. A worker restart preloads it.
- The preload exists because a vendor SDK must register its protobuf descriptors once per process. Sources in use still load at boot on the main thread, so that holds for them.

## How did you test this code?

- On a hobby install, the idle Temporal worker used 1,625 MiB before and 1,248 MiB with this PR and #142252 together. Skipping the full preload alone measured 1,345 MiB.
- On that install, which has no sources, the worker started cleanly and loaded no vendor SDK.
- Not run: a real sync after a lazy first import, and the database-backed test, which needs Postgres.

**Test rationale:**

- The database case in `test_load_sources_in_use.py` fails if the preload imports a type with no source, a deleted one, or an unknown type.
- The `is_registered` case fails if the check loads every source again.
- The dispatch case in `test_start_temporal_worker.py` fails if a database error, including `InterfaceError`, skips the fallback.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.2

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/pr-shepherd`, `/qa-swarm`, `/review-triage`

**Driver checked:** Decided to cut the full source preload on hobby. Not yet checked the diff.

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** Preloading the types in use, not nothing, keeps the once-per-process import at boot for every source an install syncs. A failed boot read falls back to the full preload, not to none, for the same reason.
- **CI report:** the comment-density alert counts comments that each give a reason the code cannot show: the late import, the fallback, the setting. None restates the code.
- **Follow-ups:** #140195 removes the same warehouse Temporal imports from web.
- **Read closely:** `load_sources_in_use` queries all teams' sources at worker start; the lazy path for a newly added type; `SourceRegistry._load_for`, now shared by `get_source` and `is_registered` in every process.

## Problem

- People writing SQL in the editor cannot see how much a query reads until it runs and times out.
- PostHog AI cannot check a query's cost before it calls `execute-sql`.
- This PR supersedes #99073, on top of #97761, #97762 and #99037.

## Changes

- The bar above the results leads with the estimate and warns past one billion events.
- Expanding the bar shows the plan: each scan with its size, its property filters and what each skips, then the join.
- A new `explain-sql` MCP tool returns the same plan without running the query.
- A read the estimate cannot follow, such as a subquery in WHERE, shows as not counted.
- Statistics lookups share one five-second budget.
- Mechanical: regenerated schema, OpenAPI clients and MCP tool schemas.

![bar_with_filters_900](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/939b9c38861a5973e50dd7fa0bc4eb00d0d61ddb/2026/09/124e457b-52b8-433a-8485-3ed4a2322de2.png)

![bar_large_no_filters_520](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/7d61d7fcd8c559bd9b4d87a35b50f6da85464fe6/2026/09/8f1f3ee6-0834-4d4e-aa69-5ac67bdabb95.png)

![scan_tables_900](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/662c9001a4b9fd271b687114530eb9b9fe0acdcb/2026/09/95e7d173-ac44-4a94-aabd-c8576fdf3396.png)

![scan_tables_520](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/b665d560c7207d6b364a2dc24d334372831e938e/2026/09/2a98f55f-416a-4f19-8a6a-2201e566fe2f.png)

![cost_plan_900](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/bdd357706638540e15a5e482cb8a9c9a568092f5/2026/09/8050b46c-b7a6-444b-8e80-99d968bde6c2.png)

![cost_plan_520](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/20900dc03f37d61943e7f22b570e1e6545fa837f/2026/09/9c016e24-0924-4331-a076-8b9287ba306a.png)

> [!WARNING]
> `HOGQL_SCAN_ESTIMATE_AT_EXECUTION` stays off by default.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** each new test catches one review finding.

- Not run: the MCP tool through a connected agent, and the estimator against production `read_rows`.

<details>
<summary>CI report findings that stay open</summary>

- Visual review: the 10 diffs are this PR's `QueryIndexUsageBar` stories. Eight are new stories. "Refreshing after an edit" changed because its header copy is now "Checking query".
- Complexity (TypeScript): 18 of the 20 functions predate this PR in `sqlEditorLogic.tsx` and `OutputPane.tsx`. `QueryIndexUsageBar` and `describeTableScan` branch once per plan state.
- Duplication (Python): the flagged blocks are the per-source upsert and reconcile functions on `master`. This PR adds the same row-count line to each.
- Bundle size: the schema adds about 3.7 KiB. The other grown bundles, such as the notebook exporter and the inbox, are files this PR does not touch.
- Comment density (5%): the comments state estimator assumptions. Left for the reviewer to judge which to cut.
- Backend coverage (93%): most uncovered lines are failure fallbacks in `metadata.py`, `estimate.py` and `statistics.py`. No test was added only to raise coverage.
- Playwright: "Add a new person property" is flaky and unrelated.

</details>

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- `hogql-python.md` in the engineering handbook describes the estimate and plan.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5. Earlier sessions used Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1).

**Skills:** `/clickhouse-migrations`, `/implementing-mcp-tools`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/stacking-prs`, `/debugging-ci-failures`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Security review:** needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** the tool lives in `products/posthog_ai/backend/mcp_tools/`, because `ee/` takes no new files.
- **Decisions:** the accuracy test uses the v3 query log archive, because #120883 removed the older tables.
- **Decisions:** the latest session merged `master`, dropped `tool-definitions-all.json`, which `master` no longer generates, and regenerated `schema.py`.
- **Follow-ups:** `execute_sql` has the query access-control gap that `explain_sql` closed.
- **Follow-ups:** a filter the model does not cover still lands under the first scan of its scope.
- **Read closely:** `posthog/hogql/cost/statistics.py` (lookup budget and HTTP pool) and `_SubqueryOutsideFromFinder` in `posthog/hogql/cost/estimate.py`.

</details>

## Problem

- An agent that follows `exploring-llm-costs` to find the most expensive traces gets the newest traces instead, and does not notice.
- `query-llm-traces-list` orders by timestamp only ([`_get_order_by_clause`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/90d137cdef/posthog/hogql_queries/ai/traces_query_runner.py#L692-L693)). `TracesQuery` has no `orderBy` field, so the MCP tool drops the key and reports it in `_ignoredKeys`.
- The skill never wrote `orderBy` literally. But it labeled the traces list "(sort by cost)" and described the tool as listing traces "with rolled-up cost", so agents tried to sort it by cost.
- Two related skills say the same thing: `exploring-ai-failures` ("sort by a metric") and `analyzing-expensive-users` ("Find high-cost traces").

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a11e06-b0c0-7b54-9116-d4862a00bc9a -->
## Origin

- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-10-09
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a11e06-b0c0-7b54-9116-d4862a00bc9a?link_source=github_pr)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P3 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a11e06-b0c0-7b54-9116-d4862a00bc9a -->

## Changes

- `exploring-llm-costs` now says that the way to rank traces by cost is the `execute-sql` cost-by-trace recipe, followed by `query-llm-trace` for each trace. It states that the list tool has no cost sort and ignores `orderBy`.
- The tool-table rows in the three skills no longer say that the list tool can sort by a metric. The "(sort by cost)" label on the traces-list UI link is gone, because the UI list uses the same timestamp-only query.
- The breakdown-patterns reference repeats the same warning under its cost-by-trace recipe.
- The table realignment in `exploring-ai-failures` is formatter output only.

No tool or API change. Adding a cost sort to `TracesQuery` is a possible separate change. If that ships, the skill can document the new parameter then.

## How did you test this code?

- `./bin/hogli lint:skills` passes. Its advisory warnings are all in other products' skills.
- `bin/hogli format:markdown` ran on the changed files.
- Not done: no live agent run against the updated skill.

**Test rationale:** Only skill markdown changes. Skill lint covers structure and tool references, and no unit test applies to prose.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None. The skills are the docs.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

- Started from an inbox report saying the skill told agents to pass `orderBy: "cost"`. The repo, the installed skill copies, and git history all have no `orderBy` in these skills. The cost-sort hints listed above are the most likely cause, so this PR fixes them.
- Duplicate search: [#107058](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/107058) edits the same reference file, but only its cross-links, so it is not a duplicate.
- Skills used: `/writing-pr-descriptions`. No session material is in the diff.

## Problem

Cloud runs on the Claude runtime call MCP tools that are set to "needs approval" without asking the user. The gateway proxy then rejects the call. Desktop already asks first.

Refs #76237

## Changes

- Cloud runs now ask with one option, "Yes, and approve this tool in PostHog". On yes, the run saves the approval, then makes the call. Two installations whose names sanitize alike stay ungated.
- An allow saves the approval only when the answer carries `confirmPersistentApproval: true`. PostHog AI and the desktop app send it only when a person clicks an allow option on a prompt marked `persistsApproval`. Anything that answers on its own (PostHog AI tabs loaded before this deploy, auto-approve modes, the Slack permission broker) picks the first allow option, so the option id alone can't show a person approved the tool. Those answers are declined, and the run tells the user to approve the tool in PostHog.
- The approval is saved with the run's credentials, so it's saved only when the person who answered is the user those credentials belong to. The `/command` JWT says who answered, and `/api/users/@me/` says who the run acts as. If a teammate answers, the run declines the same way.
- Saving an approval needs `project:write`, but `/command` needs only `task:write`. So `/command` now returns 403 for a `permission_response` with `confirmPersistentApproval` from a personal API key or OAuth token without `project:write`, before it reaches the sandbox. Browser sessions and the desktop app, whose token holds `project:write`, are unaffected.
- On codex, a decline with a reason reaches codex as a decline, not a cancel, and the reason is added to the running turn. A cancel aborts the whole turn on command approvals, and on MCP prompts the model sees only "user cancelled".
- Background runs and runs with no connected client decline without asking. Slack runs relay the prompt like any other run, and the confirmation check declines the broker's answer.
- The mobile apps don't send the confirmation yet, so allowing a tool from them is declined with the same guidance rather than saved.
- A `PreToolUse` hook forces "ask" for these tools, because `bypassPermissions` skips `canUseTool`.
- Approval states load at startup alongside session setup, capped at 5s so they never delay the run. Past that, tools load ungated. They reload on `refresh_session`, where an installation whose fetch fails keeps its last loaded states.

Out of scope: built-in agent runs (gateway grant URLs), Pi's "allow once", and saving the approval as the person who answered rather than with the run's credentials.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `agent-server.test.ts` and `posthog-api.test.ts` (301 tests), `tsc` and Biome in the agent workspace, `permissionResponse.test.ts` and the desktop `pnpm typecheck`, and all of `runStreamLogic.test.ts` (416 tests).
- Added codex cases for a command approval and an MCP prompt cancelled with a reason. Each declines and passes the reason on, and each failed with its guard removed. The codex adapter suite passes (397 tests).
- Added `test_command_persistent_approval_requires_project_write`: a `task:write` key gets a 403 and nothing reaches the sandbox, and a key with `project:write` goes through. Without the scope check, the first case got a 200 and was forwarded.
- The new cases each failed without their fix: an allow without the confirmation was saved, PostHog AI sent no confirmation for a person's allow, and the desktop helper didn't exist.
- Earlier rounds: ran the agent workspace's adapter, server and API Vitest suites, plus the full-auto cases in `runStreamLogic.test.ts` and the `toolPolicy.test.ts` table, removing each fix in turn to check its test failed.
- The approval tests answer through the real `permission_response` command with a caller user id and the confirmation flag, including a teammate who allows and an answer with no confirmation. Neither gets the tool approved.
- On a devbox running the real stack, with a DeepWiki installation named "Deep Wiki (test)", I checked the backend calls the agent makes:
  - New tools default to "needs approval".
  - A proxy `tools/call` before approval returns `-32001 "requires approval"`.
  - The agent's `PATCH tools/<name>/` approves the tool, and the same call then reaches the upstream server.
  - The sandbox config uses the raw name `Deep Wiki (test)`, so the agent needs the sanitized key, and its installation regex matches the proxy URL.

## Problem

Two reports on the same team can reach auto-start with findings that name the same file and the same causative commit, and the pipeline opens a PR for each. Nothing after research compares a report with its siblings.

Each research run writes `signal_finding` artefacts (`SignalFinding` in `products/signals/backend/artefact_schemas.py`) with `relevant_code_paths` and `relevant_commit_hashes`, plus an `actionability_judgment` (`ActionabilityAssessment.already_addressed`). `maybe_autostart_implementation_task` (`products/signals/backend/auto_start.py`) gates on `already_addressed` but has no view of other reports. `already_addressed` is filled by the research agent's own `gh pr list` check, which is an instruction, not a mechanism (see the companion issue on feeding known PRs into research).

On one customer project, eight reports over five days all carried findings on the same `providers.tsx` path and the same commit hash (an unguarded analytics init letting local dev servers report into production). Three of them auto-started and opened three PRs changing that file. The signals were genuinely different exceptions, so grouping could not have joined them; the overlap only exists at the finding level, after research.

## Fixes

1. **Sibling overlap check before auto-start.** In `maybe_autostart_implementation_task` (or a small helper in `auto_start.py` it calls), load the `signal_finding` artefacts of the other `ready` reports on the team from the last N days (30 is a reasonable start) and compare with the new report's findings. Treat as overlapping when they share a causative commit hash, or share the primary code path (first entry, or any path present in every finding of the new report). Pure Postgres, no LLM call.
2. **On overlap, do not auto-start.** Log a `skip_reason` of `sibling report already targets the same fix: <report id>` (the existing `skip_reason` pattern). Record it on the report as a `log` artefact so the inbox shows why no PR opened, and link the two reports (a `related_report` artefact or the existing linking mechanism if one fits).
3. **Prefer the report that already has a PR.** If a sibling has an implementation `task_run` with a `pr_url`, point the new report's summary at it rather than at nothing.
4. Do not merge reports automatically in this issue; linking plus no second PR is the outcome. Merging is a product decision for later.
5. Tests: two reports, overlapping commit hash, second one must skip auto-start with the sibling reason; overlapping path only; no overlap (auto-starts as today).

## Why

The pipeline already has, in its own artefacts, the fact that two reports name the same fix. Checking that is deterministic and cheap, and it is the check that would have prevented three PRs for one line of code. Relying on the research agent's `gh` lookup alone has already failed in production.

From this [Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09SK2PAGKF/p1787826992218019); the investigation is written up in the `self-driving-debugging` skill in the skills store.

## Problem

Ordered funnels drop users whose events arrive out of order: a slow request stores step one after step two, which the device captured later (#98250).

## Changes

- New `funnelUseClientCaptureOrder` modifier, off by default, orders funnel steps by the device's capture time (`$client_capture_time`, recorded by #103264).
- Each browser or mobile device gets one anchor per day, which cancels its clock error and leaves only its smallest delivery delay.
  - Mobile events without `$device_id` group by distinct ID plus device model, so two devices sharing a distinct ID stay apart.
  - The per-day bound limits the damage from a device clock change.
- Server SDK events, groups where any event lacks the capture time, and groups over 10,000 events keep the stored timestamp.
- Nothing changes until a team turns the modifier on; generated schema files are mechanical.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not enable the modifier until `$client_capture_time` is materialized on `events`; reading it from the properties JSON is far more expensive.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** `test_funnel_capture_order.py` covers each grouping rule (device ID, distinct ID plus model, day split, server SDKs, the size cap, partial coverage), funnel trends, and the materialized-column read. Breaking any one rule fails its test. The existing funnel suite and its snapshots are unchanged.

- A replay on sampled production data, browser and mobile in both regions, made under 0.5% of the reordered event pairs worse than the stored order.
- Peak memory on synthetic data stays close to the modifier-off query, because the group key is a hash.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- Ship order: #103264, then materialize `$client_capture_time`, then this.
- The anchor moved from one per device over the whole funnel window to one per SDK, device and day, after review found clock changes and mobile coverage gaps.
- An array-based anchor was benchmarked and rejected: it used more memory than window functions with a hashed key.
- Test fixtures are invented; no customer data reached the diff or this description.

## Problem

- API callers using `@current` get whichever project the user last opened, which can change between calls. The alias is being retired, and nothing tells callers to move to an explicit id or by when.

## Changes

Stacked on https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/142369, which records the id each request used.

- Responses under `projects`, `environments` and `organizations` `@current` carry `Deprecation`, `Sunset` (April 30, 2027) and a `Link` to the docs page (https://github.com/PostHog/posthog.com/pull/22844).
- Successful nested requests also get a `successor-version` link naming the id the resolver recorded. Refused ones get none.
- `/api/environments/*` no longer overwrites these headers. Bodies and status codes are unchanged.

A successful request:

```http
GET /api/projects/@current/feature_flags/?limit=1
Authorization: Bearer phx_...

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Deprecation: @1795564800
Sunset: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 23:59:59 GMT
Link: </api/projects/12345/feature_flags/?limit=1>; rel="successor-version", <https://posthog.com/docs/api/current-alias-deprecation>; rel="deprecation"
```

A refused request (key scoped to another project):

```http
GET /api/projects/@current/feature_flags/
Authorization: Bearer phx_...

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Deprecation: @1795564800
Sunset: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 23:59:59 GMT
Link: <https://posthog.com/docs/api/current-alias-deprecation>; rel="deprecation"
```

**Test rationale:** `test_routing.py` cases cover each alias, a refused key and an explicit id. They go red if `/api/environments/*` overwrites the link or a refused request gets one.

## Problem

54 products have a `backend/` directory but are not isolated, meaning they do not declare `backend:contract-check` in their `package.json`.

Two consequences, and the first one is mostly solved:

1. **Merge queue lanes.** Until recently a backend change in a non-isolated product claimed all 82 Python lanes, serializing it against every other backend PR. Stack #76952 fixes the bulk of that by deriving lanes from `tach.toml` instead, so the median product now claims 3. Isolation is no longer the big lever here.
2. **CI cost.** This one is untouched. A non-isolated product pays the **full Django test suite** on every backend change. `turbo-discover` uses `backend:contract-check` to decide whether the full suite can be skipped, so without it there is no selective testing for that product at all.

There is also a residual lane cost. Without a declared contract surface every backend file seeds the cascade, including tests and internals, so the widest products still drag in a dozen-plus lanes for a change nothing outside them can see.

## What isolation requires

Not a config edit. [`products/architecture.md`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/architecture.md) is explicit that declaring the key is a claim you have to earn first:

> Skipping the full suite for an isolated product is a claim that _a change inside the product can only break the product's own tests._ tach proves the import half of that claim. It cannot prove the other half. [...] "No importers" is necessary, not sufficient.

The unprovable half is that cross-cutting tests (permissions, schema, activity-log) reach a product's endpoints **by URL, in process**, with no import for any graph to see. So it is closed by construction, per product:

1. A facade as the product's only public interface.
2. A thin presentation layer that reaches internals only through the facade.
3. Behavior tests kept in-product.

Then, and only then:

```json
"scripts": {
    "backend:contract-check": "echo 'Contract files unchanged'"
}
```

Plus a `turbo.json` declaring the contract surface, using [`products/error_tracking/turbo.json`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/error_tracking/turbo.json) as the reference. That second part is what stops internals from cascading.

> [!WARNING]
> The inputs list is load-bearing for correctness, not just cost. Omitting a path other products import puts them in a parallel merge-queue lane, which is the silent-breakage mode lanes exist to prevent. Over-declaring only costs parallelism, so when in doubt leave a path in.

## Suggested order

Ranked by current lane width, which correlates with how much cross-product surface each one presents. CI-cost savings roughly track suite size instead, so the two orderings differ - worth checking both before picking.

| Product | Lanes today |
| --- | --- |
| `product_analytics` | 17 |
| `cohorts` | 14 |
| `feature_flags` | 14 |
| `actions` | 12 |
| `dashboards` | 12 |
| `notifications` | 12 |
| `cdp` | 11 |
| `ai_observability` | 9 |
| `signals` | 9 |
| `data_tools` | 8 |
| `experiments` | 8 |
| `alerts` | 7 |
| `event_definitions` | 7 |
| `surveys` | 7 |

The remaining 40 sit at 5 lanes or fewer, so their payoff is almost entirely the full-suite skip rather than queue parallelism.

<details>
<summary>All 54 non-isolated products with a backend</summary>

`access_control`, `actions`, `ai_gateway`, `ai_observability`, `alerts`, `analytics_platform`, `annotations`, `approvals`, `batch_exports`, `business_knowledge`, `cdp`, `cohorts`, `conversations`, `dashboards`, `data_catalog`, `data_tools`, `demo`, `early_access_features`, `event_definitions`, `experiments`, `exports`, `feature_flags`, `field_notes`, `growth`, `links`, `live_debugger`, `llm_analytics`, `logs`, `managed_migrations`, `marketing_analytics`, `mcp_analytics`, `mcp_store`, `messaging`, `notebooks`, `notifications`, `platform_features`, `posthog_ai`, `product_analytics`, `product_tours`, `pulse`, `reminders`, `replay`, `replay_vision`, `revenue_analytics`, `review_hog`, `signals`, `skills`, `slack_app`, `surveys`, `tracing`, `user_interviews`, `warehouse_sources_queue`, `web_analytics`, `workflows`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Out of scope: 12 products with no backend</summary>

`core_events`, `desktop`, `games`, `groups`, `ingestion`, `integrations`, `persons`, `session_replay`, `session_summaries`, `subscriptions`, `support`, `toolbar`

Nothing to isolate. `desktop` is already narrow via the `backendDetachedProducts` rule (a `pytest.ini --ignore` entry plus absence from `tach.toml`).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Already isolated: 15</summary>

`customer_analytics`\*, `data_modeling`, `data_warehouse`, `endpoints`, `engineering_analytics`\*, `error_tracking`\*, `legal_documents`\*, `managed_warehouse`\*, `metrics`\*, `stamphog`\*, `streamlit_apps`\*, `tasks`, `visual_review`\*, `warehouse_sources`, `wizard`\*

`*` = also declares narrowed contract inputs in `turbo.json`. The five without one treat every backend file as contract, so they still cascade on internals and are worth a follow-up too.

</details>

## Notes

This is a tracking issue, not a single PR. Each product is its own change and wants review from whoever owns it, since the architectural work is the substance and the declaration is just the last line of it.

Numbers here were measured against `master` with stack #76952 applied.

## Problem

Analysts must rerun a notebook and click **Replace rows** before downstream SQL sees fresh results. [#140517](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140517)

## Changes

An agent can now run a notebook between SQL models in PostHog’s warehouse DAG. For example, SQL totals sales, Python forecasts demand, and SQL lists items to reorder.

- **Declare** a table from a SQL or Python cell and name its upstream models.
- **Refresh** daily or on demand. Each run publishes the cell’s full dataframe.
- **Inspect** failed cells and the last published run. A failed refresh preserves the table and skips dependent SQL.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Run notebook] --> B[Save or replace rows in browser] --> C[Warehouse table]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[SQL model: total sales by item] --> B[Notebook Python cell: forecast demand] --> C[demand_forecast table] --> D[SQL model: list items to reorder]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A,D phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

<details>
<summary>Using the three MCP tools</summary>

Enable `notebook-warehouse-models` for MCP after the Django routes deploy.

| Tool | How to use it for the reorder report |
| --- | --- |
| `notebooks-declare-warehouse-model` | Choose the forecast cell, name its table `demand_forecast`, and pass the sales model’s node ID as an upstream dependency. |
| `notebooks-run-warehouse-model` | Start the model and its upstream dependencies now. After the first publication, reference `demand_forecast` in the downstream SQL model. |
| `notebooks-warehouse-model-status` | Pass the returned `dag_run_id` to see whether the run reached the notebook. Inspect cell errors and the run that produced the current table. |

Each run executes the saved notebook through the selected cell. First publication requires an unused table name. Later refreshes keep the table ID. Runs that share a notebook wait their turn, and previous generations remain readable for 24 hours.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** [Warehouse tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/posthog/api/test/notebooks/test_warehouse_model.py#L217) cover replacement. [DAG tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/products/data_modeling/backend/temporal/tests/test_execute_dag_workflow.py#L635) cover failure propagation.

<details>
<summary>CI advisories and regression coverage</summary>

The warehouse round trip read 14,000 synthetic rows on each of two refreshes. A failed third refresh preserved the second table. A local Temporal test used a stub notebook task to check dependency ordering.

The API test checks that the returned ticket identifies the queued Temporal run and that polling uses the same project, node, and ticket. The workflow tests exercise the receiver. Time-skipping tests cover a busy notebook, downstream failure, and delayed cleanup. A warehouse round trip reads both generations across replacement.

CI measured a 7.7 KiB decrease in total frontend bundle size. Of the two eager roots over budget, logged-out boot had zero growth and the authenticated shell grew 3.5 KiB against the CI baseline. The frontend diff only regenerates the notebook API. No browser code imports the new client functions or schemas. CI also shows changes in the Today sidebar chunks, outside this diff.

The database migration creates one table with a primary key on `node_id`, its node foreign key, and an index on `team_id`. The migration analyzer classified it as safe. Five Chromium cases passed on retry. Two exercise editing or deleting an ordinary notebook. The other three cover person properties, insight titles, and workflow secrets. None of the five exercises model declaration, DAG execution, or warehouse publication.

</details>

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

[Warehouse modeling guide](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/docs/published/handbook/engineering/data-warehouse.md#L117)

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** OpenAI Codex, GPT-6

**Skills:** `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/implementing-mcp-tools`, `/django-migrations`, `/writing-tests`, `/verifying-changes`, `/writing-dataclasses`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/run-posthog`, `/writing-clickhouse-queries`, `/isolating-product-facade-contracts`, `/running-ci-preflight`, `/debugging-ci-failures`, `/security-audit`, `/querying-local-postgres`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** Model declarations pin the selected cells and variables. Edits require redeclaration.
- **Read closely:** Publication checks author access again and serializes competing table replacements.
- **Verification:** Automated tests used generated inventory rows and local services. Production sandbox execution is unverified.

## Problem

- An agent that follows `analyzing-expensive-users` cannot list traces for a top spender, so it cannot explain why that user costs so much.
- The skill ranks users by `distinct_id`. Then it sends the agent to `query-llm-traces-list`, whose `personId` accepts only a person UUID.
- A `distinct_id` that is not a UUID fails validation, and the skill gives no way to get the UUID.

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a13aca-ba92-7ef2-a060-3ef8bd8be1cf -->
## Origin

- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-10-14
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a13aca-ba92-7ef2-a060-3ef8bd8be1cf?link_source=github_pr)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a13aca-ba92-7ef2-a060-3ef8bd8be1cf -->

## Changes

- The step 1 ranking query now also returns `person_uuid` (`argMax(person_id, timestamp)`). This is the same `events.person_id` column that the `personId` filter reads.
- Step 5 tells the agent to pass `person_uuid` as `personId`, never the `distinct_id`. It also gives an example call.
- Step 5 adds a lookup query that maps one `distinct_id` to its person UUID, for when step 1 did not keep it.
- Fallbacks: more than one UUID means the agent picks the busiest one and reports a caveat. No UUID means the agent stops using the list tool and opens the SQL-ranked trace IDs with `query-llm-trace`.
- The alias is `person_uuid` and not `person_id`. A bare `person_id` alias nests `argMax()` inside itself, and HogQL rejects the query. The skill says this.
- This is a skill text change only. No product code changes.

## How did you test this code?

- All three documented queries ran through the PostHog MCP `execute-sql` tool against a live project, over a 1-day window:
  - The full revised step 1 ranking query returned a `person_uuid` for each ranked user.
  - The fallback lookup query returned the same UUID for a ranked `distinct_id`.
  - A first draft that used the alias `person_id` failed with the nested-aggregate error, which confirmed the reason for the alias note.
- `query-llm-traces-list` with that `person_uuid` as `personId` returned traces.
- `hogli lint:skills` and `hogli format:markdown` pass on the changed skill, with no new warnings and no format changes.

**Test rationale:** No new test. The change is documentation for an agent skill, and the live tool calls above check it.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None. The skill file is the doc.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

- Skills invoked: `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `writing-simplified-technical-english` conventions.
- Tools: the PostHog MCP `execute-sql` and `query-llm-traces-list` tools, for read-only checks of the documented queries.
- Rejected alternative: a `distinctId` filter on the trace tool. That is a product contract change, and the SQL mapping fixes the skill without one.
- Duplicate search: [#114266](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/114266) edits the same tool-table row for a different problem (cost ranking). It does not fix the UUID mapping. The two PRs can conflict on that one row.
- Public artifact: the committed text holds no data from the agent session. All placeholders are generic.

---

## Problem

- A person with edit access to a destination can change its code, inputs or mappings to send its stored secret elsewhere, without knowing it.
- Replaces [#127873](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/127873). Stack base for [#130961](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/130961) (dialog) and [#130964](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/130964) (workflows). Integrations are covered by [#132254](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/132254) and [#132255](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/132255).

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door (merge-risk rubric)
> - Every save of a function with a stored secret runs the check. Refusals sit behind `cdp-secret-host-binding`, off by default.
> - **Revert:** turn off the flag, or revert.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

- With the flag on, a save that changes code, inputs or mappings must type every stored secret again, or it fails with `secret_reentry_required`.
- Renames, filters and enabling still save.
- Any edit to the code, inputs, schema or mappings counts, including a schema label or option list. Only server-derived fields, such as bytecode, are left out.
- Site destinations and site apps are checked too.
- Agent drafts are checked at publish and in draft test runs. Only a secret typed in a draft edit counts, until a later edit changes the content or another secret.
- A test run sends the code and mappings its secrets were checked against.
- A secret left in a legacy mapping blocks those changes until the mapping no longer holds it.
- Copies carry no secret.
- With the flag off, saves pass and count `would_refuse` on `posthog_cdp_secret_reentry_total`.

## How to test

With the flag on, on an HTTP Webhook destination with a **Signing secret**:

1. Change the code in **Edit source** and save. Expect "Enter this secret again to save changes to the code, inputs or mappings." on Signing secret.
2. Type the secret in the same edit. Expect the save to pass.
3. Rename or disable it. Expect the save to pass.
4. Duplicate it. Expect a disabled copy with the secret empty.

## How did you test this code?

- API tests cover PATCH, PUT, drafts, publish and test runs, including concurrent draft edits.
- Each new case failed on the commit before its fix.
- A UI walk ran on a local stack at `4d7431bf706`. The flag was on at 100% in the local project, with no code override. The demo secret is made up.
- Not captured: step 4, duplicate.

The saved Signing secret shows masked.

![Signing secret masked after save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/91cfb5980120f7a77cf2326311d46f1bef0511cf/2026/11/a1829b7c-e134-41d9-9b2b-3c9dce46c1ec.png)

A code edit saved without the secret shows the refusal under Signing secret and an "Upsert hog function failed" toast.

![Refusal under Signing secret with error toast](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/91cfb5980120f7a77cf2326311d46f1bef0511cf/2026/11/1a8098ec-be51-49b7-8cc9-b30fcee15acc.png)

The secret typed again in the same edit, then saved: "Configuration saved".

![Signing secret typed again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/91cfb5980120f7a77cf2326311d46f1bef0511cf/2026/11/3df82acd-d085-4ebc-85db-84785b52b31e.png)
![Save passes with the secret typed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/91cfb5980120f7a77cf2326311d46f1bef0511cf/2026/11/c91790ab-31b6-4caa-89c7-75a234b8cb3c.png)

A rename plus disable saves without the secret.

![Rename and disable save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/91cfb5980120f7a77cf2326311d46f1bef0511cf/2026/11/6867b37c-e477-4712-adff-0f9440808ba8.png)

<details>
<summary>Recording: refusal, then re-entry</summary>

![Recording of the refusal and the re-entry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/91cfb5980120f7a77cf2326311d46f1bef0511cf/2026/11/ceab6496-9cfa-4046-b033-0382d14853d2.gif)

</details>
- Backend coverage leaves 10 changed lines uncovered: guards for non-dictionary entries, and `replaces_stored_value`, which only runs for a draft secret saved before this PR added the entered mark.
- The 2 flaky Playwright tests (person properties, notebooks) run no CDP code.
- The 3 call assertions read what a test run sends to the CDP worker. They patch `create_hog_invocation_test`, the outbound HTTP call, which is the endpoint's only output. Two check that a test run sends the code and input order its secrets were checked against. One checks that a refused test run sends nothing to the worker.
- The Hogbox preview failed during template sync, because the preview's web container could not resolve the `plugins` host. This PR changes no template or preview code.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`); QA swarm panel per `fleet proof review`

**Skills:** `/tdd`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** re-entry alone closes theft of a typed secret, so the PR stores no origins and needs no worker check. The static analyzer and platform auth from earlier rounds are gone.
- **Decisions:** typing one secret counts as an input change, because code can send one secret to an address another holds.
- **Decisions:** the check validates both the stored config and the request once, then compares code, inputs, inputs_schema and mappings as canonical JSON. It leaves out only server-derived fields at fixed places (bytecode, bytecode_contract, bytecode_error, input_deps, order, transpiled) and secret values. A secret's other metadata counts. Each input keeps its own stored templating, read as hog when missing, as the worker does. A field-by-field comparison kept missing fields the worker reads, such as `choices`.
- **Decisions:** a stored config that no longer validates is compared raw, so its first save asks for its secrets. A save that copies a schema's liquid templating onto an input asks too, because the worker would evaluate it differently.
- **Decisions:** validation works on copies of the stored inputs and secrets, so it no longer writes into the stored row.
- **Decisions:** a draft edit marks each secret it writes with whether it was typed, so the same value typed again counts at publish and a value recovered before a live rotation does not. A partly masked dictionary does not count.
- **Decisions:** a restored revision of a function with a stored secret publishes once a draft edit types the secret. API-key callers cannot stage a draft, so they cannot publish such a restore.
- **Decisions:** the flag check fails open, and internal saves are counted, not refused.
- **Decisions:** copy paths checked: destination duplicate, workflow duplicate and workflow templates all start a new row with no stored secret to recover.
- **Decisions:** comment density is about 4%, over the 3% warning. The remaining comments state why each comparison rule holds, which a reviewer of this check needs.
- **Decisions:** a function's `name` stays out of the comparison. Inputs can read it as `source.name`, but they read event properties the same way, and renames must keep saving.
- **Decisions:** a test run orders object keys as Postgres `jsonb` stores them, so it runs what the comparison sees. The comparison keeps sorted keys to avoid refusing Terraform and API saves.
- **Decisions:** a draft edit validates against the draft's own schema and inputs. At publish, a secret made public needs a value other than the stored one.
- **Decisions:** a dictionary secret sent with stored entries left out counts as a change, even when every entry it sends is masked.
- **Decisions:** until the flag rolls out, saves and test runs behave as on `master`,

hits.body:
## Problem

- AI observability under-reports cost for OpenAI generations with prompts above 272K input tokens, such as GPT-6 Sol (#106645).
- OpenAI bills the whole request at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output above that threshold. The cost step only knew one long-context rule, for Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview.

Closes #106645

## Changes

- OpenAI generations above 272K input tokens now show long-context costs, and `$ai_model_cost_used` reads `<model>:large`.
- A per-model threshold table replaces the hard-coded Gemini rule. Gemini keeps its 200K threshold.
- New `:large` rows for 14 OpenAI models: standard, priority and flex rates, from the "Long" view of [OpenAI's pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing).
- The OpenAI rows apply only when `$ai_provider` resolves to `openai`. Azure, Bedrock and OpenRouter stay flat, because their long-context rates are not published there.
- A name must end at the model or a dated snapshot, so `gpt-5.4-mini` and `gpt-6-sol-pro` keep their own prices.

## How did you test this code?

- `cost-model-matching.test.ts`: `getNewModelName` cases at 272,000 and 272,001 tokens, snapshot names, excluded variants and non-OpenAI providers.
- `manual-providers.test.ts`: `processCost` for `gpt-6-sol` just under and over the threshold, on the standard, flex and priority tiers.
- `manual-providers.test.ts`: every `:large` route must equal 2x input and cache, 1.5x output of the same catalog route. A mistyped rate fails it.
- The new over-threshold cases failed on `master` (10 failures) and pass with the change. The AI cost and `process-ai-event` suites pass locally. ESLint, oxlint and Prettier are clean on the changed files.
- `tsc --noEmit` shows no errors in the changed files. The only errors come from workspace packages that were not built in this checkout.
- Not done: no run against live ingestion, and no check against a real OpenAI invoice.

**Test rationale:** The tests catch three regressions: an over-threshold OpenAI prompt that keeps the flat rate, a sibling model such as `-mini` or `-pro` that gets the wrong long-context rate, and a mistyped rate. The nearest existing tests are the Gemini `getNewModelName` cases, which these extend.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** None invoked as skills. The repo guides `writing-tests`, `writing-code-comments` and `writing-pr-descriptions` were read and followed.

**Driver checked:** Read the full diff

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code with the GitHub CLI and web fetch. Rates come from the pricing page's long-context table data, checked against the GPT-6 Sol model page.
- **Decisions:** Rates go in `manual-providers.ts` `:large` rows, as Gemini's do. This keeps them out of the generated `llm-costs.json`.
- **Decisions:** The provider gate exists because OpenAI publishes no long-context rates for other routes. Without a published rate, the flat rate is safer than a guess.
- **Follow-ups:** OpenAI publishes no long-context priority rate for gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.4, so a priority call on these models falls back to the standard long-context rate.
- **Follow-ups:** Ultrafast long-context rates are not wired, because `$ai_service_tier` has no ultrafast route.
- **Read closely:** The snapshot regex in `cost-model-matching.ts`. A Gemini name with a non-numeric suffix, other than `-tts`, no longer gets the 200K rule.

</details>

## Problem

- Some OpenAI Ads tables fail with a `server_error` on every run for weeks, but the sync error panel says the error is temporary and clears by itself.
- Customers get no step that they can do.

## Changes

- The message for an OpenAI Ads server error that is still there after all retries no longer says "temporary". It tells the customer to contact OpenAI Ads support if the error continues for a day.
- The error stays retryable, so the table stays on. A new API key can also get this error for a few minutes.
- Nothing else changes. The rest of the diff is one test.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran the OpenAI Ads vendor tests locally.

**Test rationale:** the new parameterized test covers the two error shapes seen in production: the 400 from the insights endpoint and the 403 rewritten to "Server error (HTTP 403)". It fails if `code=server_error` stops mapping to the message, or if the 403 shape starts to match the non-retryable 403 entry. The nearest test, `test_exhausted_transient_failures_are_recognized`, checks only retryability. The test failed when the mapping key was broken.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## Problem

OpenAI's [deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) lists several models that PostHog still calls. Two of them shut down on **Oct 23, 2026** and sit in live PostHog AI code paths: the insights query planner and conversation title generation. After the shutdown date, requests to these models fail.

## Shutdown Oct 23, 2026

| Model | Where | OpenAI's suggested replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `o4-mini` | `ee/hogai/chat_agent/query_planner/nodes.py:146` (insights query planner) | `gpt-5.6-terra` |
| `gpt-4.1-nano` | `ee/hogai/core/title_generator/nodes.py:85` (conversation titles) | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| `gpt-4.1-nano`, `o4-mini`, `o3-mini` | `products/ai_observability/backend/llm/providers/openai.py:56-106` (`SUPPORTED_MODELS`, `PLAYGROUND_MODELS`, `SUPPORTED_MODELS_WITH_THINKING`) | `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| `gpt-4.1-nano` | `products/ai_observability/backend/summarization/models.py:9` and `budget.py:10` (selectable summarization model, not the default) | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| `gpt-4.1-nano` | `services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/products/config.py:269` (`llma_summarization` allowlist) | `gpt-5.6-luna` |
| `o4-mini` | `posthog/llm/openai_flex.py:24` and `ee/hogai/llm.py:76` (flex-tier allowlists) | remove the entry |
| `o1-pro` | `products/ai_observability/backend/llm/providers/openai.py:77` (exclusion list) | remove the entry |

## Shutdown Apr 1, 2027

| Model | Where | OpenAI's suggested replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-5.3-codex` | `packages/agent/packages/harness/src/extensions/posthog-provider/models.ts:253`, `services/llm-gateway/src/llm_gateway/products/config.py:103` and `:172`, `products/tasks/backend/logic/services/gateway_model_pin.py:21`, `products/slack_app/evals/eval_model_classifier.py:70` | `gpt-6-sol` |
| `gpt-5.1` | `products/ai_observability/backend/llm/providers/openai.py:59` and `:99`, `posthog/llm/openai_flex.py:19` | `gpt-6-sol` |
| `gpt-5.4-nano` | `posthog/llm/openai_flex.py:17` (flex allowlist) | `gpt-6-luna` |

## Not affected

- The aliases `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.4`, `o3`, and the snapshot `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` are not on the deprecation page. These cover most PostHog AI call sites.
- `gpt-4`, `gpt-3.5-turbo`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `o1`, `whisper-1`, and `gpt-4o-audio-preview` appear only in tests, fixtures, cost tables, semgrep rule examples, and taxonomy examples. Nothing calls them.
- The `text-embedding-3-*` models are not listed.

## Things to check before swapping

- **Query planner.** It passes `reasoning` summaries and `reasoning.encrypted_content` through the Responses API. Confirm `gpt-5.6-terra` supports both, and run the PostHog AI evals, because planner quality affects every generated insight.
- **Title generator.** It sets `temperature=0.7`. GPT-5-family reasoning models typically reject a custom temperature, so the parameter probably has to go.
- **Desktop legacy pin.** `gateway_model_pin.py` keeps `gpt-5.3-codex` because older PostHog Desktop builds still call it. Those builds break at shutdown unless the gateway remaps the id.
- **LLM gateway freeze.** `services/llm-gateway` is under a code freeze while callers move to `PostHog/ai-gateway`. The allowlist edits need a parity justification, and the Go gateway's allowlists need the same audit.
- **Flex eligibility.** `posthog/llm/openai_flex.py` requires a check of OpenAI's flex pricing table before a model joins the list.
- **Config outside the repo.** Model ids set through environment variables or feature flag payloads do not show up in a code search and need a separate check.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace `o4-mini` in the query planner and run the evals
- [ ] Replace `gpt-4.1-nano` in the title generator
- [ ] Update the AI observability model lists (`gpt-4.1-nano`, `o4-mini`, `o3-mini`, `o1-pro`)
- [ ] Replace `gpt-4.1-nano` in the summarization enum, budget table, and gateway allowlist
- [ ] Remove `o4-mini` from the flex allowlists
- [ ] Plan the `gpt-5.3-codex`, `gpt-5.1`, and `gpt-5.4-nano` replacements before Apr 1, 2027
- [ ] Audit `PostHog/ai-gateway` allowlists and production config for the same ids

## Feature request

Let a user pick which model the AI detector uses (the `llm` detector type on insight alerts), per alert. Start with two models only:

| Shown as | Model id | Provider | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | `claude-haiku-5-5` | Anthropic | The default, and what every AI alert uses today |
| GPT-6 Luna | `gpt-6-luna` | OpenAI | New for this detector |

### Why

The AI detector runs on one hard-coded model, `LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"` in `products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`. A user whose metric is judged badly by that model has no second option, and we have no way to learn which model users prefer for which metrics.

#130917 proposed a model registry with shadow calls and was parked until someone asked for a per-alert model choice. This issue is that request, without the shadow part.

### Where the code is

- The judge is Anthropic-only: `build_ai_gateway_anthropic_client`, then `messages.parse(output_format=LLMDetectionVerdict)` with `thinking` disabled (`products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`).
- The chart is sent as an Anthropic base64 `image` block (`products/alerts/backend/judge/prompt.py`).
- The detector config has one field, `instructions` (`LLMDetectorConfig` in `frontend/src/queries/schema/schema-general.ts`).
- The API validates the config in `products/alerts/backend/presentation/views/alert.py`. The Max tool in `products/alerts/backend/max_tools.py` is the second writer.
- The editor renders the instructions field in `products/alerts/frontend/views/DetectorSelector.tsx`.
- Read `products/alerts/AGENTS.md` first. Its cost and gating rules all still apply.

### Proposal

**Config and API**

- [ ] Add an optional `model` to `LLMDetectorConfig`, an enum of exactly `claude-haiku-5-5` and `gpt-6-luna`. A config with no `model` means Haiku, so existing alerts need no migration and do not change behavior.
- [ ] Reject any other value with a 400 in the API validator. The Max tool goes through the same validation.
- [ ] Simulate takes the same field, so a preview runs on the model the alert will use.
- [ ] Regenerate the schema and OpenAPI types (`hogli build:openapi`), and update the MCP tool descriptions for alert create, update and simulate, plus `products/alerts/skills/authoring-insight-alerts/SKILL.md`.

**Judge**

- [ ] Replace the single constant with a small registry keyed by model id. Each entry holds the provider, how the client is built, how the chart image is encoded, and how structured output is requested and parsed into `LLMDetectionVerdict`.
- [ ] Add the OpenAI path through the AI gateway. Send the chart as an image data URL. Keep the same `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `PROMPT_REVISION` and `ai_product` (`alert_llm_detector`).
- [ ] Keep every guard on both paths: the access check, the AI credit budget check, the `X-PostHog-Billable` and `X-PostHog-Privacy-Mode` headers, the gateway credit-refusal handling, the model-call slot, the request timeout and the single in-request retry.
- [ ] The OpenAI call must be attributed and charged to the alert's team, the same as the Anthropic call is through `team_id` today.
- [ ] Use the alert's model in the verdict memo key and in `SeriesJudgment.model`, in place of the constant, so each check records the model that produced it.
- [ ] The Haiku quirks stay on the Haiku entry only (no sampling params, `thinking` disabled). Do not copy them to the OpenAI entry.

**Editor**

- [ ] Add a model select to the AI detector section, next to the instructions field. Default to Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [ ] Show the model on each AI check in the alert history, because an alert's model can change during its life.
- [ ] Follow `/writing-user-facing-copy` for the label and help text.

**Docs and rules**

- [ ] Update the comment on `LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL` and `products/alerts/AGENTS.md`, which both say the model is not exposed per alert.
- [ ] Add the cost story that `AGENTS.md` asks for: calls per check stay at one, so only the price per call changes with the model.

### Constraints

- Two models only. No free-text model id, and no frontier models.
- One model call per check, as today. No shadow call and no fallback from one model to the other. A check that cannot reach a verdict records an error.
- The feature stays behind `alerts-llm-detector`, with the same per-project cap, cadence rules and AI data processing consent check.
- The new OpenAI call site must pass `.semgrep/rules/security/` (see the OpenAI HIPAA-eligible endpoints rule).
- Changing the model on an existing alert does not clear its earlier flags. The prompt still marks the points that earlier AI checks fired on, whichever model produced them.

### Acceptance

- A new AI alert with no model chosen runs on `claude-haiku-5-5`, and an alert saved before this change behaves exactly as it did.
- An alert saved with `gpt-6-luna` is judged by that model on scheduled checks and in simulate. Its check metadata and its `$ai_generation` event both name that model.
- `detector_config: {"type": "llm", "model": "anything-else"}` is rejected on create, update and simulate.
- With the rollout flag off, or with AI credits exhausted, a `gpt-6-luna` alert pauses the same way a Haiku alert does.
- Tests cover: the default, the rejected value, the OpenAI verdict parsing, the memo key changing with the model, and the paused paths on the OpenAI entry.

### Open questions

- Does the organization's AI data processing consent already cover sending alert data to OpenAI, or does the picker need to say which provider each model uses?
- Do the two models cost a similar number of AI credits per check? If not, the editor should say so next to the select.
- Should the allowed models also be listed in the `alerts-llm-detector` flag payload, so one model can be turned off without a deploy? If so, an alert on a model that is turned off should pause (`LLMDetectorPausedError`), not be disabled.

### Out of scope

- Shadow calls and model comparison (#130917).
- A project-level or organization-level default model.
- More than two models.

## Problem

MCP Analytics can't group most tool calls from OpenAI's hosted MCP connector (`openai-mcp/1.0.0`) into conversations. That connector speaks MCP `2026-07-28`, so there is no transport session, and its agents rarely echo the `conversation_id` handle. Each call ends up as its own one-call session.

[PostHog/posthog-js#5577](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/pull/5577) reads a client's own conversation id from `_meta`. Its rules only match a `(ChatGPT)` user agent and `codex-mcp-client`, and the hosted connector sends neither. Nobody has seen what this connector does send, because the server records no `_meta` keys and no header names.

## Changes

- Every `$mcp_tool_call` now carries `mcp_request_meta_keys`, the key names in the request's `params._meta`.
- It also carries `mcp_request_header_names`, the HTTP header names on the request.
- Both hold names only, never values. A name must look like an identifier: letters, digits and `._/-`, up to 64 characters. That drops emails and `key=value` pairs.
- Each list is deduplicated, sorted, and capped at 64. Our edge proxy adds its own headers, and a lower cap pushed `x-*` names out.
- Both are non-`$` server properties, and `$session_id` resolution is unchanged.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** A parameterized case in `tool-executor-intent.test.ts` drives a real `handleToolCall`. It asserts the names, the filtering, the case with no `_meta`, and that no value reaches the event. One case in `url-routing.test.ts` covers header names. Removing the lines that emit the properties turns both red.

- Ran the hono test config and `tests/unit` locally. Two unit files didn't load because `@posthog/quill-charts` isn't built in this worktree. CI covers them.
- Not checked: real OpenAI connector traffic. Reading that is the point of this change.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `pstack:poteto-mode`, `pstack:interrogate`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** not needed

**MCP Analytics:** this adds two non-`$` diagnostic properties to `$mcp_tool_call` and uses no new SDK support. The goal is to find out which client conversation ids `posthog-js#5577` should read. The SDK's `$mcp_*` fields are untouched.

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** non-`$` names, because `$mcp_*` belongs to the SDK. Names only, so no client identifier value is stored before anyone has reviewed it.
- **Decisions:** header names come from `parseRequestProperties`, the Hono path. The legacy Workers path in `src/index.ts` is left alone, since all tool-call events come from Hono.
- **Follow-ups:** read the client's own id for `openai-mcp` once the key is known. Add that row to posthog-js#5577, bump the SDK, and pass `headers`, `clientInfo` and `requestMeta` through `PostHogMCP`.
- **Decisions:** the pre-PR gate (Opus and Sonnet adversaries) showed that a 32-name cap dropped `x-*` headers behind the proxy, and that the first filter let value-shaped names through. Both are fixed.
- **Read closely:** `observedNames` in `src/lib/request-properties.ts`.

</details>
