## Problem

Analysts must rerun a notebook and click **Replace rows** before downstream SQL sees fresh results. [#140517](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140517)

## Changes

An agent can now run a notebook between SQL models in PostHog’s warehouse DAG. For example, SQL totals sales, Python forecasts demand, and SQL lists items to reorder.

- **Declare** a table from a SQL or Python cell and name its upstream models.
- **Refresh** daily or on demand. Each run publishes the cell’s full dataframe.
- **Inspect** failed cells and the last published run. A failed refresh preserves the table and skips dependent SQL.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Run notebook] --> B[Save or replace rows in browser] --> C[Warehouse table]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[SQL model: total sales by item] --> B[Notebook Python cell: forecast demand] --> C[demand_forecast table] --> D[SQL model: list items to reorder]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A,D phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

<details>
<summary>Using the three MCP tools</summary>

Enable `notebook-warehouse-models` for MCP after the Django routes deploy.

| Tool | How to use it for the reorder report |
| --- | --- |
| `notebooks-declare-warehouse-model` | Choose the forecast cell, name its table `demand_forecast`, and pass the sales model’s node ID as an upstream dependency. |
| `notebooks-run-warehouse-model` | Start the model and its upstream dependencies now. After the first publication, reference `demand_forecast` in the downstream SQL model. |
| `notebooks-warehouse-model-status` | Pass the returned `dag_run_id` to see whether the run reached the notebook. Inspect cell errors and the run that produced the current table. |

Each run executes the saved notebook through the selected cell. First publication requires an unused table name. Later refreshes keep the table ID. Runs that share a notebook wait their turn, and previous generations remain readable for 24 hours.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** [Warehouse tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/posthog/api/test/notebooks/test_warehouse_model.py#L217) cover replacement. [DAG tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/products/data_modeling/backend/temporal/tests/test_execute_dag_workflow.py#L635) cover failure propagation.

<details>
<summary>CI advisories and regression coverage</summary>

The warehouse round trip read 14,000 synthetic rows on each of two refreshes. A failed third refresh preserved the second table. A local Temporal test used a stub notebook task to check dependency ordering.

The API test checks that the returned ticket identifies the queued Temporal run and that polling uses the same project, node, and ticket. The workflow tests exercise the receiver. Time-skipping tests cover a busy notebook, downstream failure, and delayed cleanup. A warehouse round trip reads both generations across replacement.

CI measured a 7.7 KiB decrease in total frontend bundle size. Of the two eager roots over budget, logged-out boot had zero growth and the authenticated shell grew 3.5 KiB against the CI baseline. The frontend diff only regenerates the notebook API. No browser code imports the new client functions or schemas. CI also shows changes in the Today sidebar chunks, outside this diff.

The database migration creates one table with a primary key on `node_id`, its node foreign key, and an index on `team_id`. The migration analyzer classified it as safe. Five Chromium cases passed on retry. Two exercise editing or deleting an ordinary notebook. The other three cover person properties, insight titles, and workflow secrets. None of the five exercises model declaration, DAG execution, or warehouse publication.

</details>

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

[Warehouse modeling guide](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/docs/published/handbook/engineering/data-warehouse.md#L117)

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** OpenAI Codex, GPT-6

**Skills:** `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/implementing-mcp-tools`, `/django-migrations`, `/writing-tests`, `/verifying-changes`, `/writing-dataclasses`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/run-posthog`, `/writing-clickhouse-queries`, `/isolating-product-facade-contracts`, `/running-ci-preflight`, `/debugging-ci-failures`, `/security-audit`, `/querying-local-postgres`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** Model declarations pin the selected cells and variables. Edits require redeclaration.
- **Read closely:** Publication checks author access again and serializes competing table replacements.
- **Verification:** Automated tests used generated inventory rows and local services. Production sandbox execution is unverified.

</details>

## Problem

The activity summary MVP (#119839, #119919, shipped in #119884 and #120034) runs as an offline Dagster job over PostHog's own analytics data. It showed the summaries and their cost are workable, but it cannot become the feature:

- Its MCP input exists only as usage events in one internal analytics project, so it cannot run in-region for any other project.
- It stores summaries as Parquet partitions, not as state a product surface can read or update.
- It cannot run in a local dev stack, so iterating on the filters and the prompt needs a prod run.

The next step builds the core of the feature inside the signals product: one stored summary per (project, user), updated from in-region data, runnable locally from a command.

## Changes

New package `products/signals/backend/activity_summary/`. No new product. No schedule, endpoint or MCP tool in this issue.

### 1. Move the reusable code, then retire the Dagster package

Move these from `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary/` into the new package: `render.py` and `prompt.py`, the `summarize` and `cost_usd` logic from `summaries.py`, and the input readers `member_tasks` and `member_activity` (with `TASK_ORIGIN_PRODUCTS`) from `dag.py`.

Then delete the Dagster activity summary pipeline. It was an offline MVP, and this package replaces it:

- the `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary/` package, including its MCP event queries, the cost projection, and the summaries and embeddings assets
- the `activity_summary_job` and `activity_summary_schedule` registration in `posthog/dags/locations/signals.py`
- the activity summary section of `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/README.md`
- `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/tests/test_activity_summary.py`, after moving the tests that cover the moved code into the new package

The MCP-specific rendering (`McpCall`, `McpSession`, `mcp_unit`, `job_intents` and the MCP drop rules) has no caller once the Dagster package is gone, so drop it too. Git history keeps it for when an in-region MCP source exists. Leave the Parquet partitions the job already wrote in object storage as they are.

### 2. Inputs: tasks and the activity log, in-region only

For one (team, user) and a time window:

- **Tasks:** `list_user_task_summaries` from `products/tasks/backend/facade/user_task_summaries.py`, with the origin products and drop rules the Dagster inputs already use.
- **Activity log:** `ActivityLog` rows for the user in the team, with the existing filters (no `is_system`, no impersonated rows, no `scout:` clients, the tag and auto-named drops).
  - Also read the agent intent at `detail.trigger.payload.intent`. Since #100741 the MCP server sends it with every write it makes, and the activity log stores it on the row. Render it next to the changed object, for example `updated insight "Signup funnel" (agent: <intent>)`, through the same `clean_text` and per-line caps as other free text.
- **No MCP usage events.** Read-only MCP sessions stay out until an in-region source exists.

### 3. Hardening, applied in the moved code

1. **Redact URLs to their host.** `clean_text` strips query strings and fragments, but a secret can sit in a URL path. Replace every full URL with its host, for example `[link example.com]`. Add an invented path secret to the golden fixtures for each input source.
2. **Cap the completion.** Set `max_completion_tokens` from a named constant (around 600). Treat a truncated answer (`finish_reason == "length"`) as malformed, so the existing retry and `failed` paths handle it. Also cap the length of each focus area topic, product and `recent_shift` in `normalize_summary`.
3. **Unknown usage is null, not zero.** When a response has no `usage`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out` and `cost_usd` are null.

### 4. Model

`UserActivitySummary` in the signals models, team-scoped with `TeamScopedRootMixin`, unique on (team, user). Follow `/django-migrations`.

- **Output:** `summary` (JSON), `summary_text`, `generated_at`, `model`, `prompt_version`, `render_version`
- **Accounting:** `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cost_usd` (all nullable), `inputs_used` (JSON: line counts per section and drop counts per rule)
- **State:** `status` (`ok`, `failed`), `input_watermark` (the newest input timestamp included), `next_eligible_at`
- **Cascades:** deleting the user or the team deletes the row.

No embedding column and no version table in this issue.

### 5. `update_activity_summary(team_id, user_id, *, dry_run=False)`

One update for one (team, user). A command, a later Temporal workflow and the tests can all call it.

1. Skip if the organization has not approved AI data processing, or if `next_eligible_at` is in the future (unless forced).
2. Gather inputs since `input_watermark`. On a first run, gather the last 28 days.
3. If fewer than `MIN_UNITS` (3) units survive the filters, stop and write nothing.
4. Render the input and call the model once through `build_openai_client(product="signals", ai_product="activity_summary", ...)` from `posthog/llm/gateway_client.py`, with the stored summary as the previous summary. Model `gpt-6-luna`. Pass a fixed pipeline distinct id as both `distinct_id` and `user=`. Do not set `$ai_`-prefixed property keys.
5. On success, save the output and accounting, advance `input_watermark`, and set `next_eligible_at` to one day later. On failure, set `status = failed`, record the error, and leave the stored summary and the watermark unchanged.
6. Return a frozen result with the rendered input, the summary, the accounting and the drop counts.

With `dry_run=True`, nothing is written.

### 6. Management command

`run_activity_summary --team-id N --user-id N [--dry-run] [--force]`. It prints the rendered input, the summary, the token counts, the cost and the drop counts per rule. This is the local dogfood loop for the filters and the prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- The golden-fixture tests for the task and activity log drop rules and rendering move with the code and still pass.
- The Dagster activity summary package, its job and schedule, and its README section are gone. Nothing imports from `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary`, and `check-dagster-paths.py` passes.
- New tests, with the LLM mocked at the boundary (follow `/writing-tests`):
  - a secret in a URL path never reaches the rendered input
  - a truncated completion is retried, then recorded as `failed`
  - missing usage gives null tokens and cost
  - an activity log row with an agent intent renders it, and one without an intent renders as before
  - fewer than `MIN_UNITS` units writes nothing
  - a successful update advances the watermark, and a failed one does not
  - `dry_run` writes nothing
- The command runs against a local dev stack with a configured gateway.
- No text other than the rendered input reaches the model.

## Out of scope

The daily schedule and per-user workflow, the feature flag, embeddings, the `activity summary generated` event, the read endpoint, the MCP tool, opt-out, and an in-region source for read-only MCP sessions. These are follow-up issues.

## Problem

The MCP Analytics "Intent clustering" tab shows two views, four scorecards, a list and detail split, a Sankey, a pivot table, a scatter and an overlap table, all from one sampled snapshot with no time dimension. A server owner who wants to know what agents use a tool for, whether that use is focused, where it drifts and what the outliers are, has to read all of that and still cannot see change over time. The product owner asked to condense intents to a few things with a drill-down, and to picture them as a 2D map with density per topic and the intents inside on zoom.

## Changes

Fifth layer of the intent topics stack, on top of the query layer. Everything is behind the new `mcp-analytics-intent-topics` flag; the legacy tab and its flag are untouched until the cutover PR.

- **Dashboard card "What agents use your server for"**: the top five intent topics with share of intent-carrying calls, a change arrow versus the previous window, coverage, and a link into the map. Toggleable like the other cards.
- **Tool page section "How this tool is used"**: exactly four cards. Focus (score, band and coverage), Top topics (share, trend and a calls-per-day sparkline, each linking to the map for that tool and topic), Drift (new, growing, shrinking and gone topics as chips) and Outliers (intents outside every topic). Follows the page's date range.
- **Intent map scene** at `/mcp-analytics/intents`, reached from the card and the tool page, not a top tab. Topic bubbles sized by calls at the base zoom; clicking a bubble narrows the map to that topic's intents; dragging an area pins the axes and loads up to 5,000 intents inside it; double-click resets. The right panel lists topics as a legend, or the selected topic's summary and its intents in view, most called first, with tool links and outlier tags. Date range, tool and topic ride in the URL.
- Links into the map keep the selected date range. The map sends no query with the flag off, shows a failed load apart from an empty map with a retry, and lists a topic's intents 50 at a time. The dashboard card shows a failed load with a retry. Refresh waits for the intent loaders.
- The map and the dashboard card load once when the flag arrives after the scene mounts.
- Scene, route and URL helper registered in the product manifest; new `FEATURE_FLAGS.MCP_ANALYTICS_INTENT_TOPICS`; product analytics events for map opens and topic selections.
- Mechanical: regenerated product scene registry, story mocks for the new query kinds.

Why: this is the condensed intent experience the owner asked for. The map reuses the `@posthog/quill-charts` scatter chart that the AI observability clusters view already uses; convex hulls and density shading are a follow-up.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** The regressions are a map that loads with the wrong filters or limit, a URL that does not round-trip, bubbles or points grouped under the wrong series, and a tool page that fires the profile query without the flag. No existing test covers the map. Added `intentScatter.test.ts` (bubble radius bounds, one bubble per topic with meta, points grouped by topic with outlier crosses and unassigned grey), `intentMapLogic.test.ts` (URL to state and a single load, series and selected-topic selectors, drag zoom reloads with bounds and the larger limit, narrowing to a topic clears the zoom and updates the URL) and two cases in `mcpAnalyticsToolDetailLogic.test.ts` (profile loads only with the flag). Stories: `ToolDetailWithIntentTopics`, `IntentTopicsCard` on the dashboard, and three intent map stories (overview, one topic, flag off).

Ran locally: jest for `products/mcp_analytics/frontend` and the frontend TypeScript check. Not done: rendering the new error and paging states in a browser; they are covered by the logic tests and a new `IntentMapLoadFailed` story. The screenshots below come from a local real stack (synthetic data) after the review and scale fixes; since then only the invisible ph-no-capture classes changed in the intent UI.

<details>
<summary>CI report review</summary>

- The duplication warning matches the product manifest and its generated `products.tsx` projection; both copies are required by generated-file validation.
- The existing `insightNew`, dashboard activity mapper, and `StatTiles` complexity is unchanged.
- The remaining complexity preserves explicit query mocks, flag/loading guards, and atomic URL filter hydration; no behavior change is warranted by these warnings.
- The new map uses a dynamic import. The additional 30.7 KiB of built JavaScript implements the map, tool profile, and dashboard card.
- Shared-shell growth is 828 B against an already exceeded budget. This review retains the feature registration and does not increase budgets.
- The backend coverage gaps belong to lower stack layers; this layer changes no backend code.
- The MCP schema snapshot only adds `/mcp-analytics/intents` to the canonical route list.
- The reported Playwright flakes cover experiments and person properties, outside this layer.

The [Storybook run](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/actions/runs/43554094388) requires review of 16 changed intent-topic snapshots. The baseline remains unchanged pending visual approval.

</details>

### Blast radius checks

- **Flag-gated UI:** every entry point (the map scene, the dashboard card and the tool detail section) checks `mcp-analytics-intent-topics`, which is not set, so nothing renders and no new query runs.
- **Checks:** the TypeScript check, the MCP Analytics jest suites, the app URL manifest check and all MCP unit tests pass.

## Scale test (41M intents, synthetic, local ClickHouse, 2 threads)

The data is synthetic: 41.0M intent vectors (256 dims, 200 well-separated topic centroids) written straight into the 256-dimension table, plus the hourly rollup and 130k `$mcp_tool_call` events for one hour. The functions under test are the real ones: assign, the daily rebuild, the query runners, the corpus reads, the fit sample and UMAP/HDBSCAN. Locally the topic labeler sent the same prompt and schema to OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` instead of Gemini, because there is no Gemini key or AI gateway in the local stack. ClickHouse 26.9.5 ran on one node: an 11 GiB / 8 CPU container, a 9.31 GiB per-query limit, and `max_threads=2` from the dev users.xml unless noted.

| path (41.0M intents, 30-day window) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| post-refit assign (`run_assign`, 200 topics) | OOM at 9.3 GiB | 41.0M assigned in 32 per-day slices, max 0.96 GiB per insert, 605 s for the whole run (including the 90 s daily rebuild) |
| dashboard card | 4.4 s, 3.41 GB | 1.8 s, 124 MB |
| tool profile | 10.7 s, 1.89 GB | 11.7-20.4 s, **5.2 GB** (heavier: the outliers now go through the same bounded ranking as the map) |
| intent map, base view (limit 2,000) | OOM ("couldn't load") | loads in about **57 s**, 5.2 GB |
| intent map, drag zoom (limit 5,000) | OOM | **hits the 60 s HogQL limit with 2 threads**; with 8 threads it loads in 43-54 s, 5.5 GB |
| refit sample (`fetch_fit_sample`, 7 days) | OOM | 39 s, 20,000 sampled, 3.4 GB |
| hourly sync seen-hash lookup | 6 full scans of the 41M-row table per hour (246M rows read) | one 50k-hash chunk per page, so about 5x fewer scans. `cityHash64(document_id) IN (...)` was measured and does not prune here: an hour's hashes hit every granule. |

What this means: nothing runs out of memory at 41M any more, but the map is close to the 60 s limit at this size on a small node. More threads barely help, because aggregating 41M intents and the join dominate. The next step would be a per-intent daily rollup so the map reads days instead of hours. Fix commits: #120749 `e4f75db4` (assign slices) and `adbd0e4a` (seen hashes); #120764 `4fe0c39b` (refit sample) and `94fe9ed4` (map and dashboard reads); this PR `51ea81fc` (duplicate date range, low-contrast tags).

**Monthly cost (estimates, project 2 scale):**
- OpenAI embeddings: 1.36M new intents/day x ~20 tokens x $0.02 p

## Changes

## How did you test this code?

- Both test files pass locally against Postgres and ClickHouse.
- Without the fix, both new tests fail on the time.
- Measured after opening, on a local build with real OpenAI calls through the planner and Trends generator chains: a repeat planner call in a conversation is 85,773 input tokens, with 0 cached before the fix and 85,630 after; a repeat generator call goes from 21,120 to 25,216 cached of 26,091.
- Not run: PostHog AI evals, or anything on production traffic.

**Test rationale:** the new tests require identical `instructions` at two frozen times. `test_responses_api_instruction_enrichment` misses these callers.

## Release status

## Problem

Warehouse table enrichment reports a new error tracking exception each time it runs for a deactivated organization. The LLM gateway refuses the call with HTTP 402. No retry can change that, and the sync already recovers with a `partial` status. The exception is noise for the owning team.

Report: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/01a2100d-ca6a-768c-8656-245f06b33728

## Changes

- `enrich_table_semantics_sync` skips a team whose organization is deactivated, before it calls the gateway. The status is `skipped` and the reason is `organization_inactive`. A sync after reactivation enriches the table.
- A 402 that the gateway marks with `X-PostHog-Denial` (for example, an organization deactivated during the run) returns `partial` with `llm_payment_required` and does not call `capture_exception`. This is the same handling as `GatewayNotConfiguredError`.
- A 402 without that header is the provider refusing the gateway's account, which affects every team. It still goes to error tracking, as do other errors such as a 500. Alerts, error tracking and workflows use the same header check.
- The team lookup now loads `organization__is_active`.

## How did you test this code?

- Extended the existing skip test, now `test_skipped_when_organization_blocks_llm_calls`, with a case for a deactivated organization.
- Added `test_gateway_payment_refusal_is_not_reported_as_a_failure`, with Anthropic and OpenAI cases: a marked 402 (not reported), an unmarked 402 (still reported) and a 500 (still reported).
- Both new cases fail on the old code: it has no deactivation check, and it calls `capture_exception` for every error.
- Ran test collection, `ruff check` and `ruff format`, plus a direct check of `_is_payment_required`. The DB-backed tests were not run locally, so CI runs them.

**Test rationale:** Guards against two regressions: a deactivated organization reaching the gateway, and a gateway 402 reaching error tracking. The closest existing test, `test_unconfigured_gateway_is_not_reported_as_a_failure`, covers only a missing gateway.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## Notes for reviewers

- Security review: not needed.
- Read closely: the `_is_payment_required` branch in the generic `except Exception` block in `enrich_table_semantics.py`.
- No open PR fixes the same problem.

---


## Problem

A model's adapter, name, reasoning efforts and cost are typed by hand in the task model catalog. Every new version also needs a catalog row before a product can call it or a picker can offer it. The gateway already serves all of this, and the copies have drifted ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C1T3V1RJA/p1795056481045999), #132210).

## Changes

- The backend reads a model's adapter, name, reasoning efforts and cost multiplier from its gateway row. It reads no catalog row.
- Each agent product names the model families it allows. Its token pin is every version the gateway lists in those families, and its pickers offer the two newest of each.
- A short reserved list holds the exceptions: a trial model, and ids kept for the free tier and older desktop builds. No picker offers one.
- A row that says nothing about reasoning gets no effort picker, and an effort sent for it isn't refused. The gateway lists no reasoning for GLM-5.2 or GLM-5.3 Flash, and shipped desktop builds send efforts for both.
- While the listing can't be read, a family product's token mint fails as retryable. A workflow step is checked against every model its token admits.
- A live run keeps to the versions its token was minted with.
- Rollout flags are keyed by gateway family. Workflows and the run command's model switch now check them too.

Visible: backend pickers lose GPT-5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Fable 5. Tokens can still call them, and also the older `gpt` versions the gateway lists (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2). GPT-5.6 cost multipliers drop. The Codex slider rungs move to GPT-6.2 Sol. The fixed pins for onboarding, conversations and the free tier are unchanged.

Trade-off: a trial model the gateway lists in an allowed family is admitted for every agent product unless it's reserved first.

This PR now includes #139330, which is closed.

## How did you test this code?

Every backend test gets a saved copy of the production listing. A snapshot records what each product's token may call and what its picker offers. Table tests cover the adapter rule, partial rows, the three reasoning states, the family rule, reservations, the run stamp, the flag checks and a listing outage at mint. The call assertions the CI report counts read the request sent to the gateway's token endpoint. Not done: a cold cloud start.

CI report: its TypeScript duplicate is two generated OAuth scope files this PR doesn't touch. The only shipped web change here is four model id strings, so the bundle delta, the eager graph delta and the two flaky Playwright tests (login, person properties) don't come from this diff.

Implement a `forecast(vals, steps)` function in HogQL that does N `steps` of forecasting given a timeseries in vals (array of values).

From that it returns a 3-tuple `Tuple(p10 Array(Float64), p50 Array(Float64), p90 Array(Float64))` with the p10, p50 and p90 timeseries.

This should enable adding forecasting to any timeseries plot we have in posthog.

It is gated behind a feature flag and it only support Clickhouse for now since it relies on enriching the data on our side then sending it back to clickhouse by creating a temporary table.

The current implementation is not ideal since it runs the model in CPU in memory, but it's a very tiny model that runs in 15ms in CPU and uses around 200MB of memory so for some internal testing it should be fine. If we want to productize we could move it to some dedicated instances.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

DeepSeek isn't available as a provider in the LLM analytics Playground. Users who have a DeepSeek account and credits can't add their DeepSeek API key directly — the Playground supports OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, Fireworks, and Together AI, but not DeepSeek. DeepSeek models can only be reached indirectly by adding a third-party aggregator key (OpenRouter, Fireworks, Together AI) and picking a DeepSeek model from that provider's list, which bills through the aggregator rather than DeepSeek and means existing DeepSeek credits can't be used.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add DeepSeek as a first-class bring-your-own-key provider in the Playground, pointed at DeepSeek's first-party API. Users would add a DeepSeek API key under Settings → AI Observability and select DeepSeek models (e.g. `deepseek-chat`, `deepseek-reasoner`) directly. DeepSeek's API is OpenAI-compatible, so it should fit the existing provider pattern. Built-in, PostHog-funded access (as exists for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google) would be a nice-to-have but is secondary to having direct BYOK.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- BYOK via an aggregator (OpenRouter, Fireworks, Together AI) surfaces DeepSeek models today, but routes and bills through a third party rather than DeepSeek directly, so it doesn't help users who want to use their own DeepSeek credits.
- Generic custom OpenAI-compatible provider support (a configurable base URL with `/models` discovery) would also solve this and cover other providers at once — see #54854. A dedicated DeepSeek provider gives first-class treatment; the custom base URL would be the more general fix.

## Additional context

DeepSeek already appears in PostHog's LLM cost-tracking data and there's a DeepSeek AI observability install guide, so model/cost normalization for DeepSeek is partly in place. Related provider request: MiniMax #66109.

### Bug Description



`$ai_generation` events for OpenAI's `gpt-image-2` get no cost: `$ai_total_cost_usd` is 0 and `$ai_cost_model_source` is empty.

The model is served only on the image endpoints (`/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`), so it is not in the OpenRouter catalog that `llm-costs.json` is generated from. The manual list in `nodejs/src/ingestion/pipelines/ai/costs/providers/manual-providers.ts` has no entry either. The only related row is OpenRouter's `openai/gpt-5.4-image-2`, which is a chat model, not `gpt-image-2`.

**Expected**

A manual entry using OpenAI's standard rates (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), in USD per token:

| | Rate |
|---|---|
| Text input (`prompt_token`) | 0.000005 |
| Cached input (`cache_read_token`) | 0.00000125 (cached image input is 0.000002) |
| Image input (`image`) | 0.000008 |
| Image output (`image_output`) | 0.00003 |

The model has no text output, so `completion_token` could use the image output rate. Output is then priced correctly when no modality breakdown is sent. The entry should cover the dated snapshot `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21` as well.

**Fix**

I've prepared the entry with ingestion tests, following the Gemini TTS entries, on a fork. Opening a pull request failed with "must be a collaborator":
https://github.com/michidk-contrib/posthog/commit/5b6d1ece9d585527b509c31fc8847ca0ff91ac7e

The tests run `processCost` for `gpt-image-2`, `openai/gpt-image-2` and the snapshot. They fail without the entry and pass with it. Feel free to take the commit over.

**Debug info**

Self-reported events from our own OpenAI-compatible gateway. The model is sent as `codex/gpt-image-2`, which already resolves to `gpt-image-2` once the provider prefix is stripped.

_This issue and the fix were prepared with an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Opus 5.5). The rates come from OpenAI's pricing page linked above._

## Problem

## Changes

- Capacity refusals stop immediate retries and let the team's remaining insights warm.
- Uncovered failures reuse the existing failure cache with separate warming-only history: two failures start a 2-hour wait, doubling to 8 hours.
- Query-breaker failures retain their existing cooldown and foreground recovery, without a second cooldown or counting replays as executions.
- Mechanical: remove the independent backoff implementation and extract unchanged error reporting.

Warming-only failures share the existing backoff machinery while keeping their history separate.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Before: failed warm] --> B[Query breaker]
    A --> C[Uncovered failure retried next hour]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    class A phYellow;
    class B,C phBlue;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[After: failed warm] --> B[Covered: existing query breaker]
    A --> C[Uncovered: warming-only failure cache]
    B --> D[Shared failure-cache implementation]
    C --> D
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phYellow;
    class B,C phBlue;
    class D phGray;
```

## How did you test this code?

- **Test rationale:** extend warming tests to catch overlapping cooldowns; verify backoff expiry, reset, and isolation through the failure cache.

- CI report: four counted comment lines move unchanged with error reporting. The remaining comments explain capacity retry policy and failure-history isolation, so they remain.

## Problem

Error tracking alerts created by #137235 never send because nothing evaluates them.

## Changes

- Enabled alerts announce matching new, reopened, and assigned issues.
- Product-owned Temporal registration preserves master's discovery. A concurrent index bounds change reads.
- Mechanical: rebase the migration to `0055` and regenerate the workflow catalog.

The platform tick now includes error tracking evaluation.

Before:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Tick[Platform tick] --> Sources[Other source evaluators]
  Sources --> Record[Record outcomes]
  Record --> Delivery[Deliver notifications]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  class Tick,Delivery phYellow;
  class Sources,Record phBlue;
```

After:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Tick[Platform tick] --> Sources[Other source evaluators]
  Tick --> ET[Error tracking evaluator]
  ET --> Changes[Issue change log]
  Sources --> Record[Record outcomes]
  ET --> Record
  Record --> Delivery[Deliver notifications]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  class Tick,Delivery phYellow;
  class Sources,ET,Record phBlue;
  class Changes phGray;
```

<details>
<summary>Evaluation details</summary>

- Checks read from the previous reading check's due time, with a 60-second settle margin and a 24-hour catch-up limit. The window reaches back over failed checks and over quiet hours, which the platform does not schedule, so a change made during either is announced at the next check.
- A failed read is recorded, so a failing alert goes ERRORED, then BROKEN.
- Messages link the issue by fingerprint, so the link survives a merge.
- Each tick starts at a different check, so one slow alert cannot starve the rest of its batch.
- Native filters fail closed when manual changes lack exception properties.
- Bulk actions announce nothing. Issues without new changes resolve silently, allowing later changes to notify again.
- Workflow `error-tracking-alert-evaluate` runs on the platform evaluation queue through the product declaration.

</details>

**Test rationale:** New evaluation tests fail on the previous head: a failed read recorded and read again at the next check, quiet hours deferring changes to the first check after them, an edit off the minute, and the fingerprint link. Existing evaluation and registration tests cover the rest.

Thanks for building AI Observability in the open — the OTLP path is great.

**TL;DR:** Spans from `openinference-instrumentation-*` are **accepted** by the OTel endpoint (HTTP 2xx) but **never appear as generations** in LLM observability. Root cause: PostHog classifies a span as a generation via **`gen_ai.operation.name`**, which OpenInference doesn't emit — it uses `openinference.span.kind=LLM` + `llm.*`. So OpenInference users see nothing, with no error. Is OpenInference support something you'd take? I have a minimal repro + a full mapping and would be glad to contribute.

## Reproduction

A script sends two spans over OTLP to PostHog and logs each span's export result:

1. **control** — a `gen_ai.*` span with `gen_ai.operation.name=chat` (+ model, messages, tokens).
2. **OpenInference** — a live OpenAI call wrapped by `openinference-instrumentation-openai` (emits `llm.*` / `openinference.span.kind=LLM`).

Observed against a PostHog US cloud project:

```text
[export] span='gen_ai.control'   result=SUCCESS
[export] span='ChatCompletion'   result=SUCCESS      # the OpenInference span — accepted
```

- **control** → surfaces as a fully populated generation (model `gpt-4o-mini`, messages, 8/1 tokens, cost).
- **ChatCompletion (OpenInference)** → **does not surface as a generation at all**, despite `result=SUCCESS`.

So the span is accepted, then silently dropped from LLM observability. Minimal setup:

```python
# openinference-instrumentation-openai  →  OTLP  →  PostHog
OpenAIInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
OpenAI().chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one word."}],
)
# endpoint: https://us.i.posthog.com/i/v0/ai/otel   header: Authorization: Bearer <project API key>
```

## Root cause

Per the [OTel ingestion docs](https://posthog.com/docs/ai-observability/installation/opentelemetry), `gen_ai.operation.name=chat` is what classifies a span as an `$ai_generation`, and the processor forwards spans whose keys start with `gen_ai.` / `llm.` / `ai.` / `traceloop.`. OpenInference spans pass the *forwarding* filter (they carry `llm.*`) but are never *classified* as generations, because they don't set `gen_ai.operation.name`. Even past classification, the attribute shapes differ:

| OpenInference (emitted) | gen_ai.* PostHog maps | → |
|---|---|---|
| *(no operation marker)* | `gen_ai.operation.name=chat` | classifies as `$ai_generation` |
| `llm.model_name` | `gen_ai.response.model` | `$ai_model` |
| `llm.input_messages.*` / `llm.output_messages.*` | `gen_ai.input.messages` / `gen_ai.output.messages` | `$ai_input` / `$ai_output_choices` |
| `llm.token_count.prompt` / `.completion` | `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` / `output_tokens` | `$ai_input_tokens` / `$ai_output_tokens` |
| `openinference.span.kind=LLM` | *(no equivalent)* | — |

## Questions

1. Is OpenInference support something you'd want in AI Observability?
2. If so, where best — teach the span processor to recognize `openinference.span.kind` and map `llm.*`, or a separate adapter?
3. Anything in flight (e.g. the `ai_events` trace-storage work) I should know about first?

## Offer

I've mapped the full OpenInference surface (LLM, embeddings, tools, retrieval) → `$ai_*` against the [OpenInference spec](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/blob/main/spec/semantic_conventions.md) and PostHog's [`$ai_*` schema](https://posthog.com/docs/ai-observability/generations), plus a runnable repro and tests. Glad to open a PR in whatever shape you prefer.

Thanks!

### Bug Description

The query planner and the schema generators put the current time, to the second, ahead of their static prompt, because they don't pass `conversation_start_dt` (the root agent does). 1. Local build with real OpenAI calls through the planner and Trends generator.
2. Make 2 calls in one conversation.
3. Compare `cached_tokens` on the repeat call: planner 0 of 85,773, Trends generator 21,120 of 26,091.

Fix in #132240: with it, the same repeat calls cache 85,630 and 25,216.

```shell
- [x] Local build at 1ae146752f24592906cae6e8dd317d8eb369c5c6, not PostHog Cloud
```

## Problem

MCP Analytics wants to embed every distinct agent intent (tens of millions of short strings per quarter for the largest project). The two existing embedding model tables store 1536 or 3072 Float64 values per row behind in-memory HNSW indexes, so that volume would not fit. The embedding worker also had no way to ask OpenAI for a narrower vector.

## Changes

- New embedding model `text-embedding-3-small-256`: `text-embedding-3-small` served at 256 dimensions through the OpenAI `dimensions` parameter. The Rust worker change moved to #121286, so this PR stays in the Python lane.
- New ClickHouse model tables (sharded, distributed, writable, MV) created by migration `0387_embedding_model_small_256`. The table keeps rows for one month and has no vector similarity index on purpose. `ModelTableDefinitions` gains `ttl` and `vector_index` options; the first-generation tables are unchanged.
- Deployed cloud ingestion stays running during 0387. The WarpStream MV already writes every model to the buffer, and the new model MV reads the buffer as soon as it exists. Outside deployed cloud, 0387 pauses and resumes the Kafka-to-buffer MV as 0191 does.
- `DOCUMENT_EMBEDDINGS_WS_MV_SQL` now targets the buffer by default. The old default, the legacy writable table, forwards to a sharded table that deployed cloud does not have. A migration that recreated the WarpStream MV from it would stop the consumer for every embedding model.
- The union view builder takes the list of model tables. Migration 0191 passes the first-generation tables only, so a replay on a fresh database works, and 0387 recreates the view with both sets.
- The new tables are declared in the ClickHouse HCL schema, and `EmbeddingModelName` in the query schema has the new name.
- 0387 replaces the union view in one statement (`CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`), so `document_embeddings` with `model_name = 'text-embedding-3-small-256'` routes to the new table.
- Mechanical: schema snapshots for the four new tables.

> [!WARNING]
> Deploy 0387 before the intent topics pipeline flag is on. Nothing emits `text-embedding-3-small-256` before then, so no rows reach the buffer before the new model MV exists.

Node roles follow the newest migration for this table family (0191). The live ingestion layout (WarpStream MV writes to the buffer, no Kafka-to-buffer MV) comes from a review check of dev, prod-us and prod-eu. The prod HCL goldens agree on the data side. This sandbox has no ClickHouse access.

Why: first layer of the MCP Analytics intent topics work, which embeds every tool intent and clusters all of them. Raised in #mcp-analytics.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** The regression is a model name that the worker, the Python table registry and the HogQL router disagree on. Closest existing tests: `test_escape_input` in `embeddings.rs` and `TestDocumentEmbeddingsOrderByPushdown`. Added unit tests at each layer: Rust serde round trip and request body with `dimensions: 256` (and none for the full-size models), Python table SQL (one-month TTL, no index SQL, first-generation tables unchanged, union view drop helper), and a HogQL routing test for the new model name. `test_migration_0387_leaves_deployed_cloud_ingestion_running` fails if 0387 runs any statement off the data nodes in US, EU or DEV. `test_migration_0247_points_the_warpstream_mv_at_the_buffer` fails if the WarpStream MV default target moves off the buffer.

Ran locally: `hogli test products/error_tracking/backend/tests/test_indexed_embedding.py posthog/hogql/database/schema/test/test_document_embeddings.py posthog/clickhouse/test/test_schema.py`. Migration 0387 was not run on a live cluster. The checks below replay it against the production ingestion topology instead.

### Blast radius checks

- **Migration 0387 against the production ingestion topology.** I rebuilt the embeddings path from the repo's own SQL: a WarpStream Kafka table whose MV writes to the buffer, as on the live clusters. Then I ran 0387's real operations, twice:
  - In cloud mode it runs five statements, and none touches ingestion. The WarpStream MV definition is byte-identical afterwards.
  - Kafka messages for the 1536, 3072 and 256 models each land in their own table only, and in the union view.
  - No consumer reports an exception.
- **The same check with the MSK Kafka table and the pause/resume path (local and hobby):** same result.
- **Native-JSON events schema leg:** HogQL, query runner, error tracking and Signals suites. Every local failure also fails on master at the merge base.
- **Code that walks every model:** Signals uses `SIGNALS_EMBEDDING_MODELS`, and error tracking looks model tables up by name. No other code iterates every embedding model.
- **Rollback:** drop `posthog_document_embeddings_text_embedding_3_small_256_mv` first, since no other model reads it. Then replace the union view with the first-generation models, and drop the three 256 tables.

## Dev testing (screenshots)

Dev stack in the task sandbox, team 1 (Hogflix demo). Data: the `seed_mcp_sessions` command plus a dev corpus of 2,435 extra tool calls with 292 distinct intents over 16 days, including a unicode intent, a 2,097-character intent, off-topic outliers, a topic family that only exists in the previous week and one that only exists in the last week. The sandbox cannot reach OpenAI or Gemini, so the embedding worker was replaced by a local hashed bag-of-words embedder writing straight into the 256-dimension table, and the labeler by a stub that names a topic after its most common words (labels start with `[dev stub]`). Everything else is the real code path.

![the 256-dimension model table in the dev ClickHouse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/7460315a05b41f3c56e53ea03f69359d341e953e/2026/10/71dbdd32-7bdc-406f-85a7-08b53cd782ae.png)

What the image shows, top to bottom:
- The sharded table carries `CONSTRAINT embedding_dimension_check CHECK length(embedding) = 256`, a one-month TTL, and only the Kafka timestamp index. The two first-generation tables keep their three-month TTL and both HNSW indexes.
- Edge case: inserting a 1,536-value vector into the 256 table is rejected by the constraint.
- 307 intent vectors landed in the new table through the union view, all 256 wide; `model_name` is added back by the view.
- Edge case: HogQL routes `document_embeddings WHERE model_name = 'text-embedding-3-small-256'` to the new distributed table, and a query without `model_name` is refused as before.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None. The feature is behind a flag; docs follow the rollout.

- No duplicate: an open PR search for "intent topics" finds only this stack.

hits.body:
## Problem

Scout runs on the OpenAI flex queue have no fallback when OpenAI refuses flex capacity. The refusal arrives in-band: HTTP 200, the Responses preamble, then an error frame and the stream closes. Codex retries the same flex request a few times within seconds, then ends the turn with `stopReason: refusal`, and the harness does not retry the turn. The run fails, the scout waits for its next slot, and the failure counts toward the `repeated_failures` auto-pause.

This bit twice in two weeks: a sol flex canary lost a large share of its runs to refusals, and on 2026-09-24 a terra flex refusal burst paged the gateway's upstream error alert and we moved terra back to the standard queue for 15 hours at twice the price. Since 2026-09-25 every OpenAI scout run is on flex (`scouts-model-selection` flag), so the blast radius of the next burst is the whole fleet.

[PostHog/ai-gateway#500](https://github.com/PostHog/ai-gateway/pull/500) adds the fix on the gateway side: bounded same-tier retries for flex requests and, when the caller opts in, one attempt on the standard tier before any output has been sent. The opt-in is a request header, `X-PostHog-Flex-Fallback: standard`. Without the header the gateway only retries on flex, and a run whose flex retries are exhausted still fails.

## Proposal

1. **Send the opt-in header on every flex-pinned Codex run.** `products/desktop/packages/agent/src/server/gateway-env.ts` already builds `openaiCustomHeaders` and sets `X-PostHog-Service-Tier` when the run carries a `serviceTier` (from `POSTHOG_CODE_SERVICE_TIER`, set by `products/tasks/backend/logic/services/sandbox.py` from the run state that `products/signals/backend/agent_runtime.py` resolves). When `serviceTier === "flex"` and the target is the Go gateway, also set `X-PostHog-Flex-Fallback: standard`. Codex forwards the record as static headers on every request (`model_providers.posthog.http_headers` in `spawn.ts`), so nothing else changes on the wire. The Claude path has no tier and stays untouched. Update the `serviceTier` doc comment in `server/types.ts` and extend `agent-server.configure-environment.test.ts`, which already asserts the tier header.

2. **Check Codex's pre-header timeout against the gateway's retry window.** #500 can hold the response headers for up to four minutes of flex retries (285 s first-byte deadline). Codex's `stream_idle_timeout_ms` (`SANDBOX_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, 90 s in `spawn.ts`) only starts once the stream is open, so the number that matters is the HTTP client's request timeout in `codex-api` while waiting for headers. If Codex gives up before the gateway does, it re-issues the request (`request_max_retries`), which starts a fresh gateway retry loop and burns the 15-minute run budget. Verify the value on the pinned Codex build; if it is shorter than 285 s, either raise it for flex-pinned sandboxes or agree a shorter gateway window for scout traffic. Record the answer in the PR.

3. **Make the fallback visible on the run.** #500 records each upstream attempt and whether the standard fallback was attempted and confirmed. Once the property names are settled, surface the count of fallback generations per run on `signals_scout_run_finished` next to `service_tier`, so `signals_scouts_runs` can split "ran on flex" from "fell back to standard" and the cost read stays honest (a fallback bills the standard rate).

## Sequencing

- #500 must be merged and `AI_GATEWAY_FLEX_FALLBACK_ENABLED` turned on in prod-us and prod-eu before the header has any effect. The header is harmless before that: the gateway ignores unknown `X-PostHog-*` headers it does not consume.
- Part 1 is a small PR and can land first. Parts 2 and 3 can follow separately.

## Acceptance

- A flex-pinned Codex scout run sends `X-PostHog-Flex-Fallback: standard` on every gateway request; a run with no tier or on the Claude runtime sends nothing new.
- With #500 enabled, a run that hits a flex refusal on a generation before output completes on the standard tier instead of failing; `$ai_service_tier` on that generation reads the served tier.
- The Codex pre-header timeout is documented against the gateway's first-byte deadline, with the change made if one was needed.

## Out of scope

- Retrying a refusal that arrives after output has started (the gateway does not replay; #500 ends the stream). A harness-level turn retry is tracked separately.
- Per-scout or per-arm control of the fallback. If an A/B of "flex with fallback" vs "flex without" is wanted later, a `flex_fallback` key on the model-selection payload entry can carry it the same way `service_tier` does.

## Context

- Gateway fallback: https://github.com/PostHog/ai-gateway/pull/500
- Tier plumbing this builds on: #95310, #96171 (header path), #99484 (labelled payload entries)
- Slack: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C1T3V1RJA/p1790264767840059

## Problem

An MCP server owner, or an agent using the PostHog MCP, has no way to ask how a tool is used over time: which intent topics it serves, whether its use is consolidated or spread, where it drifts, what the outlier uses are, and which other tools serve the same intents. The legacy snapshot exposes one sampled blob with no time dimension. At the largest project's volume, any query that joins the events table to per-intent results would not finish.

## Changes

Fourth layer of the intent topics stack, on top of the pipeline. Backend and MCP only; the UI comes in the next layer.

Rollup writes use the main cluster with `Workload.OFFLINE` because they run in the background. Fresh event reads retain their separate pipeline route.

<details><summary>Rollup write routing for native-events projects</summary>

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Writer[Hourly and daily rollup writes] --> Events[Events cluster]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class Writer phBlue;
    class Events phGray;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Writer[Hourly and daily rollup writes] --> Main[Main cluster]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class Writer phBlue;
    class Main phGray;
```

</details>

- **Rollups** (migration `0389_mcp_intent_rollups`, also declared in the HCL schema): `mcp_intent_calls_hourly` (calls and conversations per intent text, tool and hour, written by the hourly sync for every distinct intent in its window) and `mcp_intent_topic_daily` (calls, sessions, outlier calls and distinct intents per tool and topic per day, rebuilt by the nightly assign for its window). The assignments table gains a `tool` column. The daily rollup joins hourly rows to the canonical latest-assignment view, restricted to the window's hashes. Eligibility is checked after selecting the latest whole assignment: unknown or expired provenance leaves calls unassigned instead of restoring an older topic.
- **Exact totals under retries and overlap**: the sync writes complete hours only, the nightly rebuild covers whole days, and every reader takes the latest hourly version and the latest rebuild of each day (versions are stored with microseconds, so two rebuilds in one second stay apart). Conversations are kept as hash arrays and deduplicated across hours, intents, tools and days. Each hourly intent/tool bucket retains at most 1,000 conversation hashes; larger buckets can undercount conversations, while call totals remain exact.
- **Four typed queries** reading the rollups, the assignments and the topic registry, registered in the query runner and exposed as MCP tools behind the `mcp-analytics-intent-topics` flag:
  - `MCPIntentTopicsQuery`: topics ranked by calls, with share, change versus the previous window, sessions, outlier calls, top tools, and coverage. Optional tool scope.
  - `MCPToolIntentProfileQuery`: one tool's focus score and band, top topics with calls-per-day sparklines, drift (new, growing, shrinking, gone), and outlier intents.
  - `MCPSimilarToolsQuery`: other tools ranked by cosine similarity of topic share vectors, with the shared topics.
  - `MCPIntentMapQuery`: topic bubbles and the most called intent points, with optional tool, topic and bounds filters and a total count.
- Queries compare against the previous window of the same number of calendar days, set explicit limits on every internal read, and build map points and outliers from the intents called in the window joined to their latest assignment. Each `limit` must be 1 or more, with a maximum per query.
- MCP: query wrappers can list `response_fields` in `tools.yaml`, and the factory forwards those top-level fields next to `results`, so the profile, map and topics tools return focus, drift, outliers, coverage, topics and the point total.
- **Access**: the queries run as the caller, so member and role restrictions on `$mcp_intent` apply. A restricted caller gets no intent text, no hashes and generic topic labels. The four kinds need `mcp_analytics:read` through the query API.
- **Window cap**: a date range may span at most 366 days, because the daily rollup keeps 12 months. A longer range returns a query error before any sparkline is built.
- **Retention**: both rollups extend `EventsRetentionTable`, so reads get the project's events retention floor on `hour` and `day`.
- **Days and hours**: hourly buckets are UTC, and daily rows follow the project timezone, so a date range resolves to the same days in totals, sparklines and the map.
- The map shows only points assigned since the latest refit, so points and topic bubbles share one 2D projection.
- New `exploring-mcp-intent-topics` skill mapping the owner's questions to these tools, and a row in the tool usage skill.
- Mechanical: generated JSON and Python schema, schema snapshots.

Only the tool and the date range filter these queries; shared property filters do not apply, because the rollups carry no person or event properties. The tool descriptions say so.

Why: these are the answers the owner asked for ("how has use of tool X changed over 3 months", "is the intent consolidated", "what are the outlier uses", "which tools have a similar intended use"), and the data the dashboard card, tool page section and map read in the next layer.

Query reads remain bounded to the requested window. Refit sampling now uses fresh surviving source events through the pipeline, so the earlier hourly-rollup refit benchmark no longer describes this implementation.

## How did you test this code?

The latest pipeline reconciliation passes 98 focused tests covering source reads, embeddings, assignments, rollups and writer admission. Full-repository mypy passes across 29,839 files. API regeneration produced no tracked-file drift; the optional desktop generator was unavailable locally and remains for CI. The merge retains quorum settings, streamed hourly writes, and daily rebuilds after all assignment pages, including projects with no topics.

The existing daily totals test now also covers legacy and native events routing with a separate events host. The rollup test file passes. Removing either write-path routing guard fails at the wrong host; the test asserts persisted totals through real ClickHouse.

The daily eligibility increment extends the existing daily rebuild tests with missing/expired provenance, cross-partition latest rows, tied versions, team isolation, and hourly-count preservation. Database-backed tests exercise the real HogQL compiler and ClickHouse aggregation; the earlier latest-assignment test did not cover those cases.

Local validation after storage/writer reconciliation passed the pipeline, rollup, corpus, assignment, query and schema checks, full-repository mypy, and HCL/golden checks. An intentionally incorrect per-row eligibility implementation fails the new regressions. Actual daily-query `EXPLAIN` confirms team/hash primary-key pruning. No production benchmark or hosted-MCP check was performed for this increment.

**Test rationale:** The regressions are a rollup that double counts duplicate ReplacingMergeTree rows or loses unassigned intents, a share or trend computed against the wrong window, a focus or drift that ignores the unassigned bucket, a similar-tools vector built from the wrong topics, and map filters that leak across teams. No existing test covers the rollups or these queries. Added: `test_intent_topics_rollups.py` (hourly grouping with conversations; daily rollup with unassigned bucket, outlier calls and latest-assignment-wins across rebuilds) and `test_intent_topics_queries.py` (ranking, share, trend, top tools and coverage; tool scope and limit; focus bands, drift lists, sparkline buckets and outliers for one tool; similarity ranking with shared topics; map points, bubbles, bounds, limit, topic and tool filters), all on the test ClickHouse. The pipeline

### Feature request

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

An EU Cloud project that runs LLM-as-a-judge evaluations has no way to keep the inference inside the EU. Every provider key you can add under Project settings, AI observability, "Bring your own key" sends prompt and response content to a fixed global endpoint, so the content the judge sees leaves the region you chose PostHog EU for. Google Gemini is the case teams hit first, because it is the natural pick for anyone already on Google Cloud, and the Gemini option calls Google's global endpoint with no region control. The key is also used by the playground and taggers, so there is no per-feature escape.

## Describe the solution you'd like

A provider option where you choose the region the inference runs in, so evaluation traffic stays inside the EU. Google Vertex AI is the concrete ask: it offers region-based inference, so you supply a Google Cloud project and a location such as `europe-west4`, and requests stay in that region while you keep the Gemini model family.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Azure OpenAI works today and is the only provider whose endpoint you supply yourself, so an Azure resource in an EU region on a regional or EU data zone deployment does keep inference in the EU. It means changing provider and model family, which is not viable for a team standardized on Google Cloud. Otherwise the only option is to turn evaluations off.

## Additional context

The provider list under `/settings/project-ai-observability#ai-observability-byok` is OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Fireworks, Azure OpenAI, Together AI, MiniMax, and Zeabur AI Hub. Azure OpenAI is the only entry that reads a customer-supplied endpoint. Nothing in the dialog states where the inference runs, which makes this easy to miss when setting a key up.

Asked for by an EU Cloud team who offered to contribute the implementation.

hits.body:
## Problem

A scheduled scout run that fails is gone until the lane's next scheduled slot. `RunSignalsScoutWorkflow` runs its activity with `RetryPolicy(maximum_attempts=1)`, the coordinator's child workflow ids use `REJECT_DUPLICATE` per tick, and `resolve_scout_model` picks the model once per run with no fallback. Nothing in the harness distinguishes "the provider refused this request" from "this scout is broken": both book one `failed` run and advance the failure streak.

That is the right posture for a broken scout. It is the wrong posture for an upstream blip. On 2026-09-11 one OpenAI model refused requests for about three hours (posthog#99118). Every scout run routed to it failed on its first turn, median 31 seconds in. Most of the affected lanes run daily, so a half-minute failure cost each of them a full day of output, and a few weekly lanes lost a week. The other models in the fleet were healthy the whole time.

The failure breaker (`limits.py`, span-aware threshold) already tolerates this: no lane was paused. The gap is the lost run, not the pause.

## Proposal

One bounded retry inside the same activity, gated on the agent's own error classification, with an optional fallback model.

**Gate.** In `arun_signals_scout` (`products/signals/backend/scout_harness/runner.py`), when `_spawn_and_run` raises `AgentTurnFailed` (posthog#99119) with `retryable_upstream=True`, and all of the following hold, spawn one more session for the same `run_id`:

- the failed attempt emitted nothing (`emitted_count == 0` from `_read_run_metrics`), so a retry cannot duplicate reports
- the failed attempt spent less than a fixed budget of wall clock (say 3 minutes), so the retry fits inside `WORKFLOW_HARD_CEILING_S` and a run that died late does not get a second full-length attempt
- this is the first attempt
- the run is a scheduled or workflow-triggered one, not a manual `run now` (a human is watching those and will press the button again)

Anything else fails exactly as today.

**What the retry runs on.** Resolve the model again with a `fallback` intent:

- If the `scouts-model-selection` payload for this scout (or the `*` wildcard) carries a `fallback` key, use that model, with its runtime adapter resolved the same way `default` is. Add the key next to `DEFAULT_MODEL_KEY` in `model_selection.py` and parse it in `_scout_config`.
- If it does not, retry on the same model after a short backoff.
- If the scout has an explicit per-scout pin (`SignalScoutConfig.model` with the `scouts-model-config` flag on), retry on the same model only. A user chose that model deliberately and a trial must not silently reroute it.

**Bookkeeping.** The retry is the same run, not a new one:

- Same `run_id`, same bridge row. `_create_bridge_row` fires again via `on_task_run_created` with a new `TaskRun`; make `_create_run_row` update the existing row's `task_run_id`, model, and runtime adapter instead of inserting. The `signals_scout_run_started` marker fires once per attempt, so add `attempt` to it.
- `signals_scout_run_finished` fires once, at the end, for the final outcome. Add `attempt` (1 or 2), `retried_from_category`, and when the model changed, `model_fallback_from`. `model` is the model that produced the outcome.
- The failure streak advances only if the retry also fails. A rescued run clears it, as any success does.
- The daily cap (`_runs_today_by_team`) counts run rows, so a retry inside the same row does not consume a second slot. Confirm this in a test rather than assuming it.
- Cost: both attempts' `$ai_generation` events carry the run's `ai_stage` and `ai_agent_name`, so the failed attempt's spend (small, it died in a minute) lands on the same scout. The run-cost tooltip and the cost views (`signals_scouts_*`) should read both TaskRuns for a run, or accept the undercount and say so.

## Design points to settle

- **Fallback scope.** Start fleet-wide: one `fallback` under the `*` wildcard, so the change is a flag payload edit and no per-scout config. Per-scout fallbacks can follow if a case turns up. The fallback should be on the other runtime adapter's provider when the point is provider independence, but a same-provider fallback (a different OpenAI model) would also have covered the 2026-09-11 case and keeps the Codex tooling posture identical.
- **A/B reads.** Runs that fell back carry `model_fallback_from`. Model-trial reads (the `scouts-model-selection` fraction slices) filter them out at query time rather than the harness excluding them. Attribution stays honest without hiding the run.
- **Turn retry vs run retry.** posthog#99118 makes the agent server's two turn retries fire for a capacity refusal. If those succeed the run never reaches this code. This retry is for when they do not: the same-model retries exhausted inside a still-degraded window. The two layers are complementary, and the budget here should assume the first attempt already spent its turn retries.
- **Backoff for the same-model case.** Short and fixed (30 to 60 seconds). Anything longer and the run eats its own runtime budget; a provider still refusing after a minute needs the fallback, not patience.
- **Cancellation.** A retry must observe activity cancellation the same way the first attempt does; the `BaseException` path in `arun_signals_scout` stays as is.
- **Single-flight.** `_has_running_run` keys on the terminal status of the linked TaskRun. The first attempt's TaskRun is `FAILED` before the retry starts, so the lane is free to spawn again; confirm the check reads the bridge row's current link and not the first TaskRun.

## Acceptance

- A run whose first attempt raises `AgentTurnFailed` with an `upstream_*` category, zero emits, and a short runtime is retried once; a run failing for any other reason, or after emitting, or after the budget, is not. Test through the public runner entry point with the session factory stubbed, extending the existing runner tests.
- With a `fallback` in the payload the retry uses that model and its runtime adapter; with a per-scout pin the retry stays on the pinned model.
- `signals_scout_run_finished` for a rescued run reads `status=completed`, `attempt=2`, `model_fallback_from` set when the model changed.
- The failure streak does not advance for a rescued run.
- One run consumes one daily-cap slot regardless of attempts.
- Fleet read after deploy: on a day with a provider incident, the share of scheduled lanes that book a `failed` run with an `upstream_*` category drops to the share whose retry also failed.

## Out of scope

- Temporal-level `maximum_attempts > 1` on the scout activity. It would re-spawn a sandbox with no classification and no dedupe against a run that already emitted.
- A re-dispatch queue in the coordinator. Same outcome as the in-activity retry with far more machinery.
- Provider health probes or pre-emptive routing away from a degraded model.
- Retrying non-upstream failures (`task_spend_limit`, `agent_error`, poll timeouts). Those are the scout's or the budget's problem and must keep feeding the breaker.

## Related

- posthog#99118 (layer 0: classify the refusal so the turn retry fires)
- posthog#99119 (layer 1: carry the category into the harness)
- Failure breaker vs platform outages and model attribution are tracked in the scouts backlog.

## Problem

- People in the Data ops scene see the wrong screen in five states, and some act on what they see.
- A failed status load shows the provisioning form to an organization that already has a warehouse.
- One failed status read freezes the provisioning spinner until a reload.
- Members see a provisioning form and a "Reset password" button that the API rejects for non-admins.
- A project that has not joined the warehouse lands on Overview cards that all say "Not configured".
- The one-time password banner can end up hidden behind the Settings tab.

## Changes

- A failed status load shows "Couldn't load the warehouse status." with a "Try again" button.
- Status reads continue after a failure, with no toast on each failed read.
- Members see an ask-an-admin message, and "Reset password" is disabled for them.
- A project that has not joined sees the settings view with "Enable this project". Overview and Monitoring appear after it joins.
- The password banner sits above the tabs.
- Clicking Deprovision no longer hides the tabs before the request settles.
- The `warehouse_status` API returns `team_onboarded: null` when the control plane cannot answer, instead of `false`. The scene then keeps the tabs, warns, and retries.
- A failed refresh while an older status is shown adds an "out of date" warning with "Try again".

hits.body:
Asking PostHog for a chart through the ChatGPT connector returns the numbers as text, but the interactive visualization never appears. The same requests render correctly in other MCP clients, so this is specific to ChatGPT. Opening the connector's tool list in ChatGPT also shows a single `exec` tool rather than PostHog's individual tools, which is not what ChatGPT is meant to receive.

*If this affects the front-end, screenshots would be of great help.*

*If you are on PostHog Cloud it would be really valuable if you can share any links where the problem occurs. This speeds up our ability to troubleshoot tremendously.*

## How to reproduce

1. Connect PostHog's MCP server to ChatGPT as a connector.
2. Ask a question that has a visualization, for example "show me pageviews for the last 7 days".
3. The answer arrives as text only. No chart is rendered.
4. Inspect the connector's tool list. Only `exec` is offered, not PostHog's per-tool roster.

## Additional context

From: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/70284

### Why it happens

`resolveMode` in `services/mcp/src/hono/request-state-resolver.ts` puts every client in cli (single-exec) mode unless `isToolsModeClient()` matches. ChatGPT is meant to be one of two allow-listed exceptions.

`isToolsModeClient()` in `services/mcp/src/lib/client-detection.ts` matches ChatGPT on a `'chatgpt'` fragment in `TOOLS_MODE_USER_AGENT_FRAGMENTS`, because OpenAI's connector reports a generic `openai-mcp` as its `clientInfo.name`. That fragment assumes the user agent looks like `openai-mcp/1.0.0 (ChatGPT)`.

In observed production traffic no request carries that parenthetical. The OpenAI surfaces that do send one identify as Codex, Agent Builder, or Responses API. Everything else arrives as a bare `openai-mcp/1.0.0`. The fragment matches nothing, so ChatGPT falls through to cli mode.

In cli mode, `buildAdvertisedTools` in `services/mcp/src/hono/tool-executor.ts` advertises `exec`, plus `render-ui` only when `renderUiEnabled` is true. `renderUiEnabled` is `isClaudeUiHost()`, which matches Anthropic hosts only. ChatGPT therefore receives no tool carrying `_meta.ui.resourceUri` and has nothing to mount. In tools mode it would receive the per-tool roster, where each query tool declares its own UI resource.

What is confirmed, and what is not: that the `(ChatGPT)` fragment matches no live traffic is directly observed. Which bare-user-agent requests are ChatGPT is an inference, and that is itself part of the problem, because the bare bucket cannot currently be told apart from Codex. Simply widening the match to bare `openai-mcp` would pull Codex into tools mode, which the original change deliberately kept out.

### Where it shows up

Any PostHog query tool that has a UI app, for any user of the ChatGPT connector.

### Suggested approaches

The MCP Apps extension already has a capability handshake that removes the guesswork. Clients advertise UI support in the `extensions` field of their capabilities at initialization, under `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`, listing the MIME types they can render. The bundled SDK exports a `getUiCapability` helper for reading it.

The server does not read it today. `services/mcp/src/lib/stateless-protocol.ts` validates that a client sent a `clientCapabilities` object but never inspects it for the UI extension, and `getUiCapability` is not called anywhere in `services/mcp`.

Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. Key UI eligibility on the declared capability rather than on the user agent. That identifies any UI-capable host, including ones nobody has enumerated yet, and it stops rendering from depending on a vendor string that a third party can change at any time.
2. If a user-agent discriminator is still wanted for mode selection, confirm what ChatGPT actually sends today and re-point the fragment at that.
3. Either way, add a test that fails when an allow-list fragment matches nothing real. Today the failure is silent: the constant reads correctly, the comment describes the intended user agent, and nothing notices that it stopped matching.

### Related work

- #69629 added the cli-mode default and the Cursor and ChatGPT tools-mode allow-list. This is where the fragment was introduced.
- #69612 declares `openai/widgetCSP` on UI app resources specifically so ChatGPT permits the app's assets. That work implies ChatGPT UI apps are intended to work, and it cannot take effect while no UI-bearing tool reaches ChatGPT.
- #92078 fixes a different render failure, on Claude web and desktop, where the app does mount but its data fetch is stripped. It does not touch this path.

## Debug info

PostHog Cloud, Debug information: EU project ID 253488

## Problem

- An LLM judge evaluation stops producing results, with no event and no status, when its provider rejects the call with a 4xx we do not map.
- The OpenAI-compatible provider makes this common: a provider-specific rejection reaches no mapping, so the user sees nothing at all.
- The raw SDK error lands in the catch-all in `call_llm_judge`, re-raises, and fails the run after its retries without an `$ai_evaluation` event.

**Why:** an unknown provider rejection must show up as a visible skipped result, with the provider's message, instead of failing silently.

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0b5af-1eee-7adb-8e0f-4b2af758265c -->
## Origin

- Conversations: [ticket](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a0b541-aa4d-0000-a628-e3f60405ead7)
- First signal: 2026-09-18
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0b5af-1eee-7adb-8e0f-4b2af758265c)

- Task started by: a person, from the inbox
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0b5af-1eee-7adb-8e0f-4b2af758265c -->

- An unmapped 4xx now emits a skipped `$ai_evaluation` event with the `request_rejected` skip reason, the same reason System One uses for an unknown 4xx.
- The skip reasoning names the status and ends with the provider's own message, bounded by the existing `truncate_error_detail` helper.
- The evaluation stays enabled and the key state stays unchanged. One bad input and a bad configuration look the same at this point.
- The skip applies only to a team's own key. On a PostHog-funded key the rejection still raises and reaches error tracking, because there it is our bug.
- 408, 409, 429, 499 and every 5xx still raise and retry, so a provider outage does not turn into skips.
- The status comes from `status_code` (OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs) or `code` (google-genai), so the change covers every provider adapter.
