hits.body:
## Problem

A scout self-improvement report (`Scout self-improvement: <skill-name> – <topic>`) rarely carries `suggested_prompts`, although its next step is almost always the same: apply the suggested change to the scout's skill.

Over the last 30 days, about 37% of surfaced self-improvement reports had at least one suggested prompt, against about 78% of finding reports (`signals_scout_report_emitted`, `suggested_prompt_count > 0`, split by `report_kind`).

The gap costs more here than on a finding, because a self-improvement report has no other one-click action:

- It is filed with `repository = NO_REPO`, so `implement` is disabled (`IMPLEMENT_NO_REPOSITORY_DISABLED_REASON` in `report_task_actions.py`).
- The fix is an edit to a skill row, not a pull request, so the PR actions never apply.
- The reader is left with an empty `Ask AI` box and has to write "apply this to the skill" themselves.

## What the outcome data says

Coverage is the gap, but coverage alone will not prove the fix. Three reads from the same 30 days:

- Self-improvement reports are opened as a discussion about four times as often as findings. Owners already reach for `Ask AI` on them, with a prompt they type themselves.
- Among self-improvement reports, the ones that carry a prompt today are discussed and resolved at the same rate as the ones that do not. Not checked: whether those prompts are questions or the "apply it" action. The guidance steers scouts towards questions.
- Where a self-improvement report does carry prompts, readers press them about twenty times as often per report as on a finding. On these reports about two questions in five come from a suggested prompt, against about one in five on findings.
- Most self-improvement reports stay open with no recorded action, with or without a prompt.

So prompts on these reports are used when they exist, but they do not yet move the report to resolved. The change to judge is a prompt that performs the edit, not a prompt of any kind.

Related: #138191 covers reports the pipeline writes, which carry almost no suggested prompts.

## Why it happens

Three things in `products/signals/backend/scout_harness/prompt.py` push the scout away from writing a prompt:

1. `_SELF_IMPROVEMENT_REPORT_FIELDS` lists the fields a self-improvement report carries (title, summary, `actionability`, `repository`, `suggested_reviewers`). `suggested_prompts` is not in the list, and scouts treat the list as complete.
2. `_REPORT_SUGGESTED_PROMPTS` is written for findings. Its bar is "what your research left open", and it says to write none rather than pad. A scout reads "apply the change I just described" as the obvious prompt that section tells it to skip.
3. The same section says to leave anything a person should weigh as a question, and the report is `requires_human_input`. Together these read as "no action prompt".

An existing report grows through `append_evidence`, which does not touch prompts, so a report filed without them stays without them.

## Proposal

**1. Name the prompt in the self-improvement guidance (prompt only).**

Add `suggested_prompts` to `_SELF_IMPROVEMENT_REPORT_FIELDS`, so both escalation variants pick it up. The scout writes one action prompt that names its skill and the change, for example:

> Apply the suggested change to the `<skill-name>` skill: <the change in a few words>. Then mark this report resolved.

"Then mark this report resolved" is correct here: the edit completes in place and no pull request is involved, which is the case `_REPORT_SUGGESTED_PROMPTS` already allows.

Optionally a second, question-shaped prompt for an owner who wants to look first, for example "Show me the exact edit this would make to the `<skill-name>` skill body".

The skill name is text the scout writes into its own report, not a per-run interpolation, so the cacheable prefix is unchanged.

**2. Tell the scout when it files one without a prompt (optional, deterministic).**

Add a `hint` check for a self-improvement title with no `suggested_prompts`, returned in `quality_hints` so the scout can fix the report in the same run. `tools/report_quality.py` checks title and summary today, so this needs the check input widened to the prompt count.

**Not proposed:** a server-side default prompt synthesized at read time. It would give full coverage, including existing reports, but a fixed sentence cannot name the specific change, and it makes the harness write report content the scout owns.

## Open questions

- Can the `Ask AI` run always apply the edit? It needs `llm_skill:write` for the person who sends the prompt. If it cannot, the run should say so instead of failing quietly. Check what the discussion run's token carries for a self-improvement report.
- Should the prompt ask for the edit directly, or for a proposed diff the owner confirms? The report is `requires_human_input`, and the person clicking the prompt is the human input, so a direct edit looks right. A skill edit publishes a new version, so it is recoverable.

## Problem

- AI observability under-reports cost for OpenAI generations with prompts above 272K input tokens, such as GPT-6 Sol (#106645).
- OpenAI bills the whole request at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output above that threshold. The cost step only knew one long-context rule, for Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview.

Closes #106645

## Changes

- OpenAI generations above 272K input tokens now show long-context costs, and `$ai_model_cost_used` reads `<model>:large`.
- A per-model threshold table replaces the hard-coded Gemini rule. Gemini keeps its 200K threshold.
- New `:large` rows for 14 OpenAI models: standard, priority and flex rates, from the "Long" view of [OpenAI's pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing).
- The OpenAI rows apply only when `$ai_provider` resolves to `openai`. Azure, Bedrock and OpenRouter stay flat, because their long-context rates are not published there.
- A name must end at the model or a dated snapshot, so `gpt-5.4-mini` and `gpt-6-sol-pro` keep their own prices.

- `cost-model-matching.test.ts`: `getNewModelName` cases at 272,000 and 272,001 tokens, snapshot names, excluded variants and non-OpenAI providers.
- `manual-providers.test.ts`: `processCost` for `gpt-6-sol` just under and over the threshold, on the standard, flex and priority tiers.

## Problem

- A cold dashboards v2 load spends most of each tile's time building the HogQL database, not in ClickHouse.
- Every target in one `query_batch` request rebuilt it from scratch, so teams with large data warehouses pay that cost once per tile.

## Changes

- Cold v2 boards build the HogQL database once per batch for targets that share its inputs, then share it.
- A batch-scoped registry in `posthog/hogql/database/request_scope.py` keys each build on team, user, access-control scope, normalized modifiers, connection and the other `create_for` inputs.
- Targets with different schema modifiers (new events engine, `personsOnEventsMode`, sessions version) or another user get their own database.
- One thread builds each key under a lock while the others wait. The registry dies with the batch, so no cross-request cache.
- Workers honour the existing `HOGQL_SHARED_INSIGHT_DATABASE_ENABLED` kill switch.
- Calls outside a batch scope are unchanged.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the batch test fails if `query_batch.py` stops entering the scope (3 builds instead of 1). The `test_database.py` cases fail if the key drops modifiers or user, which would hand a member an admin's tables. The nearest existing tests cover the cross-request sources cache, not per-batch sharing. Not run: a local timing, because the local dev stack was down.

**CI report warnings:** the Python duplication block is the `create_for` and `_build_for` signatures, kept as two typed parameter lists so `create_for` can route a call to the shared registry without losing its type checks. The added call assertion counts `Database._build_for` calls, because the number of builds is the outcome this change exists to cut.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Problem

- Our experiment page only offers code snippets, and not agent prompts. So would be good to try out prompts to see if they are more frequently used and to encourage MCP usage. 

Note, this does not take into account any UX redesign for experiments. 

## Changes

- New experiment behind `experiment-implementation-agent-prompt`, in the draft header and the Code tab:
  - Control: the snippet, as today.
  - Test: a switch between "Prompt for your agent" and "Code snippet", open on the prompt.
- In the test arm, each option's controls sit on the header row, left of the switch. The prompt has the agent button, the code has the variant and SDK selects. The switch stays put when the option changes.
- In the test arm, the prompt and code snippets over 10 lines open as a preview, with a button to show the rest.
  - Copying still takes the whole text.
  - The control arm keeps today's full snippet, since it is the baseline.
- The prompt names the experiment, its page, the flag key and the variants, with the baseline marked.
  - It tells the agent to read the flag where users see the change, and to change behavior for every variant except the baseline.
  - It names a custom exposure event or action, an activation event, their property filters, the group type of a group-aggregated flag, and the source of a warehouse-native exposure, when the experiment has them. Without these, following the prompt can record no exposures or return no variant.
  - A line before the project's values tells the agent to treat them as data, never as instructions. The steps name no project values.
  - Values are JSON-quoted. Quoting also escapes line separators and bidi and zero-width characters, so the preview a teammate reads shows the same text the agent gets. Experiment names stop at 80 characters.
  - When the values would take the prompt past 3,600 characters, the prompt leaves them out and points to the experiment page. The warning and the steps then fit in Codex and VS Code deep links, which cut prompts at 4,000 characters. Flag and variant keys are never cut, since a cut key gives the agent the wrong code.
  - It ends with the PostHog MCP install line, the same text the agent button's Clipboard option copies.
- The agent button copies the prompt, or opens it in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others.
  - It leaves out PostHog AI, which can't edit the user's code, and keeps "Copy prompt" on the main button. The wizard's setup prompt does the same.
- `AgentPromptButton` now reports a Clipboard copy only once the copy lands, so a denied or unavailable clipboard isn't counted. This applies to every caller, and makes their `onRun` events match the copies people actually got.
- The flag is read inside the implementation section, so only people who see the section are exposed.
- The section shows a skeleton until feature flags load. It never picks an arm from flags persisted on an earlier visit, so a copy before the switch can't count for the wrong arm.
- The experiment and its metrics still need creating in PostHog. Until then everyone gets the control.

| Event | Captured when | Properties |
|---|---|---|
| `experiment implementation option selected` | someone switches between prompt and snippet | `experiment_id`, `placement`, `option` |
| `experiment implementation agent prompt copied` | the prompt is copied from its text or the Clipboard option, once the copy lands | `experiment_id`, `experiment_status`, `placement`, `prompt_kind: feature_flag`, `source` |
| `experiment implementation agent prompt opened` | the prompt opens in an agent | `experiment_id`, `placement`, `agent` |
| `experiment implementation snippet copied` | a code snippet is copied, from the parent PR | gains `implementation_arm` |

- `buildAgentPrompt` is now exported from the `AgentPromptButton` index. Mechanical.

| Test, open on the prompt | ![Test arm on the prompt: Copy prompt beside the switch, prompt as a preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/6c9f0ec3febac08b6906b5ef10c032f6a3db77af/2026/10/c44a2237-4459-49ad-be55-495a5dadf47c.png) |
| Test, on the code snippet, with the variant select kept | ![Test arm on the code snippet: variant and SDK selects beside the switch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/a07f436123898d540a18712bd998df870fe0c537/2026/10/a44f74c3-9a8a-4039-88c8-51c903188ee5.png) |

Screenshots from the `DraftExperiment` and `DraftExperimentAgentPrompt` stories, with mock data. The test arm screenshot on the prompt replaces the earlier ones, since the agent button moved to the header row and now reads "Copy prompt". It predates the shorter prompt, so its text is older than the code. The visual review snapshot of `DraftExperimentAgentPrompt` shows the current text.

## Problem

Ordered funnels drop users whose events arrive out of order: a slow request stores step one after step two, which the device captured later (#98250).

## Changes

- New `funnelUseClientCaptureOrder` modifier, off by default, orders funnel steps by the device's capture time (`$client_capture_time`, recorded by #103264).
- Each browser or mobile device gets one anchor per day, which cancels its clock error and leaves only its smallest delivery delay.
  - Mobile events without `$device_id` group by distinct ID plus device model, so two devices sharing a distinct ID stay apart.
  - The per-day bound limits the damage from a device clock change.
- Server SDK events, groups where any event lacks the capture time, and groups over 10,000 events keep the stored timestamp.
- Nothing changes until a team turns the modifier on; generated schema files are mechanical.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not enable the modifier until `$client_capture_time` is materialized on `events`; reading it from the properties JSON is far more expensive.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** `test_funnel_capture_order.py` covers each grouping rule (device ID, distinct ID plus model, day split, server SDKs, the size cap, partial coverage), funnel trends, and the materialized-column read. Breaking any one rule fails its test. The existing funnel suite and its snapshots are unchanged.

- A replay on sampled production data, browser and mobile in both regions, made under 0.5% of the reordered event pairs worse than the stored order.
- Peak memory on synthetic data stays close to the modifier-off query, because the group key is a hash.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

None.

hits.body:
`SignalScoutConfig.emit` is a per-scout dry-run posture, defaulting to on. A scout should always be able to write and edit reports, so the setting has no job left to do. It is an early design relic and should come out.

Worth stating plainly: #88605 just added this toggle to the web settings form, because it was reachable through the API but not the UI. That was the right fix for the inconsistency it found, and it makes the setting's real cost easier to see. This issue removes the setting and the toggle with it. Closed #88966 as the issue behind that PR.

## Why remove it rather than keep it

Three things make it worse than redundant.

**It blocks the report channel, not just signals.** `_preflight_emit_gates` in `products/signals/backend/scout_harness/tools/emit.py:510` is shared by `emit_finding`, `emit_report`, and `record_structured_output`. A dry-run scout cannot author or edit a report at all. That contradicts what a scout is for.

**It is not a preview mode, it is a shredder.** Dispatch only filters on `enabled` (`config_registry.py:58`), so a dry-run scout runs in full and costs a full agent run. Then `_gate_skip_result` (`report.py:326`) returns `report_id=None` and persists nothing. The report the agent just wrote is discarded. Nobody can read what it would have said. So dry-run buys you the spend of a live scout and the output of a disabled one, and `enabled=false` already covers "do not run this".

**It forces special cases across the harness.** The inactivity sweep filters to `emit=True` and carries a comment explaining that a dry-run scout's silence means nothing (`inactivity.py:185`). `structured_output.py:381` raises rather than record. `runner.py:700` strips the schema snapshot and `runner.py:973` withholds a prompt section. `report.py:769` keeps a set of skip reasons that must not fan out to customers. Each is a branch that exists only because a scout might be configured to throw its work away.

## What a person sees afterwards

- No mode control in scout settings or the create form, in the web app or the desktop app.
- No "Dry run" badge in the roster, the summary row, or the scout page. A scout is on or off.
- A scout that runs writes its findings and reports. There is no configuration in which it runs and discards them.
- The gates that stop output for a real reason still stop it, and still say why.

## Removal surface

Backend:

- Drop the field on `SignalScoutConfig` (`models.py:1404`) and the doc comments around it, including the `structured_output_schema` comment that says the channel requires emit.
- `_preflight_emit_gates`: drop the `scout_emit_disabled` branch and its `EMIT_SKIP_REMEDIATION` entry, and remove it from `_INACTIVE_SKIP_REASONS`.
- `structured_output.py`: drop the `if not config.emit` raise in `_reserve_capacity`, and the dry-run clause in `InvalidStructuredOutputError`'s docstring.
- `runner.py`: both `config.emit` conditionals become unconditional on the schema being set.
- `inactivity.py`: drop the `emit=True` filter and its comment.
- `prompt.py:250`: the fleet roster line telling other scouts that a dry-run scout's silence is meaningless.
- Serializers: the field on the read, update, create-options, and fleet-entry serializers, plus the caveat in `EmitEligibilitySerializer.can_emit`'s help text.
- Views: the `emit` mentions in the list, create, update, and destroy endpoint descriptions.
- `admin.py:95,102`: `list_display` and `list_filter`. These break at import if the field goes and admin does not, so they belong in the same change.

Frontend, web and desktop:

- Web: `ScoutConfigControls.tsx`, `ScoutCreateModal.tsx`, `ScoutBadges.tsx`, `ScoutSummaryRow.tsx`, `ScoutsRoster.tsx` dry-run count, `scoutGroups.ts`, `InboxWaitingForWork.tsx`, `scoutCreateModalLogic.ts`, mocks and tests.
- Desktop: `features/scouts/components/ScoutConfigControls.tsx` mode select, `ScoutBadges.tsx`, `ScoutsFleetSection.tsx` dry-run count, `useScoutConfigMutations.ts` tracked settings, the hand-rolled `ScoutConfig.emit` type in `api-client/src/posthog-client.ts`, and the stories.
- The desktop app ships on its own cadence, so an older build will keep sending `emit` in its PATCH body for a while. DRF ignores unknown fields, so those writes become no-ops and the scout stays live. That is the right way for it to fail, but confirm it rather than assume it.

Analytics: `setting` on the desktop config-changed event drops an enum member, and the detail-viewed event drops a property on both clients. Historical events stay readable, so this is deletion, not a rename.

Docs and generated files: the run-posture sections in `authoring-scouts` and `exploring-scouts`, the harness `CLAUDE.md`, the field mentions in `products/signals/mcp/tools.yaml`, and a `hogli build:openapi` run for the generated TypeScript.

## Do not remove these

`emit` is overloaded in this codebase, and three neighbors read like the same thing:

- The other three preflight gates: `scout_config_missing`, `ai_processing_not_approved`, `source_disabled`. These are the fail-closed path and the org consent gate. `_preflight_emit_gates` keeps its shape, minus one branch.
- `can_emit` in `skill_loader.py` and the project profile. That is whether a skill was granted the `emit_report` tool, which is a different mechanism.
- The `scout-emit-signal` and `scout-emit-report` MCP tool names, and the `emitted_count` / `emitted_finding_ids` / `emitted_report_ids` run tallies. Those name the act of emitting, not the setting.

## Migration

The column is a plain unindexed boolean on a product table, with no constraint, no index, and no ClickHouse mirror. It is not on a hot table. Two phases, per `/django-migrations`:

1. Remove every reference, then a state-only removal wrapped in `SeparateDatabaseAndState`. Deploy. A Django `SELECT` lists every model field, so dropping the column while any running code still expects it breaks reads mid-deploy.
2. `DROP COLUMN` in a later migration, once the first has been out for a full deploy cycle.

## One decision for whoever picks this up

A handful of scouts in PostHog's own project are dry-run today, and they look like custom ones still being tuned. When the setting goes, they either start posting to the inbox or they stop.

Suggested default: disable them and tell their owners. From the inbox's point of view disabled and dry-run already look identical, disabled stops paying for discarded output, and the owner can turn it back on in one click. Flipping them live instead means someone gets output they never asked for from a scout they thought was still in staging. Worth a look at whether any enrolled team outside our own project is in the same position before choosing.

## Problem

On a transactional email's Impact tab, a project with link tracking off sees two empty funnel steps, "Started a session" and "Converted". The only way forward is a link to a settings page, so few people turn link tracking on, and the funnel stays half empty.

## Merge risk

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door
> - Frontend only, on the Impact tab, which only projects in the `workflows-email-impact` rollout see.
> - The button turns on one project setting, `workflows_config.email_workflow_run_link_tag_enabled`, with the same request as the settings switch.
> - Once on, the email worker tags links in new emails. Links in emails already sent keep their tag after the setting goes off again.
> - **Switch-off:** the `workflows-email-impact` flag hides the button; a project turns the setting off in Settings > Workflows.
> - **Tier:** critical
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

- With link tracking off, one centered box replaces the last two steps: "Link tracking is off", a line on what it does, and a "Turn on for project" button.
- The button turns link tracking on for the whole project in one click. The funnel then flips back to all six steps without a reload.
- If the saved project still has link tracking off, the button says so and stays available.
- Only project admins can press it. Others see it disabled with the reason.
- In an environment that is not its project's main one, the button is disabled with a reason, because no endpoint writes such an environment's settings.
- A successful save updates only the link tracking setting in the loaded project, so a workflows setting saved elsewhere meanwhile keeps its newer value.
- With link tracking on and no conversion event picked, the gray "Converted" box holds an event picker. It sets the same event as the picker above the funnel, so the two stay in sync.
- Usage tracking: `transactional email impact loaded` gains `shows_link_tracking_prompt`. New events: `transactional email impact link tracking turned on` and `transactional email impact event picked` (with `source`).

| Link tracking off, no event picked | Link tracking off, event picked |
| --- | --- |
| ![Centered link tracking prompt with Turn on for project across the last two steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/67fecb4e54882563bf33269fa74856d87d3eef33/2026/11/2d8e5a54-c64f-4bb6-af4e-4359e7c16483.png) | ![Link tracking prompt beside the converted step](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/67fecb4e54882563bf33269fa74856d87d3eef33/2026/11/70fc0561-3dc3-4ad6-a5f8-a8ed60822ea0.png) |
| **Dark theme** | **After "Turn on for project"** |
| ![Link tracking prompt in the dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/67fecb4e54882563bf33269fa74856d87d3eef33/2026/11/1fe070dc-680f-43dc-8ef4-017ad6448154.png) | ![All six steps, event picker in the Converted box](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/67fecb4e54882563bf33269fa74856d87d3eef33/2026/11/35e420bf-771e-4356-b678-0df9882fbf32.png) |

The screenshots replace the earlier pair, which showed an older layout of the prompt.

## How did you test this code?

Jest tests on the funnel card cover the prompt showing only when tagging is off, a successful and a failed turn-on, the non-admin state, the synced picker, and the tracking properties. Each guarded line was broken once and its test went red.
The frontend typecheck passes. Storybook screenshots were taken in light and dark themes at 1280 px and 640 px.

The CI report's eager graph growth also shows on the logged-out entry, `src/index.tsx`, which the Impact tab never loads into. It comes from master changes between the measured trees, not this diff. The duplication scans failed to run.

The CI report counts four new mock-call assertions. They check `posthog.capture` calls, which are this change's usage tracking output.

A live walk on a dev stack at e5b765e, as a project admin: one click sent one PATCH to the shown team, the funnel flipped without a reload, and stayed flipped after one. The project API then read the setting back as on for that team. Not covered live: a member without admin access, and the template email page.

**Test rationale:** the regressions are the prompt not showing, the button sending the whole config or never re-enabling after a failure, and the two pickers drifting apart. The nearest tests were the existing `ImpactFunnelCard.test.tsx` cases, extended here.

## Problem

A canvas app can read PostHog data and file tasks, but the actions a team most wants from a control surface are still missing: turn a flag on or off for a launch, add a customer to a beta cohort, hand an error to the person on call, start or stop a survey. Each of those today means leaving the app for the product page.

Third layer of the stack on [#112103](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/112103). It is independent of the dashboard tile and could land on its own.

## Changes

- A canvas that declares them can invoke `feature_flags.enable`, `feature_flags.disable`, `cohorts.add_persons`, `error_tracking.assign`, `surveys.launch`, and `surveys.stop`. Every write runs **as the viewer** through the target product's own facade: the viewer must be able to edit the flag or survey, hold editor access to error tracking, and a scoped API key must carry that product's write scope on top of `canvas:write`.
- Flag flips go through the approval gate. A team policy that requires approval answers 409 with a `change_request_id`, and the flag stays as it was.
- The registry (`GET …/canvases/actions/`) now reports `starts_cloud_run`, and the web host asks the viewer to confirm only destructive or paid verbs (`feature_flags.disable`, `surveys.stop`, `workflows.pause`, `tasks.create_and_run`). Plain writes run on the user's click without a second dialog, as in PostHog Desktop. Every invoke still requires a user gesture.
- New facade functions in the target products: `cohorts.add_persons_to_static_cohort`, `surveys.launch_survey` / `stop_survey`, `feature_flags.find_flag_by_key`, `error_tracking.user_can_mutate_issues`. They mirror the corresponding API actions, including activity log entries.
- Mechanical: `tach.toml` dependencies for canvas on the four products, regenerated OpenAPI and MCP types for the new registry field.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Each new verb gets one test in `TestCanvasActions` (`products/canvas/backend/tests/test_canvas_api.py`) that covers the regression no existing test does: the write lands as the viewer, the refusal paths (other project 404, dynamic cohort 400, archived survey 400, unknown person 400) leave state untouched, and a member with viewer-only flag access gets 403. The scope table gains one row per verb so `canvas:write` alone never grants the write. `canvasDataBridge.test.ts` gains the case that a plain write does not prompt, next to the existing paid-task prompt case.

Ran locally: `TestCanvasActions` (31 tests), `canvasDataBridge.test.ts`, `hogli lint:tach`, mypy and ruff on the changed files, `hogli build:openapi`. Not run: the full canvas, surveys, cohorts, or error tracking suites.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

The verbs are only reachable from a canvas that declares them, and the existing `canvas-actions-disabled` kill switch turns every verb off per team.

## Docs update

None. Each verb ships its own authoring docs through the registry endpoint, which is what agents read.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.1

`/writing-tests` and `/writing-pr-descriptions` applied. The web confirm rule was a decision in the session: prompt only for destructive and paid verbs, to match Desktop, instead of for every write. Membership assertions read through the cohort count and the error tracking facade because the persons DB router blocks direct ORM reads in tests.

## Problem

When a schema's sync method changes to webhook, the switch leaves a data gap. The last batch sync ran at some point in the past. The webhook only captures changes from registration onward. Every row that changed between those two moments never reaches the table, and nothing in the switch path reconciles that window.

A user hit this on a Stripe `customer` schema that moved from full replica to webhook. They recovered by running one more full replica and then switching to webhook again.

The switch path only registers the consumer hog function — `_maybe_create_webhook` at `products/warehouse_sources/backend/presentation/views/external_data_schema.py:1138`, into `products/data_warehouse/backend/logic/external_data_source/webhooks.py`. It does not set `reset_pipeline` and does not trigger a refresh.

## Describe the solution you'd like

When `sync_type` changes to webhook: register the webhook first, then run one catch-up sync with the previous method.

- Cursor-based incremental catch-up where the table has an incremental field.
- Full refresh only where it does not.

Overlap is safe, because rows merge by key. A gap is not.

Warehouse syncs bill per row, so this probably should not fire silently. An opt-in prompt at switch time ("Run a catch-up sync now?") may be the right shape. That part is a product call for the owning team.

## Precedent already in the code

Two nearby paths do this kind of reconciliation:

- Re-enabling a paused webhook schema (`should_sync` False → True) sets `reset_pipeline` and triggers a refresh, "so a gap from the off-window gets filled" (`external_data_schema.py:1024`).
- A sync-type change into or out of XMIN forces `reset_pipeline` and a refresh (`external_data_schema.py:1012`).

A switch to webhook has the same gap property, but no equivalent handling.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Document the gap and leave the behavior as is. Cheapest, but users lose rows silently and find out much later.
- Always force a full refresh on the switch. Correct, but expensive on large tables. The incremental path covers most cases for less cost.

## Additional context

Reported by a customer in Slack: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0BMHNZT1NZ/p1788511818073059?thread_ts=1788511818.073059&cid=C0BMHNZT1NZ

## Problem

The AI judge that confirms z-score flags (#140449, #140500) can reach only the projects listed by id in the `anomaly-scoring` payload. Three things stop it from becoming the default for every scored project.

- **No rollout lever.** `ai_judge.team_ids` is the only way to pick `default-v2`. There is no percentage and no "all projects" setting, unlike scoring itself (`self_driving_organization_percentage`).
- **A profile change discards the stored models.** `load_states` in `products/signals/backend/anomaly_scores/state.py` keeps a state row only when its `profile` equals the insight's resolved profile. A project that moves from `default-v1` to `default-v2` therefore has no state, and every insight goes back to a train step. The local part of `default-v2` is `default-v1`, so the stored models are still valid. A fleet rollout would queue a first train for every scored insight at once.
- **Every score step fetches the full training history.** In `scoring.py`, a profile with an AI member raises `history` to `history_buckets(scoring)` on every score step, so the judge has context. Most score steps flag nothing and make no model call, so the larger query is wasted. This removes much of the saving of the train and score split.

## Changes

1. **A rollout lever for the judge.** Add `ai_judge.organization_percentage` (0 to 100) to the payload. A project scores with `default-v2` when its id is in `team_ids`, or its organization is inside the percentage. Use the same fixed bucket per organization as `organization_rollout_bucket`, so an organization keeps its place as the percentage grows. Add `ai_judge.skip_team_ids` to keep one project on `default-v1`. Per-deployment overrides must keep working, as they do for the other keys.
2. **Stored models survive the profile change, in both directions.** A state row trained under `default-v1` is read by `default-v2`, and the reverse, when the local part of the two profiles has the same identity. Proposed: key the state row by the local part (a model profile name that both profiles share), not by the profile name that the events carry. `plan_run` and `score_ready_by_insight` then return a score step for these insights. Events still record the real profile and detector version.
3. **History is fetched only when the judge needs it.** A score step fetches the same buckets as `default-v1`. When at least one new bucket is flagged and a model call is allowed by the caps, it fetches the judge's history for that insight, then calls the judge. A score step with no flagged bucket runs the same queries as `default-v1`. Count the second fetch in the pick's query cost and CPU spend.
4. **Telemetry to read the rollout.** The tick event reports how many scored projects resolved to `default-v2`. The pick event reports whether the judge's history was fetched.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the judge prompt or its verdicts, including repeated flags for one episode across runs.
- Showing the judge's rationale in the Anomalies tab or in anomaly search.
- Sparse series and data gaps (#138647).

## Acceptance

- With `ai_judge.organization_percentage` at 100 and an empty `team_ids`, every scored project resolves to `default-v2`. At 0 only `team_ids` do. A project in `skip_team_ids` stays on `default-v1` in both cases.
- An insight with a current `default-v1` model gets a score step, not a train step, on its first visit after its project moves to `default-v2`. The same holds when the project moves back.
- A `default-v2` score step with no flagged bucket issues the same queries as a `default-v1` score step for the same insight.
- A `default-v2` score step with a flagged bucket gives the judge as much history as a train step does.
- The caps per insight per run and per project per day still hold, and a project without AI data processing consent still makes no model call.
- A project on `default-v1` scores exactly as before.

Refs #140449.

## Problem

Teams that run their tagging through Google Tag Manager have no way to bring that configuration into the PostHog data warehouse, so container and tag setup stays invisible to queries and monitoring. Requested by a customer as a P1.

Closes #79110

## Changes

- Adds a Google Tag Manager source syncing seven tables: accounts, containers, workspaces, tags, triggers, variables, and container versions (including archived versions).
- Auth is Google OAuth through a new `google-tag-manager` integration kind requesting the `tagmanager.readonly` scope. The kind fails closed with "Google Tag Manager app not configured" until the app credentials deploy, matching the other Google source kinds.
- Every table is full refresh: the GTM API has no modification-time filter, and the tables hold small configuration objects. The primary key is the resource `path`, the only identifier unique across parents (bare ids like `tagId` repeat per workspace).
- The GTM API allows 0.25 QPS and 10,000 requests per day, project-wide, shared by every connection through one OAuth app. The client spaces requests 4.5 s apart, honors `Retry-After`, and separates quota 403s (retried, then handed to Temporal as retryable) from permission 403s (fail the sync with a reconnect prompt).
- An optional account IDs field limits syncing to named GTM accounts; `validate_credentials` rejects IDs the connected user cannot access.
- Canonical table and column descriptions come from the GTM API reference, so semantic enrichment skips the LLM for this source.
- New Django migrations only re-list enum choices; both are SQL no-ops (verified with `sqlmigrate`).
- No screenshot: the new wizard tile and connect form render entirely from the registered source config and an icon already in the repo; no UI component changed.

> [!NOTE]
> Before OAuth connect works in production, ops needs to register the Google OAuth client (scope `tagmanager.readonly`, standard redirect URIs) and deploy `GOOGLE_TAG_MANAGER_APP_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_TAG_MANAGER_APP_CLIENT_SECRET` via charts to the web app and the data-warehouse Temporal worker, per the OAuth app deployment reference. Given the shared 0.25 QPS project quota, requesting a GTM API quota increase for that project is worth doing at the same time. A follow-up worth considering before GA: routing this source through `posthog/egress/` so concurrent syncs share one Redis-backed budget.

## How did you test this code?

- Transport tests: quota-vs-permission 403 routing (a permission 403 must never be retried; a quota 403 must never disable the source), page-token advance, three-level fan-out path construction, the account filter pruning the walk, and the `includeDeleted` param reaching version_headers.
- Source tests: OAuth error mapping to reconnect prompts (raw `RefreshError` reprs must not leak to users), full-refresh-only schema declarations, and account-filter validation including the paginated-probe case.
- Ran the registry-wide source guard suites and the OAuth integration model tests locally; repo-wide mypy is clean, and the frontend type check reports no new errors against the master baseline.
- Not run: a live sync against the real GTM API. The OAuth app is not registered yet, so the source ships as `ALPHA` with request/response shapes verified against the GTM API v2 reference instead.

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

Companion posthog.com PR adds `/docs/cdp/sources/google-tag-manager` (linked in comments once open). `audit_source_docs` passes against that checkout.

Follows #127411.

## Problem

Agents and API callers wait a long time on `GET /signals/reports/for_me/` and the `inbox-reports-for-me` MCP tool.
The endpoint and the tool description both say the call returns at once and does not wait on the model.
The model is not the cost: reads that reuse a stored list and start no wait are slow too.

- On one large production project, these reads took more than ten seconds.
- #127411 measured candidate gathering locally at 36 queries and 0.1s to 0.5s, so the local numbers hide this.
- A call with `wait_seconds` can take much longer than its wait, so MCP clients can time out on the documented maximum of 30.
- Each slow read holds a web worker. The build limits do not cover reads.

The scheduled tick in #127617 checks each person's input hash with the same gathering, so its cost grows with this too.

The cause is not confirmed. `gather_candidates` is the likely place, because every read runs it before the freshness check.

## Proposed behavior

Read `products/signals/backend/personal_ranking/serve.py` and `candidates.py` first.

1. **Measure first.** Time each phase of a read in production: pool queries, report load, priorities, PR state, predictions, needs-you facts, the activity summary read, and the input hash. Record the timings on the `personal inbox ranking read` event, next to `duration_ms`.
2. **Fix what dominates.** Make the slow queries cheaper with better predicates, indexes or fewer pools. Add indexes with a safe migration.
3. **If that is not enough, add a cheap path for a fresh stored list.** Check only the stored `candidate_ids` when the list is inside `freshness_minutes`, and skip the pool queries. A report that is new since the build then joins at the next rebuild, not on this read. Write down this trade-off in the PR, because it changes when a list goes stale.
4. **Bound the whole call.** Measure `wait_seconds` from the start of the request, so that gathering spends the same budget. A call with `wait_seconds` of N returns close to N seconds, with whatever list it has and `building: true`.
5. **Keep the description true.** If a read still cannot return quickly, change "returns at once" in the view and in `products/signals/mcp/tools.yaml`. Regenerate the MCP schema.

Do not read from the Today or Inbox list paths, and do not change the ranking, the prompt or the candidates a build uses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The read event records the time of each phase, so a production read shows which phase is slow.
- [ ] A read that reuses a stored list runs a fixed number of queries, whatever the number of reports in the project. A test asserts this count.
- [ ] A call with `wait_seconds` set returns within that budget plus a small margin, including gathering time.
- [ ] A stored list still goes stale when a candidate's status, PR state or score changes.
- [ ] The PR states the before and after timings, measured on a project with a large inbox.

## Scope

Backend, plus the tool description if it must change. #127617 edits the same freshness check in `serve.py`, so whichever lands second rebases onto the other. A separate issue covers the extra build that a slow read can queue.

## Bug Description

The web analytics Max filter tool sees about a fifth of the property taxonomy it should. Most core properties never reach its system prompt, so it cannot suggest a filter on them.

`WebAnalyticsFilterNode._filter_properties_by_type` keeps only entries that carry a `type` field:

https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/web_analytics/backend/max_tools.py#L158-L164

`type` is optional on `CoreFilterDefinition`, and most entries omit it. Measured against `CORE_FILTER_DEFINITIONS_BY_GROUP` on master, after the `system` / `ignored_in_assistant` entries are already excluded:

| Group | Should be visible | Reaches the prompt | Dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_properties` | 445 | 87 | 358 |
| `person_properties` | 511 | 91 | 420 |
| `session_properties` | 49 | 22 | 27 |

`format_properties_xml` applies the same `type is None` skip a second time, so removing only the first filter is not enough.

The drop is silent. Nothing logs it and no test covers it, so the tool just behaves as though those properties do not exist.

## How to reproduce

1. Ask Max to filter web analytics on a core property with no `type` in the taxonomy, for example `$referring_domain` or `$geoip_country_name`.
2. The model has never been shown the property, so it cannot build the filter.

## Suggested fix

`posthog/taxonomy/taxonomy.py` now exports `visible_definitions(group)`, which yields the entries of a taxonomy group an LLM prompt may show, with no type requirement. Routing `_filter_properties_by_type` through it fixes the selection.

The renderer still needs to handle a missing type. `format_properties_xml` groups entries under type-named tags, so an untyped entry has no tag to go in. Either give it a fallback bucket, or emit `<type>` as an optional child the way `products/cdp/backend/prompts.py` does.

## Context

Found while fixing the same class of bug for the CDP filter tool, where a stale hand-copied taxonomy had drifted. The CDP fix is in `products/cdp/backend/prompts.py` and shows one way to render untyped entries.

## Additional context

Whether `type` should stay optional on `CoreFilterDefinition` is worth a separate look. Two independent consumers have now treated a missing `type` as "skip this entry", which suggests the field reads as more load-bearing than it is.

## Problem

- Agents on projects with no saved metrics call `metric-list` before metric-shaped questions and get an empty result every time.
- Each empty lookup costs a turn. Context: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C27FSAW2G/p1794412394386969

## Changes

- Projects with no saved metrics skip `metric-list`, even where a skill says to call it first.
- They keep the save offer, the no-match marker, and `learn analytics` where learn is on.
- Projects with metrics, or a failed read, keep the current prompt.
- The MCP reads a new `metric_availability` endpoint, which skips the HogQL schema build the metrics list runs.
- Eval fixes: the judge reads a scout's `finish` report, and long case names fit the org name.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    A1[MCP session start] --> B1[metrics list, limit 1] --> C1[HogQL schema build]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[MCP session start] --> B2[metric_availability] --> C2[one exists query]
  end
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  class A1,A2 phYellow;
  class B1,B2 phRed;
  class C1,C2 phGray;
```

## MCP Analytics

- Events from sessions with `metric-list` carry `metric_catalog_mode` (`lookup`, `empty`, `unknown`), so the drop in empty lookups is measurable. Server property only, no SDK change.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** gating cases render each prompt surface per catalog state. The endpoint test fails if it counts deleted metrics or builds the schema.

- Not rerun: the evals after the endpoint switch, since each state's prompt is unchanged.

## Problem

Most reports come from the research pipeline, not from scouts.
Research already makes one structured LLM call that writes the title and summary (`ReportPresentationOutput` in `report_generation/research.py`).
That call could also return a few tags at almost no extra cost, but has no field for them.

## Proposal

Depends on the report tags storage issue (the `SignalReport.tags` column and the `set_report_tags` helper).

- Add an optional `tags: list[str]` field to `ReportPresentationOutput`, carried through `ReportResearchOutput`. Invalid slugs are normalized or dropped with a warning; a bad tag never fails the research run.
- Persist the tags with the title and summary when the run settles. Research replaces the whole set on each pass, the same way it replaces title, summary and charts.
- Put the report's current tags in the presentation prompt, so research can keep good tags.
- Put the team's existing report vocabulary in the prompt: the most used report tags in the team (for example the top 20 to 30 by count). This lets the vocabulary grow from use with no maintained list, the same idea as the scout tag-vocabulary loop.
- The field description says tags are short topic slugs, and that they do not repeat what the title type/scope, source or priority already say.

## Out of scope

- Tags from scouts (separate issue).
- Any controlled vocabulary or namespaces. Free-form slugs first; structure can come later.

## Acceptance

- A research pass that settles a report writes its tags.
- A later pass can keep, change or clear them.
- The prompt shows the team's existing report tags, and the query that builds that list is bounded.

Some metrics fail with a `validation_error` on every recalculation until someone edits them. Each scheduled run, page load heal, or config change still sends them to the calc activity, and the error comes back the same each time.

This is PR 1 of a stack for a pre-run recalculation skip classifier. It stacks on #120818, which stores the calculation key on every `metric_errors` entry. Later PRs add one check each, and the frontend copy for skipped metrics.

<!-- Does this fix an issue? Uncomment the line below with the issue ID to automatically close it when merged -->

## Changes

<!-- For each change a person can notice, say what they will now see or do differently, not only the code path that does it. Mark the rest as mechanical so a reviewer knows nothing user-visible is hiding in it. -->

<!-- If there are frontend changes, please include screenshots. For a new interaction that one screenshot cannot show, a short GIF or animated WebP of the flow can replace the after screenshot. -->
<!-- PostHog employees: `hogli pr:upload-image <file>` uploads to the public PostHog/pr-assets repo and prints markdown to paste here. Never upload customer data, secrets, or internal info. -->

Discovery now skips a metric whose latest failure is a `validation_error` with the same calculation key as now, behind the `experiments-recalculations-skip-failing-metrics` organization flag. With the flag off (shadow mode), discovery sends `experiment metric would skip` and the metric runs as usual. No frontend changes, so there are no screenshots; PR 2 adds the frontend copy.

### Pure skip modules

`skip_recalculation` holds the `@frozen` types (`MetricKey`, `MetricHistory`, `MetricRunOutcome`, `MetricSkip`) and `find_metric_skips`, which runs the checks in order and keeps the first skip per metric. A check that raises is logged and returns no skip. Every trigger skips, `manual_retry` included, so only a new calculation key ends a skip. `skip_recalculation_checks` holds the one check for this PR. Neither module reads the database.

- `products/experiments/backend/metric_calculation/skip_recalculation.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/metric_calculation/skip_recalculation_checks.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/test/test_skip_recalculation.py`

### Discovery writes the skip

Discovery reads the latest two terminal runs of the experiment in one query and builds a `MetricHistory` per metric. Discovery is per experiment, so a lateral join is not needed. A skip entry from an earlier run reads as the failure it skipped, so the skip holds until the metric changes. Any error in skip planning skips nothing. With the flag on, each skipped metric gets a `metric_errors` entry (`step: "skipped"`, `error_type: "metric_skipped"`, `skipped_error_type`, `skip_reason`, `failed_recalculation_id`, `failed_at`). That entry keeps the frontend gap check from starting a heal loop.

### The calc activity fails the metric early

The calc activity finds the skip entry, sends `experiment metric error` with `error_type: "metric_skipped"`, `skipped_error_type` and `skip_reason`, and returns a failure before any query. The run ends failed, the same as for any other `metric_errors` entry. `metric_skipped` joins `NON_RETRYABLE_ERROR_TYPES`. The workflow code does not change, so no `workflow.patched` gate is needed.

- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/recalculation_logic.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/models.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/test_recalculation_activities.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/ARCHITECTURE.md` (also corrects which failures show "Try again": only a retriable one, and no failure starts a heal)

### Known limit: what the key does not cover

Key version 1 hashes the metric definition, the start date, the stats method, the stored exposure criteria, maturity and the excluded variants. A fix in any of these places keeps the key, so the metric stays skipped:

- The end date and the analysis window.
- Stats settings beyond the method: the Bayesian prior and interval, the frequentist alpha, sequential testing, and the baseline variant.
- CUPED settings.
- The feature flag variants and the aggregation group type.
- Team settings: test account filters, the time zone, and the team defaults for sequential testing and CUPED.
- Definitions the metric references: actions, cohorts, warehouse tables and their schema, property types, and HogQL modifiers.

The shadow events show how often a skip of this kind happens before the flag turns on.

hits.body:
## Problem

Research writes impact metrics and charts with the same guidance for every report, whatever its signals came from.
That guidance fits some sources and is wrong for others, so source types that should almost always carry a measurement often ship without one.

Error tracking shows it most clearly:

- Since mid-September, about 20–24% of ready error-tracking pipeline reports carry a chart or an impact metric. Over the same period their chart rate fell from about 21% to about 6% as metrics replaced charts.
- Most of the rest are low-volume issues, and their summaries explain that the count is "too small for a useful metric".
- Prose explaining a skipped metric has become more common since #116221 asked research to say why it skips one. The skips themselves follow the generic metric rule in `_REPORT_METRICS_GUIDANCE` (`report_generation/research.py`): "A weak number is worse than none: … a one-off migration crash … or a count with no person context … a report with no metric beats a report with a weak metric." That rule describes most error-tracking reports almost exactly.
- For an error-tracking issue, the occurrence count of that issue is the before-and-after measure of whether a fix worked, at any volume. One occurrence is a valid baseline, because the fix is judged on it not coming back.

The source is already visible to research: `_render_signal_for_research` prints `source_product / source_type` for each signal.
But the presentation step, where charts and metrics are written (`build_report_presentation_prompt`), takes no source information. Its only switches are feature flags.

Scope: the research pipeline only. Scout prompts are out of scope.

## Proposal

### 1. Per-source evidence playbooks in the research prompt

Add a small registry in `products/signals/backend/report_generation/`, keyed by `source_product`, owned by the Signals team.
Each playbook entry is a few lines:

- the default metric `kind` and query shape for this source
- when a chart is worth it, and which chart
- what to leave in prose

Render only the entries for sources present in the report's signals, into the presentation prompt next to `_REPORT_METRICS_GUIDANCE` and `_REPORT_CHARTS_GUIDANCE`.
The generic guidance stays as the fallback for sources with no entry.
For a mixed-source report, render each relevant entry, and let research pick the primary metric from the report's central claim.
A playbook entry overrides the generic "weak number" rule for its source where they conflict, and the prompt says so explicitly.

Start with the two highest-volume data-shaped sources, and let the rest fall back to the generic text:

| Source | Metric default | Chart |
|---|---|---|
| `error_tracking` | Always a `primary` metric for the issue: `$exception` events filtered on `$exception_issue_id` with a structured property filter. Use `affected_users` (`math: dau`) when the events carry person context, `occurrences` otherwise. Low volume is not a reason to omit it. | Attach an occurrences-over-time chart when the issue shows a burst, a rising trend, or spread across many users. Skip a chart for a handful of events. |
| `replay_vision` | `affected_sessions` (`math: unique_session`) on the event or action that marks the observed problem, when one exists. | Chart when the observation rate moves over time. |

Other entries (health checks, conversations, Linear, GitHub, pganalyze) can follow in later PRs with their own measured baselines.

### 2. Deterministic floor for error tracking

Research can still omit the metric even with a playbook, so the pipeline also guarantees one:

- After the presentation result is resolved, if the report has `error_tracking` signals and the resolved metric set has no `primary` metric, add an `occurrences` metric for the issue.
- Use the signal's `source_id`, which is the error-tracking issue ID (see `emit_issue_lifecycle_signal` in `products/error_tracking/backend/temporal/lifecycle/side_effects.py`).
- Use the default inclusive window (`-13d`, daily) and a plain title naming the issue.
- When several error-tracking issues share a report, one metric can filter on all of their issue IDs.
- Issue merges can move a fingerprint to another issue after its events were captured, so check whether a filter on the event property `$exception_issue_id` misses merged events. If it does, prefer the issue's current fingerprints or the error-tracking query path.
- Never replace or edit a metric that research authored. The floor fills a gap only.
- Respect the existing `signals-report-metrics` organization flag and the whole-set limits in `report_metrics.py`. Build the metric through the same validation path as research-authored metrics, so it gets the same access-policy checks.
- Persist it in the same transition as the rest of the metric set, so the "atomic with prose" contract in `report_generation/AGENTS.md` still holds.

### 3. Docs

Update `products/signals/backend/report_generation/AGENTS.md`: the impact-metrics and charts sections, plus a short section on the playbook registry and the floor.

## Acceptance criteria

- `build_report_presentation_prompt` receives the report's source products and renders only the matching playbook entries. A report with no matching source gets today's prompt unchanged.
- Prompt tests cover: an error-tracking report, a replay-vision report, a mixed report, and a report with an unknown source.
- Floor tests cover: a metric is added when error-tracking research returns none, is not added when research returned a primary metric, is not added when the metrics flag is off, and passes `report_metrics.py` validation.
- No Temporal workflow command changes. If the floor needs one, gate it with `workflow.patched(...)`.

## How we'll know it worked

Track weekly per source, for ready pipeline reports (`scout_emitted = 0`), the share with a chart, with an impact metric, and with either.
Success for error tracking: the impact-metric rate reaches 90% or more with the floor, and the chart rate rises among issues with a burst or trend.
Replay vision should show its own lift in metric rate, without its chart rate falling.

## Feature request

Let a user pick which model the AI detector uses (the `llm` detector type on insight alerts), per alert. Start with two models only:

| Shown as | Model id | Provider | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | `claude-haiku-5-5` | Anthropic | The default, and what every AI alert uses today |
| GPT-6 Luna | `gpt-6-luna` | OpenAI | New for this detector |

### Why

The AI detector runs on one hard-coded model, `LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"` in `products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`. A user whose metric is judged badly by that model has no second option, and we have no way to learn which model users prefer for which metrics.

#130917 proposed a model registry with shadow calls and was parked until someone asked for a per-alert model choice. This issue is that request, without the shadow part.

### Where the code is

- The judge is Anthropic-only: `build_ai_gateway_anthropic_client`, then `messages.parse(output_format=LLMDetectionVerdict)` with `thinking` disabled (`products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`).
- The chart is sent as an Anthropic base64 `image` block (`products/alerts/backend/judge/prompt.py`).
- The detector config has one field, `instructions` (`LLMDetectorConfig` in `frontend/src/queries/schema/schema-general.ts`).
- The API validates the config in `products/alerts/backend/presentation/views/alert.py`. The Max tool in `products/alerts/backend/max_tools.py` is the second writer.
- The editor renders the instructions field in `products/alerts/frontend/views/DetectorSelector.tsx`.
- Read `products/alerts/AGENTS.md` first. Its cost and gating rules all still apply.

### Proposal

**Config and API**

- [ ] Add an optional `model` to `LLMDetectorConfig`, an enum of exactly `claude-haiku-5-5` and `gpt-6-luna`. A config with no `model` means Haiku, so existing alerts need no migration and do not change behavior.
- [ ] Reject any other value with a 400 in the API validator. The Max tool goes through the same validation.
- [ ] Simulate takes the same field, so a preview runs on the model the alert will use.
- [ ] Regenerate the schema and OpenAPI types (`hogli build:openapi`), and update the MCP tool descriptions for alert create, update and simulate, plus `products/alerts/skills/authoring-insight-alerts/SKILL.md`.

**Judge**

- [ ] Replace the single constant with a small registry keyed by model id. Each entry holds the provider, how the client is built, how the chart image is encoded, and how structured output is requested and parsed into `LLMDetectionVerdict`.
- [ ] Add the OpenAI path through the AI gateway. Send the chart as an image data URL. Keep the same `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `PROMPT_REVISION` and `ai_product` (`alert_llm_detector`).
- [ ] Keep every guard on both paths: the access check, the AI credit budget check, the `X-PostHog-Billable` and `X-PostHog-Privacy-Mode` headers, the gateway credit-refusal handling, the model-call slot, the request timeout and the single in-request retry.
- [ ] The OpenAI call must be attributed and charged to the alert's team, the same as the Anthropic call is through `team_id` today.
- [ ] Use the alert's model in the verdict memo key and in `SeriesJudgment.model`, in place of the constant, so each check records the model that produced it.
- [ ] The Haiku quirks stay on the Haiku entry only (no sampling params, `thinking` disabled). Do not copy them to the OpenAI entry.

**Editor**

- [ ] Add a model select to the AI detector section, next to the instructions field. Default to Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [ ] Show the model on each AI check in the alert history, because an alert's model can change during its life.
- [ ] Follow `/writing-user-facing-copy` for the label and help text.

**Docs and rules**

- [ ] Update the comment on `LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL` and `products/alerts/AGENTS.md`, which both say the model is not exposed per alert.
- [ ] Add the cost story that `AGENTS.md` asks for: calls per check stay at one, so only the price per call changes with the model.

### Constraints

- Two models only. No free-text model id, and no frontier models.
- One model call per check, as today. No shadow call and no fallback from one model to the other. A check that cannot reach a verdict records an error.
- The feature stays behind `alerts-llm-detector`, with the same per-project cap, cadence rules and AI data processing consent check.
- The new OpenAI call site must pass `.semgrep/rules/security/` (see the OpenAI HIPAA-eligible endpoints rule).
- Changing the model on an existing alert does not clear its earlier flags. The prompt still marks the points that earlier AI checks fired on, whichever model produced them.

### Acceptance

- A new AI alert with no model chosen runs on `claude-haiku-5-5`, and an alert saved before this change behaves exactly as it did.
- An alert saved with `gpt-6-luna` is judged by that model on scheduled checks and in simulate. Its check metadata and its `$ai_generation` event both name that model.
- `detector_config: {"type": "llm", "model": "anything-else"}` is rejected on create, update and simulate.
- With the rollout flag off, or with AI credits exhausted, a `gpt-6-luna` alert pauses the same way a Haiku alert does.
- Tests cover: the default, the rejected value, the OpenAI verdict parsing, the memo key changing with the model, and the paused paths on the OpenAI entry.

### Open questions

- Does the organization's AI data processing consent already cover sending alert data to OpenAI, or does the picker need to say which provider each model uses?
- Do the two models cost a similar number of AI credits per check? If not, the editor should say so next to the select.
- Should the allowed models also be listed in the `alerts-llm-detector` flag payload, so one model can be turned off without a deploy? If so, an alert on a model that is turned off should pause (`LLMDetectorPausedError`), not be disabled.

### Out of scope

- Shadow calls and model comparison (#130917).
- A project-level or organization-level default model.
- More than two models.

## Problem

- PostHog Code and Tasks sessions cannot use MCP connections that split writes (related: #138684).
- On those connections the server lists `exec-read` and `exec-write` instead of `exec`, and the agent harness only gates `exec`.
- The server keeps these sessions on `exec` until the harness handles both tools.

## Changes

- `exec-read` and `exec-write` sub-tools that the permission regex names now prompt exactly like `exec` ones. This covers the Claude hook, the Codex approval prompt and the cloud permission relay.
- `exec-read` is gated too: the Tasks regex names cross-project calls, which can read, so the harness keeps its own check there.
- A deny, ask or allow rule written for `exec` also covers `exec-read` and `exec-write`, so existing rules survive the split.
- An "always allow" on a gated sub-tool now holds for that dispatcher only. Approving it on `exec-read` no longer lets `exec-write` run it. Approvals stored before the split count for `exec` only.
- Bypass permissions mode now prompts for gated sub-tools on all three tools in cloud runs. Before, the prompt fired only when an allow rule already matched the tool.
- Usage tracking and pi tool-call parsing recognise all three tools. Pi's sanitized `exec_read` and `exec_write` names parse too.
- Plain `exec` behaves as before.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** New cases extend the nearest existing tests. Each one failed when `exec-write` was dropped from the gated list, when approvals lost the dispatcher, when the hook asked only on an allow rule, or when it dropped an `exec` ask rule for the split tools.

- A scratch run drove the real Claude adapter and SDK against a stub `posthog` MCP server and a scripted model, in default, auto and bypass modes, locally and in the cloud. It reproduced each review point before the fix and passed after it.
- Not tested: the Codex adapter end to end, and a live split-writes connection.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

- **Decisions:** `POSTHOG_GATED_EXEC_TOOLS` is the one list behind the gating regex and the Codex `approval_mode` map. Approval keys are `<dispatcher>:<sub-tool>`, and plain `exec` keeps the bare sub-tool so existing approvals still apply to it.
- **Follow-ups:** lift the server rule that never splits connections sending `x-posthog-mcp-consumer`.

### Bug Description

The query planner and the schema generators put the current time, to the second, ahead of their static prompt, because they don't pass `conversation_start_dt` (the root agent does). The prompt prefix changes on every call, so the provider's prompt cache can't match it. The planner resends an ~84K-token static prompt on each step at full input price.

## How to reproduce

1. Local build with real OpenAI calls through the planner and Trends generator.
2. Make 2 calls in one conversation.
3. Compare `cached_tokens` on the repeat call: planner 0 of 85,773, Trends generator 21,120 of 26,091.

## Additional context

Fix in #132240: with it, the same repeat calls cache 85,630 and 25,216.

### Debug info

```shell
- [x] Local build at 1ae146752f24592906cae6e8dd317d8eb369c5c6, not PostHog Cloud
```

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

When a production issue happens, teams want to know if a prompt change caused it. Today they must open each prompt to see its version history. There is no single view of all prompt changes across the project.

## Describe the solution you'd like

A global prompt history: one activity feed for all prompts in the project, with who changed which prompt, when, and what changed (new version, label moved, prompt archived). `LLMPrompt` and `LLMPromptLabel` are already activity-logged scopes, so this can build on the existing activity log.

Useful additions:

- Filter by prompt, by label (for example only `production` label changes), and by time range.
- Show prompt changes as annotations on LLM analytics charts, so a change lines up with a metric shift.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

The per-prompt version history. It does not help when you do not know which prompt changed.

## Additional context

From customer feedback on prompt management.

hits.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Customers who have signed a BAA with PostHog cannot use any of PostHog's AI features. Per [the HIPAA compliance docs](https://posthog.com/docs/privacy/hipaa-compliance), PostHog AI and other AI features are not covered by BAAs and should not be enabled in an organization where any project processes protected health information (PHI). Signing a BAA through the app automatically turns off third-party AI data processing for the whole organization, and the in-app consent prompt says the same thing. The practical effect is that healthcare customers on paid plans lose PostHog AI, session summaries, replay vision, and anything else that sends data to an AI subprocessor, across every project in the organization, including projects that hold no PHI. Several customers in regulated healthcare have asked whether this will change.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Bring AI features under BAA coverage so organizations handling PHI can use them, or publish a supported path that lets those organizations use some AI features safely. Two shapes would each help, and they are independent:

1. Full coverage: route AI workloads only through model providers where the necessary agreements and data handling terms are in place, then remove AI features from the list of services excluded from the BAA.
2. Partial coverage: allow AI features to be enabled per project rather than per organization, so a project with no PHI can use them while PHI projects stay opted out. This is much narrower and needs no change in provider coverage.

Either way, publishing which AI features and which providers are in scope would let customers map this onto their own compliance requirements instead of asking support.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Leaving AI features disabled. This is the current guidance and what the app enforces on BAA signature. It works, but BAA customers get no value from any AI feature.
- Splitting PHI and non-PHI work across separate PostHog organizations so AI features can stay on in the non-PHI one. Possible today, but it means duplicated setup, billing, and team management, and no cross-organization analysis.
- Self-hosting, which the docs note is only suitable for smaller event volumes and lacks advanced features.

## Additional context

### Current behavior

- [posthog.com/docs/privacy/hipaa-compliance](https://posthog.com/docs/privacy/hipaa-compliance) lists AI features and the managed reverse proxy as the only services not covered by a BAA.
- Signing a BAA in the app sets the organization's AI data processing approval to off and emails the organization owners. The opt-out is organization-wide, not per project.
- The AI consent prompt tells admins that AI features are not HIPAA compliant and that an existing BAA does not cover them.

### Related issues

- #17504 (HIPAA compliance, closed February 2024) predates AI features, so it does not cover this.

Filed by PostHog support on behalf of multiple customer requests.

Implement a `forecast(vals, steps)` function in HogQL that does N `steps` of forecasting given a timeseries in vals (array of values).

From that it returns a 3-tuple `Tuple(p10 Array(Float64), p50 Array(Float64), p90 Array(Float64))` with the p10, p50 and p90 timeseries.

This should enable adding forecasting to any timeseries plot we have in posthog.

It is gated behind a feature flag and it only support Clickhouse for now since it relies on enriching the data on our side then sending it back to clickhouse by creating a temporary table.

The current implementation is not ideal since it runs the model in CPU in memory, but it's a very tiny model that runs in 15ms in CPU and uses around 200MB of memory so for some internal testing it should be fine. If we want to productize we could move it to some dedicated instances.

## Problem

Every signals scout run gets the same fixed runtime budget: `DEFAULT_MAX_RUNTIME_S = 15 * 60` in `products/signals/backend/scout_harness/limits.py`. The constant's comment currently says tuning it is a config decision, not a per-run override knob.

That one-size budget no longer fits the fleet:

- The per-scout model pin (#78764) lets an owner run a scout on a slower frontier model. A pinned scout can be doing correct, on-script work and still get killed by `poll_for_turn: timed out after 900s` because a single judging generation takes several minutes. Five such timeouts in a row trip the failure-streak breaker and auto-pause the scout, so a healthy scout+model pairing reads as a broken lane.
- Batch-scale measurement scouts (structured-output judges scoring ~100 entities per run) sit near the wall even on default models.
- Conversely, cheap watchdog scouts that close out in under a minute could take a tighter budget as a cost/safety bound.

## Proposal

Add an optional per-scout max runtime to `SignalScoutConfig`, as an **enum of sanctioned values rather than a free integer**: `5 / 15 / 30 / 45 / 60` minutes.

- Default stays exactly as today: null means 15 minutes, no behavior change for any existing config.
- 60 minutes is the hard upper bound.
- No feature-flag gate. Unlike the model pin this is a general need - some scouts just need longer or shorter runtimes - and an enum with a capped ceiling bounds the blast radius on its own.
- Exposed on the config API / `scout-config-update` like `model` and `network_access`.

An enum keeps validation trivial, keeps the coordinator's capacity math predictable (a run can only hold a sandbox lease for one of five known durations), and leaves room to grow the ladder later without a migration.

## Implementation notes

Both enforcement points are already set per dispatch, so the plumbing is small:

- `start_to_close_timeout` on the agent activity (`temporal/agentic/scout_scheduler.py`) - currently `DEFAULT_MAX_RUNTIME_S + ACTIVITY_SLACK_S`.
- `max_poll_seconds` passed to `MultiTurnSession` (`scout_harness/runner.py`). Note `poll_for_turn`'s own `MAX_POLL_SECONDS` default is already 30 min; scouts pass 900s down.

Things the PR must handle:

- `STALE_RUN_CUTOFF_S` (the orphan reaper) derives from the global ceiling. It must key off the **max allowed** budget (60 min) or the run's own stamped budget, otherwise a legitimately long run gets reaped alive.
- Stamp a non-default budget on the run row `metadata` (like `model` / `runtime_adapter`) and carry it on the `signals_scout_run_started` / `_finished` lifecycle events, so timeout rates stay sliceable across mixed budgets.
- The dropped-finalization salvage window in `custom_prompt_internals.py` is tuned relative to the budget it is given - verify it still fires sensibly at 45-60 min.
- A budget longer than the scout's `run_interval_minutes` self-throttles via the `_has_running_run` single-flight guard; fine, but worth a test and a docs sentence.
- Update the `limits.py` comment that says this is deliberately not a per-run knob.
- Longer leases cost more sandbox time per run; the enum ceiling plus the existing per-team run caps bound this, but the config UI help text should say a bigger budget means a more expensive run.

## Out of scope

- Free-form integer budgets.
- Per-run (as opposed to per-scout) overrides.
- Changing the coordinator tick or the per-team run caps.

## Problem

A person who wants the inbox to act on what is said in Slack has no way to set that up from the inbox. The Sources tab lists error tracking, issue trackers and other sources, but not Slack.

Reading Slack is possible today: a scout can query the Slack tables of the data warehouse. But the person has to know that, write the scout by hand and find the right table names. Someone who thinks of Slack as a source looks on the Sources tab and finds nothing.

## Proposal

Add a "Slack channels" entry to the Sources tab. It does not add a signal source. It helps a person create regular scouts that read the Slack channels they pick, through the data warehouse.

- A person can create as many Slack scouts as they want. Each has a name, a set of channels, a free-text steer on what to look for, and a schedule.
- Each one is a regular scout. It also shows on the Scouts tab, and everything a scout can do applies to it. The Sources tab is a second way in to the same objects.
- The whole feature sits behind a feature flag (see [Feature flag](#feature-flag)).

### Why scouts and not a signal source

- A signal source judges one record at a time. A Slack message is a fragment. The unit that means something is the thread.
- Threads gain replies for days. A scout can keep a watermark and dedupe on the thread root. A signal source has no memory between records.
- The source registry and the frontend's required-table check are static. Slack tables are named per channel ID, so the set of tables differs for every project.

## Problem

- When an OAuth MCP server (for example GitLab) rejects an expired token, PostHog AI shows a vague tool failure and never refreshes the token or asks the user to reconnect.
- The MCP transport cancels the pending call on a failed request. The real `HTTPStatusError` surfaces only in `close()`, as an `ExceptionGroup` that replaces the call's error.
- Raised in #posthog-inbox ([Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0B8ZE81ZT7/p1795685219863319?thread_ts=1795685219.863319&cid=C0B8ZE81ZT7)).

## Changes

- A 401 from an MCP server now refreshes the token and retries. If the refresh fails, PostHog AI asks the user to re-authenticate.
- Other HTTP statuses reach the agent as a retryable error that names the status, for example `HTTP 500`. They no longer mark the installation for re-authentication.
- `MCPClient` closes the transport when a call is cancelled and raises the request's error as `MCPClientError` with `status_code`. `close()` logs and does not raise.

## How did you test this code?

- `hogli test ee/hogai/tools/call_mcp_server/test/test_tool.py` and repo-wide `mypy` pass.
- A local script with an `httpx.MockTransport` 401 server showed `ExceptionGroup` before the fix and `MCPClientError` (401) after.
- Not tested against a real GitLab MCP server.

**Test rationale:** The new tests drive a real `MCPClient` against a fake HTTP server. A 401 on `initialize` or `tools/call` must refresh and retry. A 500 must not mark re-authentication. Existing tests mock `MCPClient`, so they cannot see the masking. All three tests fail on the old code.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** PostHog Slack app (Claude Code), claude-opus-5-5

**Skills:** None (read the repo guides for `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`)

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

<details>
