hits.message:
feat(devex): auto-quarantine proven flaky visual review snapshots (#133364)

* feat(visual-review): quarantine a proven flaky snapshot automatically

A flaky story fails the gate of merge queue runs and kicks every pull
request in the batch, and a person quarantines it hours later. The
backend already sees every full run on the default branch and on
trunk-merge/ branches, so it can prove a flake from those runs alone:
the same code rendered the story both ways against the same baseline.

- Superset proof: changed in run A, unchanged in run B whose tree holds
  all of A's tree (ancestry on the default branch, batch heads plus the
  batch base commit for merge queue runs).
- Disjoint proof: changed in two runs that share no pull request, and
  unchanged in a run created after the earlier one.
- Only `changed` against the default branch's baseline counts, so a
  pull request that broke the story or carried its own baseline never
  leads to a quarantine.
- Batch contents come from the GitHub compare API, from the Trunk
  merge commits on the test branch, cached by head SHA.

The check runs in finish_processing right before the recount, so a run
that completes a proof passes. Errors are logged and never fail the run.

Repo.auto_quarantine_mode (off by default, preview, on) gates it. On
quarantines for 14 days with source=auto and notifies the owning team.
A daily cap of 10 automatic quarantines per repo stops a capture harness
regression from being hidden. Each proof emits a vr_flake_proven event.

* fix(visual-review): accept a same-commit re-run as flake proof and report a proof once

- Two default-branch runs of one commit that render a story both ways
  are the strongest flake proof there is, and commit_contains already
  answers True for equal SHAs. The extra different-commit condition
  refused exactly that case.
- In preview mode, and in on mode past the daily cap, a proof is not
  applied, so the story stays provable and every later trusted run in
  the window logged it and emitted vr_flake_proven again. An atomic
  cache add per repo, run type and identifier for the proof window now
  reports it once, also when two runs finish together. A proof that
  quarantines needs no dedupe, because the quarantine removes the story
  from the next evaluation.
- Drop the backtest numbers from the daily limit comment, since they
  are a perishable measurement.

* chore: update OpenAPI generated types

* fix(visual-review): type the default baseline lookup

mypy rejected one variable holding both the finishing run's id (UUID) and the optional result of the newest default-branch run lookup (UUID | None), and then read the None branch as unreachable. A helper for the lookup gives each case its own type and keeps one early return.

* refactor(visual-review): decide flake proofs in a pure core and bound the reads

The proof search called GitHub while it decided, so a failure with no
clean superset could ask for the batch of every clean queue run in the
window, inline in run completion. The observation read pulled every
row of up to 25 stories across the whole window.

- Every proof now includes the finishing run, as a failing or the clean
  run. A proof without it was there when its last run finished, so
  this bounds the work without losing proofs.
- Pure core: proof_candidates (capped at 5 per story, superset first,
  newest first), batch_runs, ancestry_questions, first_proof over plain
  batch and ancestry mappings, and proof_action. No database, client
  or clock. The shell fetches only what the candidates name, memoized
  per evaluation, and asks GitHub nothing for a story without one.
- Reads: the changed-row read filters the quarantine flag in SQL; the
  default-branch baseline run comes from the window list; clean renders
  are read only from the finishing run, runs of its commit and the 20
  newest window runs.
- Two runs finishing together take an atomic 10 minute claim per story
  before quarantining, so one quarantine and one notice go out.
- The first proof the daily limit blocks in a window sends one Slack
  notice to the owner of products/visual_review/, routed like the
  digest's unowned items.
- The daily limit comment carries its durable reason plus a dated
  snapshot of the numbers behind 10.

* fix(visual-review): prove a flake only by a closing failure on held code

One failure followed by a clean run that holds it is no flake proof: a
fixing or reverting pull request renders the same way. Batch
disjointness by head SHA broke when a pull request was queued again
with a new commit, and a tolerated match of the failing picture read as
a clean render.

- A proof needs the finishing run to fail the story. Same commit: a
  clean run of its commit rendered another picture. Chain: fail in A,
  clean in B, fail again in the finishing run C, with B descending from
  A and C from B by git ancestry. A deterministic story would need a
  break, a fix and a second break in the window without a baseline edit.
- The clean picture must differ from every failing picture in the proof.
- Merge queue batch parsing (compare paging, Trunk commit regex,
  MergeQueueBatch) is gone; tree order is commit ancestry only.
- A run that fails no story leaves after one query, so nothing runs in
  the synchronous completion path. Candidates are built lazily up to 5
  per story, and one evaluation stops after 20 seconds.
- Branch and pull request number are client-supplied, so before a
  proof counts, its default-branch commits must be in the default
  branch head and its merge queue runs must pass the source PR check.
- The daily limit and the active-quarantine check are re-read under a
  lock on the repo row, so the count and the create are atomic across
  runs. This replaces the cache claim.
- One analytics capture context per evaluation.

* fix(visual-review): use a no-key repo lock and honor commit-scoped lifts

A plain FOR UPDATE on the repo row conflicts with the KEY SHARE lock
that a foreign-key check takes when a child row of the repo is inserted.
A run creation that holds its run row and waits for the repo could then
deadlock with the quarantine create, which waits for that run. FOR NO KEY
UPDATE still serializes the daily-limit count and the create across runs.

A quarantine lifted at a commit the finishing run does not contain still
covers the story for that run, as the gate already treats it. Without
excluding those stories, a re-run of an old commit could prove a flake
for a story that was fixed and lifted, and open a new quarantine. The
lookup asks GitHub, so it runs only when the run has failing rows; a run
without failing rows still leaves after one query.

* chore(visual-review): share the quarantine author label and trim comments

The "Quarantined automatically" decision sat inline in four components
that are already above the complexity limit. A pure helper in
lib/quarantineAuthor.ts now picks who quarantined a snapshot, so the
label text lives in one place and the components carry fewer branches.
Rendered text is unchanged, including the lowercase variant in the
snapshot card.

The automatic quarantine constants carried long comments; each now
keeps its reason in one or two lines, and the dated snapshot on the
daily limit stays.

The repo PATCH test now also sets auto_quarantine_mode, so the API
wiring of that field is covered.

hits.message:
feat(devex): lift visual review quarantines after 500 clean master runs (#133371)

* feat(visual-review): lift a quarantine after a clean week of runs

Quarantines pile up. The flakiness page flags a quarantine whose story
stopped failing, but a person still has to come back and lift it, so
most never get lifted.

- A full default-branch run queues release_clean_quarantines, at most
  once an hour per repo and run type (atomic cache add). The task
  checks with GitHub that the run is on the default branch.
- An active quarantine of any source lifts when it is at least 7 days
  old, the trusted runs (default branch and merge queue) of the last 7
  days hold at least 300 rows for the story, all unchanged, and the
  finishing run rendered it unchanged against a baseline. Any other
  result blocks, also a quarantined, approved or tolerated one.
- 7 days matches FLAKINESS_RATE_DAYS and merge queue run retention, so
  the window never reaches past stored runs. A shorter clean streak
  relapses too often to act on.
- The lift works like a manual one, scoped to the verifying run's
  commit, and records QuarantinedIdentifier.lift_reason (new field,
  migration 0023, exposed read-only on the quarantine entry).
- Pending lift requests on a lifted quarantine need no handling here:
  the next default-branch reconcile marks them superseded.
- Repo.auto_quarantine_mode now covers both directions. Preview logs
  and emits vr_quarantine_clean once per story per 24 hours.

The trusted-run helpers in auto_quarantine.py are public now so both
modules share one definition.

* fix(visual-review): read the clean week by run ids, not a run subquery

A subquery on the run lets the planner pick the identifier index and
read every run the repo stored. The flakiness reads hit the same shape
and anchor on a list of run ids for that reason.

* chore: update OpenAPI generated types

* fix(visual-review): lift a quarantine after 500 clean default-branch runs

A day count does not adapt to how busy a repo is: a slow week lifts on
too little evidence. In this repo's default-branch history 15 percent of
clean streaks relapsed after 300 runs and 3 percent after 500. The old
grouped count also read every unchanged row of the window, which
production plans showed at over a second.

- AUTO_LIFT_CLEAN_RUNS = 500 replaces the day and minimum run rules.
  The window starts at the 500th newest completed full default-branch
  run; with fewer such runs nothing lifts.
- A quarantine lifts when it predates the window, no trusted run since
  the window start has a changed, new or removed row for the story
  (whatever its quarantine, approval or toleration state), and the
  window's first run and the finishing run rendered it unchanged.
- The blocking-row read counts only hard results by a list of run ids,
  so it stays an index-only scan on the covering run/result index.
- is_clean is pure over one dataclass of plain values, no clock.
- lift_reason names the window's first commit; the event field is now
  clean_default_branch_runs.

* chore(visual-review): say that automatic release exists in the expiry comment

* fix(visual-review): keep the clean-window read on its index and the hourly slot on the default branch

- Count("*") instead of Count("id") in the blocking-row read: id is not
  in the covering run/result index, so counting it forced heap reads.
- The enqueue compares the run's branch with the default branch before
  taking the hourly cache slot, so a full run without a pull request on
  another branch can no longer use up the slot for the hour.
- One analytics capture context per task instead of one per event.
- Wording: merge queue runs are stored for 7 days and the window of 500
  default-branch runs is usually longer, so older merge queue failures
  are not visible. The module docstring, README and MCP tool text now
  say "every stored trusted run" and name the default-branch history as
  the evidence. Retention is unchanged.
- The render lookup returns a small dataclass instead of a tuple, for
  the tuple-return-prefer-dataclass semgrep rule.

* chore: update OpenAPI generated types

* fix(visual-review): check every render and the commit before a lift

The clean window checked for zero blocking rows plus an unchanged render
at the window's first run and at the finishing run. A story missing from
the runs in between had no rows there, so it still lifted without being
watched. A grouped count of the story's rows in the window's
default-branch runs, by their ids, now has to reach the number of those
runs. With zero blocking rows that means unchanged in every counted run,
so the separate read at the window start is dropped.

The run's branch name and commit are client-supplied, and the lift writes
the commit as lifted_at_sha. A run that names the default branch with an
off-branch commit would leave a lift that real default-branch runs do
not contain, so they would keep applying the quarantine. Before lifting,
and only when at least one quarantine is clean, GitHub must confirm the
commit is in the default branch head's history. Unknown head or not
contained: nothing lifts and a warning is logged. The head lookup is
shared with the proof-run check in auto_quarantine.

* fix(visual-review): anchor the lift window to its run and verify first

The hourly task can run after newer default-branch runs landed. The
window took the newest runs of the repo, while the lift records the
given run's commit as lifted_at_sha, so the evidence and the recorded
commit could describe different points. The window and the trusted-run
read for blocking rows now stop at the finishing run.

The GitHub check that the finishing commit is on the default branch ran
between the evidence read and the write. A run that completed with a
changed result during that request was missed. The check now runs
before the evidence read, so the read is the last step before the
write. That costs one GitHub lookup per hourly check, also when nothing
lifts.

* chore(visual-review): trim comments in the automatic lift

The CI report flagged a high comment density for the automatic lift.
Each comment now keeps only the reason the code cannot show: why a run
count and not days, why the commit is verified before the evidence read,
why the hourly throttle exists. The dated relapse snapshot on
AUTO_LIFT_CLEAN_RUNS stays.

feat(devex): extend visual review quarantines of stories that still differ (#138108)

* feat(devex): extend visual review quarantines of stories that still differ

Quarantines run out on a fixed date, also when the story still renders
differently on the default branch. Production data shows most such lapses
get re-quarantined by hand (roughly three in four), and PRs fail on the
story in between. Automatic quarantine does not catch these again: a story
that renders one fixed picture in every run (a stale baseline under
quarantine) never renders clean, so it is never proven flaky and fails
every merge queue run after the lapse.

- New rule in auto_extend: an active quarantine that expires within 48
  hours gets a fresh automatic quarantine (14 days) when its story rendered
  `changed` at least once in the last 100 full default-branch runs.
  Otherwise it lapses as planned. Any source counts (human, agent, auto).
- The extension goes through quarantine_identifier, the same path as
  automatic quarantine, so the old row is superseded the usual way. The
  row is locked and re-checked first, so a lift or replace by a person in
  between wins.
- When every recent render is the same changed picture, the reason says
  the baseline looks stale, so a person approves the picture instead of
  waiting for the next expiry.
- Runs from the hourly release task, after the lift. Follows
  auto_quarantine_mode: preview only logs and captures
  vr_quarantine_extend, once a day per story. Extensions skip the daily
  automatic quarantine limit (they hide nothing new) and are capped per
  run by AUTO_QUARANTINE_MAX_STORIES_PER_RUN.
- The owning team gets the quarantine notice, with a lead that says the
  quarantine was extended.
- auto_lift's docstring claimed a relapse needs no handling; corrected.

* chore(devex): trim auto-extend comments and record capture events in tests

The CI report flagged comment density above 3% and call assertions on the
capture mock. Comments that restated field names or the code are gone. The
tests now record the captured event names and assert on them, which is the
rule's real output in preview mode.

* fix(devex): keep visual review extensions out of the daily limit and lift requests

- Extensions no longer count toward the daily limit of automatic quarantines.
  They hide nothing new, and counting them blocked new flakes for a day after
  a batch of extensions. The reason prefix moves to contracts so the limit and
  the notice read one constant.
- An extension moves pending fix-PR lift requests to the new quarantine row.
  On the old row the lift found the quarantine ended and resolved as superseded.
- Only renders against the story's current baseline count. Approving a stale
  picture changes the baseline, so the older changed renders no longer extend
  the quarantine and ping its owners.
- The per-run cap counts handled entries, so preview mode does not report the
  same deduped entries every run while later ones lapse unseen.
- The lift and the extension get separate rate-limit handling, so a rate limit
  in the lift does not skip extensions before an expiry.

* fix(devex): keep lift requests moved by an extension pending across a race

Lift reconcile and the extension run as separate tasks for the same
default-branch run. A reconcile that read a request before the extension
moved it locked the old, ended quarantine and resolved the moved request
as superseded, so the fix PR could no longer lift the story. The request
updates now also match the quarantine they decided on; a moved request
stays pending for the next run.

The extension also locks the run before the quarantine, the same order as
quarantine_identifier, so it cannot deadlock with a manual quarantine.

* fix(devex): verify the default branch before extending visual review quarantines

- The run's branch and commit are client-supplied. Auto-lift and automatic
  quarantine both check the commit against the default branch head on
  GitHub; the extension now does the same, so an off-branch upload that
  names the default branch cannot keep quarantines alive. The lookup runs
  only when a quarantine is due.
- The run lock in the extension is no-key. FOR UPDATE conflicted with the
  KEY SHARE lock a lift request takes when it records the run, which could
  deadlock against a lift that holds the quarantine row.

feat(knowledge-writer): label each llm call with its stage (#142177)

The facts, judge and grounding calls all reached the AI gateway with the
same labels, so their cost and latency could not be told apart, and
grounding traces counted as merge checks in per-merge cost.

parse_structured_output now takes a required stage and sends it as the
ai_stage label, the key the shared gateway builder and other products
already use. The Go gateway reads labels from one X-PostHog-Properties
JSON header, so the call merges ai_stage into the client's existing
labels instead of replacing them, keeping ai_product and commit_sha.

One test drives a real Anthropic client over an httpx mock transport and
checks the sent labels; it fails when the merge drops the client labels.

The review also noted that this decodes X-PostHog-Properties itself, as
products/signals/backend/llm_spend.py does; a shared label-merge helper in
posthog/llm/gateway_client.py would own that format, outside this change.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(aio): cap the events query-llm-trace reads on large traces (#141969)

* fix(aio): cap the events query-llm-trace reads on large traces

TraceQueryRunner collected every event of a trace, with all prompts and
outputs, into one array. On traces with hundreds of thousands of events
the request timed out, even with detail=summary, because summary is
applied in the MCP layer after the backend returns.

TraceQuery gets an optional eventsLimit. When set, ClickHouse keeps only
the earliest events by timestamp while the cost, token and latency
totals still read every row, and hasMore says the trace had more. The
MCP tool sends 1,000 and tells the agent to use SQL for later events.
Callers that leave it unset, including the trace view, get today's
query.

  uuid) and the events table, which the runner falls back to when
  ai_events has no rows for the trace.
- The note and the eventsLimit description say the totals cover every
  matching event, since property filters narrow them.
- eventsLimit is capped at 10000 so a large value cannot reach

- query-llm-trace retries once without eventsLimit when an older backend
  rejects the field.
- The query-llm-trace prompt and the exploring-llm-traces skill document
  the 1,000-event cap and the _eventsLimit marker.

hits.message:
feat: llm override on gateway (#62567)

## Problem

Models not yet present in LiteLLM's upstream cost map are invisible to the gateway even when they are allowlisted in products config. The gateway derives both `/v1/models` responses and billing costs from that map, so a missing entry means the model cannot be routed or priced correctly. `claude-fable-5` is one such model that needs to be available before LiteLLM ships it upstream.

## Changes

Introduces a `model_cost_overrides.py` module containing a `MODEL_COST_OVERRIDES` dictionary of bridge entries for models absent from LiteLLM's upstream cost map. `apply_model_cost_overrides` merges these entries into the live cost map only when the model is not already defined upstream (upstream always wins). This function is called in both `cost_refresh.py` and `model_cost_service.py` immediately after fetching the upstream map, so overrides are applied on every refresh cycle.

`claude-fable-5` is the first entry, with pricing verified against OpenRouter (Anthropic + Bedrock), a 200k context window (the 1M window is a beta-header feature), and prompt caching support. The `ModelCost` TypedDict is extended with `cache_read_input_token_cost`, `cache_creation_input_token_cost`, and `supports_prompt_caching` fields to accommodate these entries.

Each override entry should be deleted once LiteLLM ships the corresponding upstream definition.

## How did you test this code?

New unit tests in `tests/test_model_cost_overrides.py` cover:

- `apply_model_cost_overrides` adds missing models and does not overwrite existing upstream entries.
- The inserted entry is a shallow copy so mutations by LiteLLM internals do not corrupt the shared constant.
- After a mocked `_refresh_cache`, `ModelCostService.get_costs` and `get_all_models` both surface `claude-fable-5`.
- `get_available_models("posthog_code")` includes `claude-fable-5` when the Anthropic key is set and the model is absent from the upstream map.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

The intent was to make `claude-fable-5` routable and priceable in the gateway before LiteLLM ships it upstream. A dedicated overrides module was chosen over inline patching so the bridge entries are self-documenting and easy to prune. The `apply_model_cost_overrides` call was placed after `get_model_cost_map` in both refresh paths to ensure overrides survive every TTL-driven refresh. Pricing figures and token limits were taken from OpenRouter's published Anthropic/Bedrock rates and matched against the existing `claude-opus-4` pattern for the 1M-window caveat.

fix(agent): default PostHog Code gateway URLs to the Go ai-gateway (#141158)

* fix(agent): default PostHog Code gateway URLs to the Go ai-gateway

The region-derived gateway base (getCloudTaskGatewayUrl, getLlmGatewayUrl)
still pointed at the legacy Python gateway (gateway.{us,eu}.posthog.com,
localhost:3308), so any caller without an explicit URL sent PostHog Code
traffic there. It now resolves to ai-gateway.{us,eu}.posthog.com,
ai-gateway.dev.posthog.dev or localhost:8080, with no product slug, because
Go routes by credential and header rather than path.

The sandbox only reaches the Python gateway through an explicit
LLM_GATEWAY_URL. An unrouted product with no such URL now fails at
configure time instead of silently falling back to a hardcoded legacy host.
Every sandbox product is routed to Go in prod, so this only affects
misconfigured or local setups.

The LLM helper host no longer exposes messagesUrl. Helper prompts have been
Go-only since the gateway token service landed, so the field was dead
wiring that still built a legacy URL.

* fix(agent): send Go-format headers when the SDK agent calls the AI gateway directly

Without a gatewayUrl override, the in-process Agent now talks to the Go
ai-gateway, which reads one X-PostHog-Properties blob and needs ai_product
and team_id in it. The per-property legacy headers would have reached Go
unattributed, so a direct run now sends the blob, the session header and
isAiGateway. The desktop app always passes its loopback proxy, which keeps
the legacy format and converts it, so its requests are unchanged.

Also: a configureEnvironment test pins the refusal when an unrouted product
has no LLM_GATEWAY_URL, the token-missing warning names the variable it
falls back to, only a custom-cloud gateway URL is trimmed, and the web
container comment says what goEnabled: false means for helper prompts.

* fix(desktop): drop the legacy usage fallback and legacy gateway names

The usage fallback to the legacy gateway's /v1/usage/posthog_code now has
no host to fall back to, since the derived gateway base is the Go
ai-gateway, whose /v1/usage/{request_id} is a different endpoint. Usage is
read only from Django's desktop/usage endpoint, and with no project selected
there is no request. This is the change that already landed on master in
#132774, applied here so this branch carries it too.

getLlmGatewayUrl becomes getAiGatewayUrl, because it returns the Go base,
and the desktop containers and workspace-server tests drop imports and
mocks of it that nothing uses. The harness dev region points at the local
Go gateway on localhost:8080 instead of the Python one on 3308.

* fix(agent): send only AI-gateway credentials and full attribution on direct runs

The in-process Agent's direct route to the Go ai-gateway sent whatever key
getApiKey returned. Go accepts only pha_ OAuth tokens, phs_ project secret
keys and phe_ scoped tokens, so the documented personal-key setup failed
authentication on both adapters. It now refuses any other credential before
choosing the gateway, with an error that names the accepted kinds and the
gatewayUrl/gatewayApiKey override. A personal key has no Go counterpart:
Django mints gateway tokens only for OAuth sessions. The README example now
uses an OAuth access token.

Direct runs also lost attribution Go only reads from dedicated headers: the
Claude route now sends X-PostHog-Session-Id, and both routes send the
person's distinct id as X-PostHog-Distinct-Id, without which Go files the
generation under the team instead of the person.

The usage monitor now resets its failure backoff when the selected project
changes within an org. A refresh requested inside an open backoff window
returned without retrying, so usage stayed stale until other activity or the
30-minute backstop.

* fix(agent): keep personal-subscription runs off gateway resolution

A cloud run on the user's own Claude or ChatGPT plan gets no gateway env
from the worker: no AI_GATEWAY_URL, token or LLM_GATEWAY_URL. The agent
server still built the gateway env at startup, and an unrouted product with
no LLM_GATEWAY_URL now fails closed, so every such run crashed before it
asked for the subscription credential. The server now skips the gateway env
when the run's adapter is on a subscription, still exports the server-level
PostHog env, and lists Claude subscription models from Django's tasks/models

fix(llm-gateway): free-cap posthog_code users with no seat (#70810)

## Problem

A posthog_code user with no seat skips the $75 free-plan cap and falls through to the default user cost limits ($500/day burst, $3k/30d sustained). That carve-out was deliberate when it shipped in #54983: alpha users had no seats yet, and free limits were meant to kick in "automatically when beta launches and seats are created". The alpha is long over, and every real user has had a seat since then, so the carve-out has been dormant.

#70790 wakes it up: with seat creation retired, every new signup lands seatless and inherits roughly 40x the free monthly allowance, at pure inference cost, until the usage-based cutover.

## Changes

- `PlanInfo` gains `seat_missing`, set only when the seats endpoint definitively returns 404 (the user has no seat). It rides the existing Redis plan cache and threads into `ThrottleContext`.
- The free-plan cap now applies when a seat exists **or** the seat is confirmed missing.
- Both the enforcement path (`dependencies.py`) and `/v1/usage` reporting carry the flag, so displayed limits match enforced limits.
- **Review follow-up:** the Django best-seat endpoint's multi-org fan-out used to return 404 when billing lookups *failed*, not just when they conclusively found no seat, which would have poisoned the `seat_missing` cache during a billing blip and free-capped paying users. `fetch_seat` is now transport-only (it returns each org's forwarded billing response), the caller classifies outcomes in one place, and the endpoint returns 503 when nothing was found but any lookup failed. 404 is reserved for "every org checked, no seat anywhere". The gateway needs no change for this, since non-404 errors already fail open and uncached. Found-seat-with-partial-failure still returns the best available seat, as before.

> [!NOTE]
> Plan-resolution **failures** are unchanged: `seat_missing` stays false and unresolved users keep default limits. This preserves the shipped fail-loose behavior deliberately, so a billing-service outage degrades to looser limits instead of hard-blocking paying users at $75 mid-session. The loose path stays bounded by the product-wide cost cap and the 15-minute plan cache.

Cache entries written before the field existed read as `seat_missing=false` and turn over within the cache TTL.

Should deploy BEFORE #70790.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only, full gateway suite green (1200 passed). New coverage and the regression each piece catches:

- Parameterized pair in `test_cost_throttles.py`: confirmed-404 context blocked at the free cap, failure-shaped context allowed at default limits. Catches both a revert of the fix and an accidental flip to fail-tight.
- Cache round-trip test in `test_plan_resolver.py`: the flag survives write then read. Catches caching it on one side only, which would flip-flop a user's limits between cache hit and miss.
- One-line `seat_missing` assertions folded into the existing 404, error, no-url, and legacy-cache-entry tests.
- `test_seat_api.py` best-seat cases: all-lookups-fail flips from asserting 404 to asserting 503 (the bug the review caught), plus partial-failure-with-no-seat returns 503 and all-conclusive-404s still return 404 (the contract `seat_missing` depends on).

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

Internal rate-limiting behavior, no public docs affected.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Written by Claude in a PostHog Code session, directed by @adboio, as part of the Code usage-based billing transition. We traced the seatless fallback to #54983's PR description before changing it, confirming the loose limits were an alpha-era bridge rather than an outage-protection design, then made fail-loose-on-failure an explicit decision rather than a side effect. The `/writing-tests` skill gated the new tests. Pre-existing mock assignments in `test_plan_resolver.py` needed `ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]` suppressions (the file predates ty in lint-staged); restructuring the file's mocking pattern was rejected as churn.

feat(posthog-code): bill LLM costs as pass-through credits (no markup) (#69062)

## Problem

PostHog Code is moving to usage-based pricing (see the pricing v2 RFC). The billing infrastructure needed to meter Code's LLM usage at cost (1.0x, pass-through) doesn't exist yet – Code generations aren't tagged billable, and everything billable today assumes the PostHog AI 20% markup.

## Changes

- Gateway: `ProductConfig.billable` becomes `credit_bucket`. `posthog_code` bills into its own `posthog_code_credits` bucket, so `$ai_billable=true` gets stamped on Code generations without tying them to the AI credits throttle.
- Django: the usage report query takes a per-product markup (0% for Code, 20% default). Max `/usage` filters to `POSTHOG_AI_PRODUCTS` so Code costs stay out of the AI credits display.
- Trace panel: markup computed per `ai_product`, mirroring the billing whitelists.

This starts metering, not charging. Billing-service wiring, a `posthog_code_credits` quota resource, grandfathering, and user comms all land separately before anything is charged. `background_agents` and `conversations` stay unbilled on purpose (see comments in `products/config.py`).

feat(llm-gateway): add billing-denial error codes and legacy-client shim (#71343)

## Problem

PostHog Code's usage-based billing cutover (#70951) gates unbilled orgs to the free-tier model list, but the gate's 403 goes out as a bare FastAPI `detail` string. Pre-cutover desktop builds classify errors by substring: they treat that 403 as a fatal session error and tear a healthy session down ("Connection lost" + recovery loops), and no client can tell which limit tripped a 429 without parsing prose.

**Why:** installed desktop builds can't be updated in time for the cutover — the gateway's error bodies are the only lever that reaches them, and this can deploy ahead of the model-gate flip.

## Changes

- The free-tier model-gate 403 now uses the standard error envelope with a machine-readable `code: "model_gate"`, and its message carries a `(rate_limit)` suffix — a compat shim that routes pre-cutover PostHog Code clients to their usage-limit modal instead of session teardown (documented inline; remove once those builds roll forward).
- Throttle 429s repeat the reason in `error.message` (SDK error strings often surface only the message) and carry the throttle scope as `error.code` (`billable_credits`, `user_cost_burst`, `user_cost_sustained`, …), so clients can classify the limit cause.

Companion client work: [PostHog/code#3485](https://github.com/PostHog/code/pull/3485) classifies these bodies into cause-aware billing UX.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only: the enforcement-path gate tests now pin the new envelope (`code`, the `(rate_limit)` suffix), the rate-limiting endpoint test pins the message/reason/code shape, and a TestClient-level test pins the gate 403's wire body end-to-end (top-level error envelope with `code: "model_gate"` and the `(rate_limit)` suffix — never `{"detail": ...}` nesting) through the raise site and the exception-handler unwrap together. All would fail if the shim or codes were dropped. Full llm-gateway suite green locally (1239 passed, 50 skipped, 30 xfailed, 22 xpassed).

None — internal error-body shape.

hits.message:
fix(data-modeling): start view enrichment only for views it can enrich (#138273)

After a materialization succeeds, the succeed activity decides whether
the workflow starts the semantic enrichment child workflow. It compared
the enrichment hash and checked the AI approval, and nothing else.

The enrichment activity then skips a managed viewset view, a test view
and a view with no stored columns. A skip stores no hash, so the next
run of the same view starts the child workflow again. One day of
production logs showed that nearly every child workflow ended in one of
these skips, and that no LLM pass failed.

The succeed activity now calls view_ready_for_enrichment, the check the
save path already uses, so it reports enrichment_needed only for a view
the enrichment activity processes. The decision stays in the activity
result, so the workflow emits the same commands and needs no patch.

The fixture view in the succeed activity tests has no columns. The tests
that expect enrichment, and the test for an unchanged hash, now store
columns so they still exercise the hash comparison.

fix(replay-vision): gate runs on delivery_config, not the vestigial hog_flow_id (#66892)

## Problem

Every scheduled group-summary vision action was silently skipping — runs landed with `{"skip_reason": "no_delivery_flow"}` and **nothing ever delivered to Slack**. Found while testing a real action in prod.

Root cause: the delivery rework swapped the per-action **HogFlow** for **`internal_destination` HogFunctions** provisioned from `delivery_config` (`api/delivery.py`), which leaves `VisionAction.hog_flow_id` permanently null. But the engine's validate gate still checked it:

```python
if action.hog_flow_id is None:
    return "no_delivery_flow"
```

Since nothing populates `hog_flow_id` anymore, that gate fired for **100% of actions**, before any synthesis or delivery. The rework updated `_emit` and `delivery.py` but missed this `_validate` gate.

## Changes

- Gate on **`delivery_config`** (the field that actually drives provisioning) instead of the dead `hog_flow_id`. Empty config → nothing to deliver to → skip before spending an LLM call; non-empty → proceed. `perform_create` provisions the destination atomically with the action, so a non-empty config faithfully means a destination exists — this restores the gate's original pre-rework intent.
- Rename the skip reason `no_delivery_flow` → `no_delivery` (there are no flows anymore).

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (PostHog Code); automated tests only:

- Added `test_validate_passes_when_delivery_configured` — asserts `_validate` returns `None` when `delivery_config` is set. This is the regression that was missing: against the old `hog_flow_id` check it would have failed (always skipped), which is exactly the prod bug.
- Updated the existing `test_validate_reasons` parametrization (`no_delivery_flow` → `no_delivery`, set up via an action with empty `delivery_config`) and the workflow-level skip test's mocked reason.
- Full `test_vision_action_engine.py` suite passes (19), `ruff` clean.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Built with PostHog Code (Claude). Diagnosed from a real prod run that skipped with `no_delivery_flow`; traced it to the stale `hog_flow_id` gate left by the HogFlow → internal_destination delivery rework. Chose to gate on `delivery_config` (decoupled, trivially testable, faithful given atomic provisioning) rather than re-querying the provisioned HogFunction from the temporal activity, which would couple the engine to the CDP/api layer. Invoked `/improving-drf-endpoints` earlier in the session for adjacent serializer work; this change is engine-only.

Standalone fix off master (the engine PR already merged), independent of the open run-history stack.

chore(llm): fail loudly instead of falling back to the Python gateway (#141186)

* chore(llm): fail loudly instead of falling back to the Python gateway

The build_* helpers in posthog/llm/gateway_client.py fell back to the
legacy Python llm-gateway whenever the Go ai-gateway pair was unset or
malformed. That fallback is the last source of the small workflows and
slack_app trickle on the legacy gateway, and it hides a missing Go
config instead of surfacing it.

They now raise GatewayNotConfiguredError, as the task sandboxes already
do. Warehouse semantic enrichment loses its Chat Completions leg for the
same reason, and openai_gateway_configured() accepts only the Go config.

get_llm_client stays, cut down to the one argument its last caller uses:
the tasks model catalogue still reads the legacy /models list directly.

* refactor(llm): drop the dead product route from the gateway builders

`product` only chose the Python gateway route, which the previous commit
removed, so every caller passed a value nothing read. Dropping it also
leaves build_anthropic_client and build_ai_gateway_anthropic_client as
the same function, so they merge into build_anthropic_client with its
privacy_mode flag.

* chore(tasks): stop listing the legacy gateway hosts as sandbox infrastructure

gateway.us/eu.posthog.com served the Python llm-gateway, which sandboxes
no longer need now that runs without a Go gateway token fail. They drop
out of the static egress list and the startup probe hosts; the
ai-gateway hosts stay. `*.posthog.com` still admits them, so egress does
not change, but the probe stops checking a host nothing should call.

* fix(llm): name the gateway misconfiguration and drop dead fallback paths

A malformed AI gateway config (a URL without /v1, or only one of the
pair set) raised the same "must be configured" message as an unset one,
which hid the actual fix from whoever reads the error. The builders now
raise the specific reason from _gateway_misconfig when either setting is
present.

With the Python gateway fallback gone, the signals emission pipeline's
gateway_mode flag was always true, so the per-header
x-posthog-property-* branch could never run. Remove the flag and that
branch, and drop review_hog's per-call ai_stage header, which the Go
gateway ignores (the builder already carries ai_stage). Also remove
comments that described the removed fallback.

* fix(llm): default local dev to the sibling go gateway

In DEBUG (outside tests) AI_GATEWAY_URL and AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY default to the local Go gateway and the key bin/setup-gateway-e2e registers, and the unset-config error names the ai_gateway capability and setup script.

ci: extract llm-gateway to its own workflow with required roll-up (#55387)

## Problem

We mark roll-up CI jobs as GitHub required status checks so branch protection doesn't need reconfiguring every time we rename, split, or add a CI job. The `llm-gateway` job isn't covered by any roll-up today, so we can't make it required without coupling branch protection to a specific job name.

On inspection, the `llm-gateway` job has **no runtime coupling** to Backend CI — its only steps are checkout, Python 3.12, uv, `uv sync` in `services/llm-gateway/`, pytest, upload junit. It lives in `ci-backend.yml` purely because that workflow's `changes` path-filter already had an `llm_gateway` output when the job was first added.

## Changes

- New workflow `.github/workflows/ci-llm-gateway.yml` (`LLM Services CI`) owning its own path filter, the migrated `llm-gateway` job, and an `llm_services_tests` roll-up named `LLM Services Tests Pass`. Future LLM service test jobs can be added to its `needs` without touching branch protection.
- Removed from `.github/workflows/ci-backend.yml`: the `llm_gateway` output, the `llm_gateway` path-filter entry, and the `llm-gateway` job block.
- Registered `LLM Services CI` in `.github/workflows/ci-master-status.yml` (`workflow_run.workflows` and `REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS`) so master-is-red detection picks it up.
- Extended the informational `./bin/ty.py check` in `.github/workflows/ci-python.yml` to include `services/llm-gateway`. Ruff and mypy already cover the service from repo-root invocations.

Follow-up (not in this PR): add `LLM Services Tests Pass` as a required status check on `master` in the GitHub branch-protection UI, and remove any stale entry for the old `LLM Gateway Tests` job name.

## How did you test this code?

Agent-authored — no manual test run. Verified:

- All four touched workflow files parse as valid YAML.
- No remaining references to `llm-gateway` / `llm_gateway` in `ci-backend.yml`.
- Roll-up shape matches existing conventions (`django_tests`, `python_tests`, `mcp_tests`): `if: always()`, tolerates `skipped`, fails on explicit job `failure`.

Recommended reviewer checks:

- PR with no `services/llm-gateway/**` changes: `llm-gateway` skips, `llm_services_tests` reports green.
- PR that touches `services/llm-gateway/**`: `llm-gateway` runs; break a test on a branch to confirm the roll-up goes red.

## Publish to changelog?

no

## Docs update

None needed — internal CI plumbing.

## 🤖 LLM context

Agent-authored session. Plan file: `we-have-some-roll-compiled-peacock.md`. Session traced via Task-Id in the commit trailer.

feat(subscriptions): scheduled AI delivery via Temporal (email + Slack) (#59631)

## Problem

AI-prompt subscriptions need a dedicated delivery pipeline that runs an LLM report generation step before sending, rather than the insight/dashboard export pipeline used by standard subscriptions. The scheduler, value-change handler, and test-delivery API all need to route AI-prompt subscriptions to this new path.

Additionally, disabled-subscription notification emails previously included only a generic "fix the issue and re-enable" message. AI subscriptions need actionable, reason-specific remediation instructions so creators know exactly what to do to restore delivery.

## Changes

**New `ProcessAISubscriptionWorkflow`**

A dedicated Temporal workflow for AI-prompt subscriptions with a two-phase structure:
1. **Generate** (`generate_ai_subscription_report`): runs the LLM pipeline (planner → HogQL → synthesis), gates on org AI-data-processing consent, and persists the markdown onto the `SubscriptionDelivery` row. The report travels through Postgres rather than on the wire to avoid Temporal's ~2 MiB payload cap.
2. **Deliver** (`deliver_subscription`): reads the persisted report back from the delivery row and ships it to email or Slack. No LLM work happens here.

Terminal pre-delivery failures (consent revoked, prompt rejected) auto-disable the subscription and record `FAILED` without counting as a platform SLO failure.

**Scheduler and API routing**

- `fetch_due_subscriptions_activity` now includes `content_type` on each `SubscriptionInfo`, derived from the subscription's `insight_id`, `dashboard_id`, or `prompt` fields.
- `ScheduleAllSubscriptionsWorkflow` fans AI-prompt subs to `ProcessAISubscriptionWorkflow` and everything else to `ProcessSubscriptionWorkflow`, using distinct child-workflow ID prefixes to preserve the duplicate-start guard.
- `HandleSubscriptionValueChangeWorkflow` applies the same routing for target-change and test-delivery triggers.
- The subscription API (`create`, `update`, `test_delivery`) now passes `content_type=instance.resource_type` when starting the value-change workflow.

**Actionable disable-notification emails**

`send_notifications_for_disabled_subscription` now accepts a `DisableReason` object instead of a plain string, and passes both `reason.description` and a formatted `action_message` to the email template. The template renders the `action_message` when present, falling back to the previous generic copy. Two new disable reasons are added: `AI_PROMPT_INVALID_DISABLE_REASON` and `AI_CONSENT_REVOKED_DISABLE_REASON`.

**Shared retry policies**

Retry policy constants (`_RECORD_LIFECYCLE_RETRY`, `_VALIDATE_RETRY`, `_DELIVER_RETRY`) are hoisted to module level so `ProcessSubscriptionWorkflow` and `ProcessAISubscriptionWorkflow` can't drift on retry behavior.

## How did you test this code?

New and updated automated tests cover:

- `generate_ai_subscription_report`: consent-revoked abort, prompt-rejected abort, successful report persistence, and idempotency on Temporal redispatch (no LLM re-bill when the report is already persisted).
- `deliver_subscription` AI path: email delivery with the persisted report, Slack auto-disable on missing integration, non-retryable failure on missing report, and non-retryable failure when `delivery_id` is absent.
- `fetch_due_subscriptions_activity`: AI subscriptions are returned with `content_type == AI_PROMPT`.
- End-to-end `ScheduleAllSubscriptionsWorkflow` test: a due AI subscription is routed through `ProcessAISubscriptionWorkflow`, the LLM runs once, the report is shipped, and the delivery record lands `COMPLETED`.
- `send_notifications_for_disabled_subscription`: the email template context includes both `reason` and a formatted `action_message`.

## Publish to changelog?

No

feat(alerts): add the forecast detector and its scheduled checks (#135974)

* feat(alerts): add the forecast detector and its scheduled checks

Add `forecast` as an insight alert detector type behind the alerts-forecast-detector flag. A scheduled check forecasts the latest point from up to 512 points before it, one gateway call per series, and fires in band, relative or absolute mode on the chosen side. A history shorter than 30 points leaves the check uncomputed. The check keeps expected, lower, upper, actual and mode, with no score, and the breach names the expected value, range and actual value.

The flag gates alert writes through admit_llm_alert_write and each scheduled check. A disabled flag, a gateway 402 or 403, or a gateway that is not configured pauses the check and leaves the alert enabled. Each failure records its own owner-readable error code. An unreadable gateway response is now retried. The real-time cadence is refused, and forecast checks run on the AI worker, which holds the gateway credentials.

The https check that kept the System One key off plain http moves to resolve_https_ai_gateway_config in the shared gateway helper, with the same localhost exceptions, and the forecast client uses it before it sends the bearer key.

Refs #135961

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Generated-By: PostHog Desktop
Task-Id: 90d8fad7-544e-4e34-a615-c81fefafc43b

* fix(alerts): check ai processing approval and keep forecast alerts out of the parallel run

The forecast detector sends an insight's series to a model, so its access check now refuses when the organization has not approved AI data processing, as the AI detector does. Writers refuse, and a scheduled check pauses with the alert left on. The forecast client sends the privacy-mode header when the organization's privacy mode is on.

The parallel-run copy guards now skip every detector that calls the AI gateway, so a forecast alert is not checked, and paid for, twice.

Also fixes CI: the facade re-exports forecast_rule for the presentation layer, the quantile levels are a frozen dataclass instead of a tuple, a test reads an optional error safely, and the MCP tool schema snapshots are regenerated.

feat: add session property values support for V3 table (#54267)

## Problem

The session property values API endpoint (`/sessions/values/`) only routes to V1 or V2 session tables. Teams configured for V3 (`raw_sessions_v3`) silently fall through to V2, missing the V3 table's improvements (materialized `session_timestamp` column, bloom filter indexes, reduced column count).

Additionally, the V3 SQL templates for property value lookups had no timestamp filter, so queries scanned the entire team's session history — the same performance issue fixed for V2 in #54239.

## Changes

- Wire V3 into the `SessionViewSet.values()` and `SessionViewSet.property_definitions()` endpoints, routing when `sessionTableVersion == V3`
- Add `session_timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY` to both V3 SQL templates — cleaner than the V2 `bitShiftRight(session_id_v7, 80)` expression since V3 has a materialized `session_timestamp` column that matches the partition key directly

## How did you test this code?

- Existing V3 session tests pass (`test_sessions_v3.py` — 21 passed, 1 skipped)
- Session API tests pass (`test_session.py` — 11 passed)
- The timestamp filter uses the materialized `session_timestamp` column which is the partition key (`toYYYYMM(session_timestamp)`), enabling ClickHouse partition pruning

## Publish to changelog?

No

## LLM context

Stacked on #54239 (V2 timestamp filter). Part of a performance investigation into property value lookup latencies using Jaeger trace analysis over 30 days — session URL property lookups (`$entry_current_url`, `$entry_pathname`) were taking 10-70 seconds due to full-table scans with expensive `finalizeAggregation()` calls.

feat(replay-vision): provision a built-in daily digest for new scanners (#69051)

## Problem

Scheduled summaries only exist if a user finds the tab and configures one, so most scanners never show the AI narrative that's the product's payoff. We want every scanner to have a daily digest by default, surfaced on the scanner page (frontend follows in the next PR up the stack).

Standalone on master; #69037 (the scanner-page digest card) stacks on top.

## Changes

- New `is_scanner_digest` flag on `VisionAction` + partial unique constraint (at most one digest per scanner), surfaced in the serializer with a friendly 400 on duplicates.
- Creating a scanner auto-provisions its digest (`Daily digest: {scanner}`, daily 8:00 in the team timezone, no delivery targets), gated on the `replay-vision-actions` flag and fail-soft so digest provisioning can never break scanner creation. The digest carries the creating user as `created_by` (synthesis refuses to run for a null creator). No backfill for existing scanners; the UI offers one-click opt-in instead.
- Delivery becomes optional in the engine: the `no_delivery` validate-skip is removed (the persisted run is now the in-app artifact) and `_emit` no-ops when there are no destinations. Cost stays bounded: synthesis already skips empty windows and over-budget teams without an LLM call.
- Regenerated OpenAPI types.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_api.py`: digest provisioned on scanner create with the right defaults; not provisioned when the actions flag is off (would silently bill non-flagged teams); scanner creation survives a digest provisioning failure (fail-soft regression).
- `test_vision_actions_api.py`: second digest for a scanner is a 400, not a DB 500.
- `test_vision_action_engine.py`: validate passes with and without delivery (the old gate skipped every deliveryless action); emit no-ops without destinations.
- Migration checked with `sqlmigrate` and the risk analyzer (constraint warning acknowledged: tiny internal-flag table, matches existing product precedent for partial unique constraints).

feat(subscriptions): AI report pipeline primitive (planner, HogQL, synthesis) + sanitization (#59630)

## Problem

AI subscriptions need a backend that turns a user's natural-language prompt into a delivered analytics report. This PR adds the **report pipeline primitive** — the planner → execute → synthesize core — plus the prompt-injection sanitization it depends on. It's the foundation the scheduled Temporal delivery (#59631) and the API/UI (#59632) build on.

## Changes

- **Pipeline** (`posthog/temporal/subscriptions/ai_subscription/`): `generate_ai_report` runs three stages — an LLM **planner** emits 1–3 HogQL queries, **execute** runs them concurrently with a bounded per-step LLM fix-retry and degrades a failed step to a placeholder, and an LLM **synthesize** writes the markdown. The pipeline owns no side effects (persistence/delivery are the caller's job) and takes a plain `window_days: int` so it stays decoupled from the subscription domain.
- **Prompt-injection sanitization** (`posthog/text_sanitization.py`): single canonical module that strips LLM framing markers and invisible-Unicode smuggling vectors from all user-controlled text (event names, prompt, query results) before it enters a prompt. Consolidated from the former temporal `prompt_sanitization.py`.
- **Prompts via the LLMPrompt product**: planner/synthesis/fix prompts resolve through `resolve_prompt(team, name, default)` — a team can override by name in the Prompt product; the code constant is the default (LLMPrompt is team-scoped with no global tier).
- **Models**: `gpt-5-mini` for both stages.
- **Subscription model**: `content_type` column replaced by a derived `resource_type` property; `ai_report_window_days` derived from cadence; migration `1177` only adds the `prompt` field.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent. Automated tests only (no manual testing):
- Unit/behaviour tests for each stage, the retry/degrade paths, sanitization, and the model helpers.
- `test_report_pipeline_integration.py` — mocks only the two LLM boundaries and runs the planned HogQL **against the test ClickHouse for real**, asserting results flow into synthesis and that an invalid query degrades to a placeholder while the report still ships.
- Full `ai_subscription` suite: 38 passing.

## Follow-ups (tracked for when this ships)

- **Observability — create an LLM eval (UI):** the pipeline tags its generations with `feature = "ai_subscription"` and `stage = "synthesis"`/`"plan"`. Once the feature emits generations, create an **`llm_judge`** evaluation in LLM analytics conditioned on `feature = "ai_subscription"`, `stage = "synthesis"`, judging report quality/usefulness (boolean, allow N/A). There's no MCP tool to create evals, so this is a UI step. `_capture_report_quality` emits a lightweight coverage signal in the meantime.
- **SLO:** add the new SLO type over the pipeline's success/latency once available.
- Converge `_resolve_slack_integration` with the similar helper in #59912 once it lands.

## Publish to changelog?

no

## 🤖 Agent context

Agent-assisted (Claude Code). Built the pipeline, sanitization, and tests; iterated across two review rounds. Decisions of note: kept the pipeline LLM-agnostic and side-effect-free; chose a derived `resource_type` over a stored column (can't drift); resolved prompts via LLMPrompt with a code-default fallback rather than seeding per-team records; moved the package out of the celery `ee/tasks/` folder into `posthog/temporal/subscriptions/` since it runs through Temporal. Requires human review; not self-merged.

feat(replay-vision): vision action synthesis activity (#64176)

## Problem

PR 2 of the Replay Vision "and then…" stack (scheduled Slack digests). With the data model in place (#64168), this adds the piece that actually turns a scanner's observations into a report: the synthesis activity.

## Changes

Adds `synthesize_action_activity` (`products/replay_vision/backend/temporal/vision_actions/`), the Temporal activity that produces one digest for a `VisionAction` and persists it on its `VisionActionRun` — the report never crosses the Temporal wire.

It runs all blocking work (ORM + LLM + Redis budget read) in a single sync function behind a thin async delegator, and:

- **Gates** on AI data-processing consent (`organization.is_ai_data_processing_approved`) and the team's AI credit budget (`is_team_over_ai_credit_budget`), mirroring the AI-subscription path.
- **Short-circuits** on an empty selection window (no noise digests) or a missing creator (can't attribute the LLM call).
- **Fetches** summarizer observations per the action's `selection` (modeled on `max_tools._fetch_and_format`), keeping the prompt-injection defang (`_as_untrusted_data` / `_neutralize_markup`).
- **Synthesizes** via `MaxChatOpenAI` (billable), **strips external links** from the output (Slack auto-unfurls), and stores both the markdown and a light Slack-mrkdwn rendering.
- **Idempotent**: a retry after the markdown is persisted does not re-bill the LLM.

The external-link defang is ported locally (`markdown_safety.py`) rather than imported from the exports private helper; no cross-product dependency is added.

I'm an agent (PostHog Code). Added and ran `products/replay_vision/backend/tests/test_vision_action_synthesis.py` — **12 tests passing** locally via `hogli test` (LLM and credit-budget calls mocked). Coverage: happy-path persistence + Slack conversion, idempotency (LLM not re-called), consent/credit/empty-window/missing-creator short-circuits, succeeded-only filtering, external-link stripping, window-days filtering, prompt-guide plumbing, and the markdown→Slack transform incl. truncation.

feat(subscriptions): gate AI summaries on AI credit budget (#59625)

## Problem

Subscription AI summaries call an LLM on every delivery with **no budget check**. Now that subscriptions are available on the free tier (#59624), an org could keep generating summaries while over its AI credit budget. We should stop generating once an org is over budget — the same way the chat assistant already behaves.

## Changes

Adopt the chat assistant's enforcement pattern (`ee/api/conversation.py`): `is_team_limited(QuotaResource.AI_CREDITS)`, which reads the billing quota-limiting cache (not the retrospective usage query).

- **Enable-time gate** (`SubscriptionSerializer.validate`): raises `QuotaLimitExceeded` (402) when a summary is being toggled *on* while the org is over budget. Reuses the existing "becoming active" check, so grandfathered summaries and unrelated edits are unaffected.
- **Generation-time gate** (`snapshot_subscription_insights`): when over budget, skips the summary and delivers the rest of the subscription (graceful degradation) rather than failing the delivery. **Fail-open** — if the quota lookup itself errors, the summary is generated rather than silently dropped.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (Claude Code) — automated suites I ran locally:

- `ee/api/test/test_subscription.py` — enable-time gate over/under budget, the patch-transition case, and the grandfathering case (unrelated edits while over budget aren't blocked).
- `posthog/temporal/subscriptions/test_snapshot_ai_consent.py` — generation-time skip when over budget, generate when under, and fail-open when the quota check raises.

## Publish to changelog?

No — internal cost-control guard, no user-facing feature.

We reuse that chokepoint rather than introducing a bespoke check, so this is the second adopter of an established pattern, not new billing infrastructure. Behaviour differs by context deliberately: a hard 402 at enable-time (API), graceful skip-and-deliver at generation-time (background workflow).

fix(replay-vision): bill vision action summaries through posthog ai (#69074)

## Problem

Vision action summary synthesis gates on the team's PostHog AI-credit budget (`is_team_over_ai_credit_budget`) but then calls Gemini directly with our own API key. The generation was instrumented for LLM analytics, but it never carried `$ai_billable`, so token usage never actually drew from the budget we gate on — teams were being quota-checked against a meter their usage never moved.

Standalone on master, independent of the vision-action feature stack.

## Changes

Synthesis now runs through PostHog AI, matching how insight AI summaries are generated in Temporal (`products/exports/backend/temporal/subscriptions/llm_change_summary.py`):

- `posthoganalytics.ai.openai.OpenAI(posthog_client=..., base_url=settings.OPENAI_BASE_URL)` — the LLM gateway in production.
- Model: `gpt-4.1-mini` (same as insight summaries), replacing Gemini 3 Flash.
- The generation event carries `$ai_billable: true`, `team_id`, and project/org groups, so token usage charges the team's AI credits — the same budget the pre-flight gate checks.
- Tagged `ai_product: replay_vision`, `feature: vision_action_group_summary` for LLM analytics attribution.
- System prompt, prompt-guide-leads/untrusted-observations-last ordering, empty-output handling, and the budget gate are unchanged.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_vision_action_synthesis.py` (27 tests, all green): mocks reshaped from the Gemini client to the OpenAI chat-completions client; the existing behavioral assertions (prompt ordering, injection fencing, RBAC exclusion, empty-window skip, budget skip, markdown/Slack output) all still pass against the new call shape. No new tests: the billing tagging is declarative kwargs on the wrapper, and asserting them would be a change-detector test.
- Not manually tested against a live gateway by the agent.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

N/A — internal billing plumbing behind the `replay-vision-actions` flag.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Authored with PostHog Code (Claude), directed by Kim after her TL pointed at the insight-AI-summaries Temporal path as the reference for charging token usage. Skills invoked: /writing-tests. The subscriptions `llm_change_summary.py` client construction and billing property shape were ported as-is; the replay-vision distinct-id convention (`replay_vision_distinct_id`) was kept over the subscriptions-style region user tag for consistency with the product's other generations.

feat(data-catalog): rank metric search hits by meaning behind a flag (#133537)

* feat(data-catalog): rank metric search hits by meaning behind a flag

Word matching cannot find a metric when the agent uses other words, such as
"subscriber income" for MRR. With data-catalog-metric-semantic-search on and
AI data processing approved, search also ranks metrics by cosine similarity
between the query embedding and a vector stored on each metric.

A Celery task embeds the name, display name, description and unit after a
write that changes them, and backfill_metric_embeddings embeds existing
metrics. The two lanes merge by each hit's best rank, so weak word matches
that both lanes find cannot push down the closest semantic hit. A failed or
slow embedding call leaves word matching only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): address review findings on semantic metric search

- Give the embedding model and text hash columns a database default, so
  the previous release can still insert metrics during the rollout.
- Skip a stored vector whose text changed since it was made.
- Store a refreshed vector with one conditional update on the embedded
  fields, so an edit during the embedding call cannot be overwritten.
- Defer the vector column when loading the returned metrics.
- Cap metric-list searches per project, because a search can call the
  embedding worker.
- Register the refresh task in the task snapshot.
- Bound the eval's OpenAI client, and store text hashes on seeded vectors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): throttle metric writes and drop unused facade exports

A metric write that changes its embedded text schedules an embedding call,
so create and update get a per-project throttle pair that also covers
session-authenticated callers. Nothing outside the product used the
embedding exports, and the facade lint rejects one that takes a model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(data-catalog): pass the flag mock to the list filter test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(data-catalog): backfill metric embeddings with a beat task

Metrics written before semantic search have no vector, and the management
command needs someone to run it in every region. A beat task now runs
every 10 minutes, picks up to 100 live metrics with no current vector in
organizations that approved AI data processing, and queues their
refreshes 4 seconds apart, so the embedding worker sees a steady trickle.

The task is temporary: once existing metrics have vectors, writes keep
them current, and the task and its schedule entry can go.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): keep confident word matches first and bound the semantic lane

- A confident word match ranks above every meaning-only hit.
- The semantic lane skips teams with more than 2000 embedded metrics, and
  streams vectors instead of holding them all.
- A text change clears the stored vector, so the backfill sweep finds a
  metric whose refresh failed.
- Metric reads no longer load the vector, except the semantic lane.
- Drop the unused embedding_model parameter and hit fields, and name the
  refresh outcomes.
- Test the flag-on search path, its fallback, and where the throttles apply.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): read vectors in one query and keep them on a same-text write

- The semantic lane clears the embedding deferral from metrics_for_team, so
  it no longer loads each vector with its own query.
- A write that resends the same search text keeps its current vector.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(data-catalog): gate the metric embedding backfill behind its own flag

The beat sweep and the backfill command now embed existing metrics only for
teams with data-catalog-metric-embedding-backfill on. A metric write still
embeds that metric with no flag.

* feat(pulse): route brief synthesis through the Go AI gateway

MaxChatOpenAI only routed calls made inside a PostHog AI runner, so pulse
kept calling OpenAI directly from its Temporal activity. Allow the pulse
product through without a runner config, with the direct twin as fallback.

Unknown privacy mode redacts on the gateway, so the new generation events

path and the usage report does not list it, so nobody is charged either way.

* fix(pulse): fit the gateway attempt and fallback inside the activity timeout

The OpenAI gateway client always used the 150s gateway timeout, ignoring the
caller's. When the gateway stalled, pulse spent 150s there and then up to two
120s direct attempts, 390s against a 300s synthesize activity timeout.

The gateway client now keeps the caller's timeout, as the Anthropic client
already does, and pulse lowers its per-attempt timeout to 90s. A stalled
gateway plus two direct attempts now takes at most 270s.

feat(aio): daily eval report cadence and gpt-6.1-terra report agent (#132837)

* feat(aio): send count-triggered eval reports at most once a day by default

The default count trigger fires every 100 results with a one-hour gap, so a
busy evaluation gets up to ten near-identical reports a day. Raise the
default gap to 24 hours: busy evaluations get one report a day, and quiet
ones still report when they reach 100 results.

- Model default for cooldown_minutes goes from 60 to 1440.
- Migration moves count-triggered reports still on 60 minutes to 1440. An
  explicit one-hour setting looks the same and moves too.
- New evaluations in the UI start on the same count trigger instead of a
  daily schedule, which fires even when nothing ran.
- The create page summary, MCP tool description, and evals skill name the gap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(aio): write eval reports with gpt-6.1-terra on the responses api

Switch the eval report agent from gpt-5.2 to gpt-6.1-terra, which costs
less per token on the flex tier.

- gpt-6.1-terra joins the flex allowlist, checked against OpenAI's flex
  pricing table.
- gpt-6 models reject function tools with reasoning on /v1/chat/completions,
  so the report agent's client sends calls to /v1/responses. The shared
  client builder takes this as an opt-in, so the clustering agents keep
  chat completions.
- Responses API calls set store=False. /v1/responses keeps a response for
  30 days by default, and report prompts carry customer traces.
- Tests cover the no-store setting in both routing modes and the flex to
  standard fallback on the Responses path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(mcp): update unit test snapshots

* fix(aio): carry reasoning across report agent turns and split cooldown migration

- Responses API clients ask for encrypted reasoning and use the
  responses/v1 output format. With store=False, a tool loop's second call
  otherwise sends a reasoning item by an id OpenAI never stored, and fails.
- The create page summary shows the saved cooldown in minutes until
  someone edits the hours, so a 90-minute gap no longer reads as 2 hours.
- The default change and the backfill move to separate migrations, which
  the migration risk check requires.
- The batched count test fixture pins the minimum cooldown, since it
  relied on the old one-hour default.

* chore(subscriptions): add summary styling eval

One-shot eval that scores how AI subscription summaries look once Slack
renders them. It compares the production structured output rendered with
and without the untagged-text normaliser, and a plain Markdown variant,
on invented Hedgebox-style insight states. Stub mode runs without gateway

call, so it needs only OPENAI_API_KEY rather than a local AI gateway.
generate_report_summary and request_summary_completion take an optional

The date scorer also accepts a window whose qualifier sits outside the

On real dashboard deliveries gpt-6-luna paraphrases insight names and

The report synthesis model often returns a Markdown table as one visual

feat(hobby): support BYO AI keys and gate cloud-only replay summaries (#61823)

## Problem

We advertise PostHog's AI surface on self-hosted (hobby) installs, but it's broken-not-hidden:

- **Max** (the main assistant) runs on Anthropic (`claude-sonnet-*`), reading `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment — yet the only AI signal we expose to the frontend is `openai_available`, and the only key any install/upgrade flow prompts for is OpenAI. So on hobby the Max tab renders, the user types a message, and gets a **raw auth error at call time** because no key is configured and nothing told them to set one.
- **Session-replay AI summaries** are Cloud-only on the backend, but the frontend triggers (player dock, per-row playlist icon, notebook person-feed) are visible on self-hosted and surface that restriction as a `lemonToast.error` rather than a proper paywall.

This makes AI on hobby a real bring-your-own-key experience, and replaces the replay error with the standard move-to-cloud upsell.

## Changes

**Make Max work on hobby (BYO key):**

- Backend: add an `anthropic_available` flag to the authenticated preflight (mirrors the existing `openai_available`), since Max needs Anthropic and had no signal at all.
- Frontend: add an `isMaxAvailable` selector to `maxGlobalLogic` (`isCloudOrDev || anthropic_available`) and render a `MaxNotConfigured` empty-state in both Max render paths when it's a self-hosted instance with no key — telling the user to set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and restart, instead of failing silently.
- Install/upgrade DevEx: `bin/deploy-hobby` optionally prompts for Anthropic + OpenAI keys on a fresh install; `bin/upgrade-hobby` offers to append them only when absent (existing keys are never overwritten — the established append-if-missing pattern). The vars are threaded into the `web`, `worker`, and `temporal-django-worker` services in `docker-compose.hobby.yml` via `${VAR:-}` so a blank stays blank.

**Gate replay summaries behind the cloud upsell on hobby:**

- The backend stays the boundary (still Cloud-only). The player dock now shows the standard "move to PostHog Cloud" link instead of the summarize button on self-hosted; the per-row playlist icon and the notebook person-feed summary block are hidden on self-hosted (the dock carries the upsell rather than repeating a paywall per list row).
- Note: a billing-style `PayGateMini` was intentionally **not** used here — this feature isn't billing-gated on Cloud, so the simple `isCloudOrDev` + move-to-cloud link (the same pattern as the Help/Account menus) is the correct gate.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (PostHog Slack app). I did not perform manual UI testing.

- Updated and reviewed `posthog/api/test/test_preflight.py` to assert the new `anthropic_available` field. I could **not** execute the DB-backed test suite in this environment (no local Postgres) — CI should run it; the test change mirrors the existing `openai_available` assertion exactly.
- `bash -n` syntax-checked `bin/deploy-hobby` and `bin/upgrade-hobby`.
- Ran `ruff check`/`ruff format` on the Python changes (clean). The frontend formatter/typecheck could not run here (no `node_modules`); import ordering was set by hand to match oxfmt conventions.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

The self-host environment-variables docs may want an entry for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` enabling AI features — flagging for the docs agent.

## 🤖 Agent context

Authored by the PostHog Slack app agent at a maintainer's request. The ask: propose and implement a solution for setting AI provider keys on hobby installs — DevEx at install/upgrade time plus UI treatment.

Key decisions:
- **Show + prompt, not hide** for Max — keep the surface visible with a clear "set the key" empty-state.
- **Anthropic is the headline gap** — Max can't run without it, and we exposed no signal for it. OpenAI features already had a BYOK path (`openai_available` + existing "set OPENAI_API_KEY" messages), so they're unchanged.
- **Replay summaries stay Cloud-only** per maintainer direction — surfaced as the standard move-to-cloud upsell rather than enabling BYOK for them.
- Rejected `PayGateMini` for the replay gate because it gates by billing plan on Cloud, which would wrongly block Cloud users of a non-billing-gated feature.

chore(llm): fail loudly instead of falling back to the Python gateway (#141186)

* chore(llm): fail loudly instead of falling back to the Python gateway

The build_* helpers in posthog/llm/gateway_client.py fell back to the
legacy Python llm-gateway whenever the Go ai-gateway pair was unset or
malformed. That fallback is the last source of the small workflows and
slack_app trickle on the legacy gateway, and it hides a missing Go
config instead of surfacing it.

They now raise GatewayNotConfiguredError, as the task sandboxes already
do. Warehouse semantic enrichment loses its Chat Completions leg for the
same reason, and openai_gateway_configured() accepts only the Go config.

get_llm_client stays, cut down to the one argument its last caller uses:
the tasks model catalogue still reads the legacy /models list directly.

* refactor(llm): drop the dead product route from the gateway builders

`product` only chose the Python gateway route, which the previous commit
removed, so every caller passed a value nothing read. Dropping it also
leaves build_anthropic_client and build_ai_gateway_anthropic_client as
the same function, so they merge into build_anthropic_client with its
privacy_mode flag.

* chore(tasks): stop listing the legacy gateway hosts as sandbox infrastructure

gateway.us/eu.posthog.com served the Python llm-gateway, which sandboxes
no longer need now that runs without a Go gateway token fail. They drop
out of the static egress list and the startup probe hosts; the
ai-gateway hosts stay. `*.posthog.com` still admits them, so egress does
not change, but the probe stops checking a host nothing should call.

* fix(llm): name the gateway misconfiguration and drop dead fallback paths

A malformed AI gateway config (a URL without /v1, or only one of the
pair set) raised the same "must be configured" message as an unset one,
which hid the actual fix from whoever reads the error. The builders now
raise the specific reason from _gateway_misconfig when either setting is
present.

With the Python gateway fallback gone, the signals emission pipeline's
gateway_mode flag was always true, so the per-header
x-posthog-property-* branch could never run. Remove the flag and that
branch, and drop review_hog's per-call ai_stage header, which the Go
gateway ignores (the builder already carries ai_stage). Also remove

* fix(storybook): disable partial raster in snapshot runs

Chromium re-rasters a partly invalidated tile in place, and the
anti-aliased pixels in that tile (rounded corners, borders) come out a
color level or two off from a full raster. Which tiles get hit depends
on timing, so one story renders slightly different pictures across runs
and visual review flags them as flaky.

the per-browser jest-playwright launchOptions key, so WebKit shards
never see the Chromium-only switch.

SurveyResults gave 3 distinct pictures per theme in 6 runs without the
switch and 1 with it, and settled on the second capture every time.
